reviews.skip_if: Users expecting proof that the workflows improve their model on their codebase: the repository provides eval tooling, but our measured test covered only 1 test case.

reviews.name: ui-ux-pro-max-skill
reviews.verdict: Our UI UX Pro Max CLI install added 32 packages in 31 seconds and built in 13 seconds with 0 audit findings, but it exposed no test target to our harness.
reviews.skip_if: Teams expecting a finished designer-approved interface from one prompt: the skill supplies guidance and the coding agent still produces the implementation.

reviews.name: browser-tools-mcp
reviews.verdict: Our browser-tools-mcp run built in 8 seconds and passed 355 of 356 tests, with the one failure in degraded attachment handling and 0 audit findings.
reviews.skip_if: Playwright-style test authors who need the agent to drive a clean, reproducible browser: the README recommends automation-first MCP servers for that job.

reviews.name: serena
reviews.verdict: Our Serena run built successfully, but the 840-second test step ended with 36 failures and 164 setup or collection errors, including an explicit missing-Ruby error.
reviews.skip_if: Developers who expect a marketplace install to stay current: the README explicitly warns that marketplace commands are outdated and says to use its quick start.

reviews.name: kratos
reviews.verdict: Our Kratos checkout installed in 27 seconds, built in 45, and passed all 44 Go test packages, making it the strongest measured source baseline in this batch.
reviews.skip_if: Developers seeking an AI agent or inference framework: the README describes general microservice transport and middleware, with no model runtime.

reviews.name: haystack
reviews.verdict: Our Haystack run installed 69 packages and built in 45 seconds combined, but the repository test command ended with 112 failures and 88 errors in the base environment.
reviews.skip_if: Developers seeking a tiny wrapper for one model call: Haystack's value comes from pipelines and agents, while its component model adds concepts a small script does not need.

reviews.name: agentscope
reviews.verdict: Our AgentScope run passed 1,977 tests after a 269-second install that consumed 1,039 MB, so it is well tested and expensive to install.
reviews.skip_if: Developers who need a small dependency footprint: our source install pulled 298 packages and occupied 1,039 MB before any external model assets.

reviews.name: chrome-devtools-mcp
reviews.verdict: Our Chrome DevTools MCP build finished in 43 seconds, but its test suite failed after 108 seconds in a Puppeteer browser-connection path even though npm audit found 0 vulnerabilities.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone planning to expose a personal browser session: the README says MCP clients can inspect, debug, and modify any data in the connected browser.

reviews.name: JavaGuide
reviews.verdict: JavaGuide is an excellent free map for Chinese-reading Java developers who need to find gaps before an interview.
reviews.skip_if: English-only readers expecting a fully translated course: the English README translates the index, while linked core lessons such as the Java basics article are still Chinese.

reviews.name: litellm
reviews.verdict: LiteLLM is the practical default when a team needs one API in front of several model vendors.
reviews.skip_if: Small applications committed to one provider with no routing or governance needs: LiteLLM adds another dependency or network hop.

reviews.name: codex
reviews.verdict: Our Codex checkout installed 1 pnpm package in 21 seconds but exposed no build or test target, so that run validates only a thin Node workspace path and not the 1.5-million-line Rust project.
reviews.skip_if: Developers seeking a fully offline coding assistant: the README requires ChatGPT sign-in or separate API-key setup for model access.

reviews.name: browser-harness
reviews.verdict: Our Browser Harness install, build, and all 140 tests passed in 61 seconds combined, with 0 known package vulnerabilities.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone unwilling to expose a logged-in browser session to agent actions: the harness can reach the same pages and accounts that Chrome can.

reviews.name: actionlint
reviews.verdict: Our actionlint build took 17 seconds, but its 5-group test run ended 4 passed and 1 failed in the popular-actions generator.
reviews.skip_if: Authors seeking to lint `action.yml` metadata for custom or composite actions: issue 46 has requested that separate file type since 2021.

reviews.name: hatchet
reviews.verdict: Our Hatchet build succeeded in 224 seconds, but 3 of 43 Go package results failed, so teams should trial their exact SDK and failure cases before committing.
reviews.skip_if: Developers who cannot use Docker locally: the README's quickest local server path requires Docker on macOS, Linux, or WSL.

reviews.name: flux2
reviews.verdict: Our Flux build finished in 9 seconds, but the test command ended with 8 passes and 1 unexplained failure, so this checkout did not earn a clean lab result.
reviews.skip_if: Teams without Kubernetes operations experience: Flux adds controllers, custom resources, service accounts, source credentials, reconciliation rules, and upgrade work to every managed cluster.

reviews.name: motrix-next
reviews.verdict: Our Motrix Next checkout installed in 27 seconds, built in 43 seconds, and passed its tests in 34 seconds, making it a credible modern replacement for the older Motrix codebase.
reviews.skip_if: Windows or macOS users who require a trusted publisher signature: the README says neither platform's binaries are code-signed and documents security warnings.

reviews.name: keda
reviews.verdict: Our KEDA build took 273 seconds, and the test command finished with 20 of 23 packages passing, so the code built but the pinned checkout did not clear its plain sandbox suite.
reviews.skip_if: Teams without Kubernetes: KEDA is an operator, metrics server, admission webhook, and set of custom resources for a cluster.

reviews.name: karpenter-provider-aws
reviews.verdict: Our Karpenter build passed in 180 seconds, but tests ended with 19 of 21 packages failing, so source contributors need the project's intended test environment before treating a generic Go run as healthy.
reviews.skip_if: Kubernetes teams outside AWS: this repository implements the AWS provider, while other clouds use separate Karpenter providers or managed services.

reviews.name: agent-browser
reviews.verdict: Our source install consumed 1,091 packages and 894 MB, while the workspace offered no build or test target, so agent-browser's excellent command design was not independently exercised in our sandbox.
reviews.skip_if: Conventional end-to-end test suites that need code-level fixtures and assertions: Playwright is a clearer primary test framework.

reviews.name: gh-aw
reviews.verdict: Our gh-aw run installed 241 packages and built successfully, but 1 of 3 tested packages failed because the Go container had no `node` executable for fuzz sanitization.
reviews.skip_if: Teams seeking deterministic CI replacement: the README says builds, tests, linting, deployments, and reproducible scripts should remain conventional Actions.

reviews.name: kueue
reviews.verdict: Our Kueue build passed in 263 seconds, but its 614-second test run ended with 4 of 8 packages failing after a performance checker received an empty summary path.
reviews.skip_if: Clusters older than Kubernetes 1.34: the v0.19 README says only 1.34 or newer is supported and tested.

reviews.name: temporal
reviews.verdict: Our Temporal build took 278 seconds, and 13 of 15 test targets passed before two PostgreSQL CLI tests failed, so source contributors should expect a large server with persistence-sensitive tests.
reviews.skip_if: Simple cron jobs or short queues whose failure recovery is already obvious: Temporal adds a server, SDK workers, task queues, histories, and replay rules.

reviews.name: airflow
reviews.verdict: Our Airflow run installed 151 packages and built in 26 seconds, but its test command stopped after 7 seconds on an unrecognized pytest option, so established data teams should expect a capable scheduler with a serious development environment.
reviews.skip_if: Teams processing continuous event streams: the README says Airflow is not a streaming system and recommends handling stream data in batches.

reviews.name: kestra
reviews.verdict: Our Kestra UI build took 45 seconds after a 1,420-package install, but that workspace had no test target and npm audit found 1 moderate vulnerability.
reviews.skip_if: Teams unwilling to give a local development container Docker socket access: the README's quick start mounts `/var/run/docker.sock` and runs as root.

reviews.name: windmill
reviews.verdict: Our Windmill CLI build finished in 22 seconds, but all 111 test files errored when the suite could not find `cargo`, so contributors should budget for the full multi-language toolchain.
reviews.skip_if: Companies embedding Windmill in a paid product without reviewing the license terms: the README says redistribution, managed service use, wrapping, and some customer-facing uses require AGPL compliance or a commercial license.

reviews.name: n8n
reviews.verdict: Our n8n install took 633 seconds, occupied 3,667 MB, and built successfully, but the full test command still exited 1 at the computer-use package.
reviews.skip_if: Buyers who require an OSI-approved open-source license: n8n uses its Sustainable Use License and a separate enterprise license.

reviews.name: vitess
reviews.verdict: Our Vitess checkout built in 252 seconds, but 7 of 43 Go test results failed after a 506-second run, so adoption should begin with failure analysis rather than a clean-build badge.
reviews.skip_if: Applications that fit comfortably on one MySQL primary with replicas: Vitess adds VTGate, VTTablet, topology storage, workflows, and more failure modes to own.

reviews.name: rxdb
reviews.verdict: Our RxDB run installed 1,737 packages and used 1,241 MB, then all 1,447 Mocha tests passed before the overall test command failed on a missing `test:browser` script.
reviews.skip_if: Small browser apps that only need a thin IndexedDB wrapper: RxDB's 1,737-package contributor install and replication machinery add work that Dexie can avoid.

reviews.name: trackerslist
reviews.verdict: Our 3-CPU, 8 GB sandbox could not run commit 31bd8e4 because the repository has no supported language ecosystem or Dockerfile, so Trackerslist is a published data feed rather than executable software.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that need to inspect or self-host the checker: commit 31bd8e4 contains generated lists and no checker source, workflow, package manifest, or Dockerfile.

reviews.name: hiring-without-whiteboards
reviews.verdict: Our run installed 243 packages in 11 seconds and passed the available tests in 6 seconds, so the repository is easy to check locally and useful as a starting list.
reviews.skip_if: Candidates who need a guarantee about their next interview: the README says experiences that contradict an entry should be reported as a dud, so processes can change before the list catches up.

reviews.name: worldview
reviews.verdict: Our Worldview run installed 1,680 packages, built successfully in 382 seconds, and passed all 9,477 Jest tests, which makes it a credible base for teams that specifically need NASA-style imagery browsing.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that primarily need dataset search, filtering, and bulk download: Worldview sends data-download work to Earthdata Search rather than replacing that catalog.

reviews.name: typeorm
reviews.verdict: Our TypeORM install took 29 seconds, pulled 951 packages, and occupied 533 MB, then the test command failed after 26 seconds in Mocha's module-loading path.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that want a small dependency footprint: our install pulled 951 packages and occupied 533 MB before any application database driver was configured.

reviews.name: kafka
reviews.verdict: Our Kafka checkout installed 45 Python packages and built `committer-tools`, but pytest collected 0 tests, so our run says nothing about broker correctness.
reviews.skip_if: Small applications that only need a job queue: Kafka's brokers, partitions, retention, and operational surface can cost more attention than the workload deserves.

reviews.name: marimo
reviews.verdict: Our build passed in 31 seconds and all 82 measured Vitest tests passed, but the 1,899-package, 1,505 MB install shows that marimo is a full development environment rather than a thin notebook widget.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that need drop-in Jupyter behavior: marimo can convert `.ipynb` files, but its dependency graph and reactive execution change notebook semantics.

reviews.name: alloy
reviews.verdict: Use Alloy when one team owns several telemetry signals and wants one programmable agent that speaks OpenTelemetry and Grafana's native ecosystems.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that only need to tail a few log files: Alloy's multi-signal component graph adds concepts and configuration that a focused log shipper avoids.

reviews.name: sqlx
reviews.verdict: SQLx is the default recommendation for Rust teams that already know their SQL and want async access without hiding the database behind an ORM.
reviews.skip_if: Developers who want an ORM with relationships and a Rust query DSL: the README explicitly says SQLx is not an ORM.

reviews.name: cloudnative-pg
reviews.verdict: CloudNativePG is a strong choice when Kubernetes is already your operating model and your team wants PostgreSQL expressed through the same API.
reviews.skip_if: Teams without Kubernetes: the project explicitly supports only Kubernetes and is not a standalone PostgreSQL manager.

reviews.name: jax
reviews.verdict: Our JAX run installed 39 packages and built successfully, but pytest stopped after 200 collection or setup errors before any test ran.
reviews.skip_if: Developers expecting arbitrary NumPy code to compile unchanged: the README says `jit` constrains Python control flow, and traced values follow JAX-specific rules.

reviews.name: polars
reviews.verdict: Our Polars sandbox installed 441 packages in 49 seconds, then both the build and tests failed because the linker could not find `-lpython3.11`, so source contributors need a prepared Python development toolchain.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that require drop-in pandas compatibility: Polars uses its own expression model, and migration means changing code rather than swapping an import.

reviews.name: google-timeline-visualizer
reviews.verdict: Our Timeline Visualizer run installed 42 packages in 32 seconds and passed all 36 tests, making the Python path unusually easy to verify for a location-video tool.
reviews.skip_if: People unwilling to sideload Android software: the README says the app is not yet on Google Play and requires installing an APK from GitHub.

reviews.name: tantivy
reviews.verdict: Our Tantivy run built in 111 seconds and passed all 1,270 tests, the cleanest lab result in this group.
reviews.skip_if: Teams expecting a drop-in Elasticsearch or Solr replacement: the README says Tantivy is a library, and distributed search is out of scope.

reviews.name: vector
reviews.verdict: Our Vector build was still unfinished at 900 seconds, and the test command failed after 708 seconds with no test count, so source contributors should expect a heavy Rust cycle.
reviews.skip_if: Trace-pipeline buyers: the README still labels traces as coming soon rather than a current capability.

reviews.name: arnis
reviews.verdict: Our Arnis run built in 345 seconds and all 618 tests passed, making it an unusually credible starting point for turning one selected real place into a Minecraft save.
reviews.skip_if: Server owners seeking an Earth world that expands safely over time: issue 1036 says fixed coordinates, generated-area tracking, and protection for player-built chunks are still requests.

reviews.name: tempo
reviews.verdict: Our Tempo run built in 204 seconds, but 1 of 54 tested packages failed, so the measured commit needs a test investigation before an internal build is promoted.
reviews.skip_if: Teams seeking one install with collection, storage, authentication, and a full user interface: Tempo is the backend, and the official architecture puts collectors before it and Grafana after it.

reviews.name: payload
reviews.verdict: Our Payload workspace installed 2,292 packages and built in 101 seconds, but all 95 test files failed during setup before any tests ran.
reviews.skip_if: Teams outside the Next.js and TypeScript stack: Payload's main advantage is its native place inside that application model.

reviews.name: directus
reviews.verdict: Our Directus install added 2,195 packages and used 1,227 MB, then built in 42 seconds before the overall test command failed after 292 seconds.
reviews.skip_if: Organizations that assume source-visible means OSI open source: Directus uses the Monospace Sustainable Core License, with revenue, employee, tier, and commercial terms.

reviews.name: metabase
reviews.verdict: Our source install of Metabase commit ad801f2 failed after 67 seconds at its Bun preinstall check, so most BI teams should start with the official image, JAR, or cloud service.
reviews.skip_if: Developers wanting a small codebase to fork casually: our checkout had 21,439 files, about 1.36 million source lines, and separate Clojure and JavaScript stacks.

reviews.name: dbt-core
reviews.verdict: Our dbt Core run installed 33 packages in 23 seconds and built in 9 seconds, but the harness found no test target, so the measured checkout is easy to build and incomplete to verify.
reviews.skip_if: Teams without an existing warehouse or compatible adapter: dbt transforms data where it already lives and is not a database or ingestion service.

reviews.name: typesense
reviews.verdict: Our Typesense checkout installed only 10 API-test packages in 14 seconds, then exposed no build or test target, so this run proves little about server readiness.
reviews.skip_if: Log and observability teams that need Elasticsearch's broad analytics stack: the Typesense README positions this server around user-facing search rather than petabyte-scale logs.

reviews.name: chroma
reviews.verdict: Our Chroma install took 392 seconds, and pytest ran 0 tests because 2 collection errors stopped on a missing `hypothesis` module.
reviews.skip_if: Teams demanding identical local and distributed behavior: Chroma's open-source page says the two modes use different storage systems and local Chroma may lack features.

reviews.name: qdrant
reviews.verdict: Our Qdrant build took 680 seconds, and `cargo test` ended with 23 failures in storage-read API cases despite 134 passes, so source adopters should reproduce that suite before shipping commit `74f3e85`.
reviews.skip_if: Developers wanting a library that creates embeddings for them: Qdrant stores and searches vectors, while the application or another model service supplies them.

reviews.name: redis
reviews.verdict: Our Redis checkout run installed 40 packages and found 2 known vulnerabilities in a nested validator, but it collected 0 tests and never built the server, so it cannot support a server-readiness claim.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that need the supplied lab run to prove the Redis server itself builds and passes tests: our harness only exercised `utils/req-res-validator`.

reviews.name: mermaid
reviews.verdict: Our run installed 2,209 packages, then completed both the 38-second build and 217-second test step successfully.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that need precise, free-form visual design rather than layout from text Small projects unwilling to absorb a large Node development dependency tree Maintainers who expect a tiny contributor setup with near-instant installation Users who need every diagram change to…

reviews.name: podman
reviews.verdict: Our Podman checkout installed 35 Python packages and built in 22 seconds combined, but all 47 REST tests errored during setup because `bin/podman` was absent.
reviews.skip_if: Kubernetes nodes that need a CRI runtime: the README places CRI support outside Podman's scope and points to CRI-O.

reviews.name: nnn
reviews.verdict: Our nnn run installed in 6 seconds and built in 21 seconds, but its test step stopped with `no test target`, so the program is easy to compile while the checkout gives a new contributor no passing test command.
reviews.skip_if: Users who want graphical drag, drop, thumbnails, and discoverable menus with no terminal vocabulary: nnn's normal interface is keyboard driven, and the README tells beginners to rely on arrows, `/`, `q`, and `Tab`.

reviews.name: magic-wormhole
reviews.verdict: Our Magic Wormhole run installed 76 packages in 51 seconds and passed 462 tests with 0 failures, making it an easy recommendation for occasional person-to-person transfers.
reviews.skip_if: Backup or migration jobs that must resume safely after interruption: issue #722 reports a 31.53 GB directory transfer that stalled at 100% and left no received files after the receiver stopped it.

reviews.name: ruby
reviews.verdict: Our Cargo-oriented run built in 4 seconds but discovered 0 tests, so it says nothing about whether a full CRuby checkout passes its documented Make suites.
reviews.skip_if: Application developers who only need a stable Ruby executable: the README directs them to official downloads and third-party version managers instead of a source checkout.

reviews.name: roslyn
reviews.verdict: Our sandbox did not run commit db9d3ac because C# is unsupported and the repository supplied no Dockerfile, so source-build ease remains unverified here.
reviews.skip_if: Application developers who only need to compile C# or Visual Basic: the .NET SDK already ships the compiler, so cloning Roslyn adds needless complexity.

reviews.name: swift
reviews.verdict: Our run of Swift's `cmpcodesize` utility installed 36 packages and passed 3 of 3 tests, but that small success should not be mistaken for building the 3.5-million-line compiler.
reviews.skip_if: Contributors with a small development machine: the official guide recommends 150 GB free, at least 8 GB of RAM for a toolchain build, and 16 GB for development.

reviews.name: nx
reviews.verdict: Our Nx checkout installed 4,313 packages, used 3,120 MB, then failed both build and tests because `dotnet` was absent, so contributing to Nx requires a genuinely polyglot toolchain.
reviews.skip_if: Small repositories with a few fast scripts: Nx adds a project graph, configuration, plugins, and upgrade work that may cost more than it saves.

reviews.name: terminal
reviews.verdict: Our 3-CPU, 8 GB Debian sandbox could not run commit `ad06aa0` because the C++ project has no supported lab path and no Dockerfile.
reviews.skip_if: macOS or Linux users seeking a native cross-platform terminal: the supported application requires Windows 10 2004, build 19041, or later.

reviews.name: jdk
reviews.verdict: Our OpenJDK run stopped after 5 seconds because direct execution of `./configure` was denied, so it says nothing about whether the 13-million-line JDK builds or passes tests.
reviews.skip_if: Application developers who only need Java to compile or run software: a vendor JDK binary avoids a 694 MB source checkout and native toolchain setup.

reviews.name: llvm-project
reviews.verdict: Our 2,270.2 MB LLVM checkout installed 35 Python packages, but the 9-second harness build failed before producing a native toolchain, which shows how poorly a generic project runner fits this repository.
reviews.skip_if: Developers who only need a C or C++ compiler on a workstation: the release notes recommend platform binaries, while our source checkout occupied 2,270.2 MB before a real native build.

reviews.name: micro
reviews.verdict: Our build finished in 24 seconds and all 12 measured tests passed, which makes micro an easy editor to trial and a credible tool to keep on remote machines.
reviews.skip_if: Vim or Neovim users whose workflow depends on modal editing, language-server clients, and a large plugin market: micro deliberately starts from conventional shortcuts and simpler built-ins.

reviews.name: raylib
reviews.verdict: Our raylib configuration failed in 12 seconds because the fresh Debian container lacked X11 development files, so source setup on Linux is simple only after the platform packages are in place.
reviews.skip_if: Developers who want a visual editor, scene graph, asset pipeline, or inspector: the README explicitly describes raylib as code-only and offers no visual helpers.

reviews.name: nuclei
reviews.verdict: Our Nuclei run installed 758 packages and built in 269 seconds, but 3 of 143 tests failed with no cause visible in the supplied tail.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone without explicit permission to probe the target: Nuclei can send active HTTP, DNS, TCP, headless-browser, fuzzing, and code-driven checks at high concurrency.

reviews.name: usage
reviews.verdict: Our npm run installed 274 packages in 35 seconds, then found no standard build or test target, so it verified the documentation toolchain's dependencies rather than the Rust product.
reviews.skip_if: Authors of deliberately unusual parsers: the specification documentation says Usage targets standard GNU-style options and cannot model every CLI.

reviews.name: DefinitelyTyped
reviews.verdict: Our DefinitelyTyped checkout reached 62,951 files and npm stopped after 70 seconds because the monorepo requires pnpm.
reviews.skip_if: TypeScript library authors deciding where to publish new types: the README tells authors to bundle declarations with their own package.

reviews.name: slint
reviews.verdict: Slint is one of the strongest open-source choices for a team that needs the same native UI model across Rust or C++, desktop, and constrained devices.
reviews.skip_if: Proprietary embedded products without budget or approval for a commercial license: the free royalty-free license excludes embedded systems.

reviews.name: learnGitBranching
reviews.verdict: Our sandbox installed 598 packages in 25 seconds, built the app in 12 seconds, and passed its tests in 8 seconds, so LearnGitBranching is straightforward to verify even with a sizable dependency tree.
reviews.skip_if: Learners who need exact behavior from every Git command: an open issue confirms that the simulator models `git clone` in the opposite direction from real Git.

reviews.name: cilium
reviews.verdict: Our Cilium build took 438 seconds and 209 of 210 tests passed, so skilled Kubernetes teams have a credible codebase here, with one unresolved failure in our sandbox.
reviews.skip_if: Clusters on unsupported hosts: the current requirements name AMD64 or AArch64 and Linux kernel 5.10 or an approved distribution equivalent.

reviews.name: zizmor
reviews.verdict: Our zizmor install took 352 seconds, while the build needed only 5 seconds and pip-audit found 0 known vulnerabilities in the installed Python packages.
reviews.skip_if: Teams whose pipelines live mainly in GitLab CI, CircleCI, Jenkins, or another non-GitHub format: the documented audits center on GitHub Actions, Dependabot, and pre-commit.

reviews.name: GitNexus
reviews.verdict: Our GitNexus install took 15 seconds and left 205 packages using 93 MB, but the repository root exposed no build or test target for us to verify.
reviews.skip_if: Commercial teams expecting a permissive open-source license: PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0 requires separate permission for ordinary workplace use.

reviews.name: quiche
reviews.verdict: Our quiche run built in 216 seconds and passed all 1,386 cargo tests, the cleanest result in this group.
reviews.skip_if: Application developers who only want to make HTTP/3 requests: the README says quiche is low level and makes the caller provide sockets, timers, and an event loop.

reviews.name: nixpkgs
reviews.verdict: Our check of `ci/github-script/` took 11 seconds, installed 0 packages, and found 5 known vulnerabilities, but it did not build Nixpkgs or run NixOS tests.
reviews.skip_if: Users who want a conventional mutable Linux setup and do not want to learn Nix expressions: the README describes NixOS as purely functional and points to three separate manuals.

reviews.name: wasmtime
reviews.verdict: Our Wasmtime build succeeded after 389 seconds, but the 286-second test run failed when `wasm32-unknown-unknown` was unavailable to a test-program build.
reviews.skip_if: Teams seeking a tiny source build: our checkout installed 351 packages and the successful build took 389 seconds on 3 CPUs.

reviews.name: yazi
reviews.verdict: We built Yazi successfully in 264 seconds, but `cargo test` ran 0 tests, so the project is easier to build than its green test result is to trust.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone who needs upgrades to preserve every configuration and plugin API: the README calls Yazi a public beta in heavy development and warns about breaking changes.

reviews.name: omarchy
reviews.verdict: Omarchy is compelling if its screenshots, shortcuts, and chosen applications already resemble the workstation you want.
reviews.skip_if: Organizations that require Secure Boot or TPM to stay enabled: the installation guide explicitly tells users to disable them in firmware.

reviews.name: rayhunter
reviews.verdict: Our Rayhunter build stopped after 147 seconds because embedded web assets were absent, and the test command hit the same compile failure in 16 seconds.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone seeking a phone app that works on arbitrary hardware: the docs recommend the Orbic RC400L for the Americas and TP-Link M7350 for Africa, Europe, and the Middle East.

reviews.name: LACT
reviews.verdict: Our LACT build stopped in 42 seconds because GTK 4.8.3 did not meet the required 4.14 floor, and the test command hit the same check before running tests.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone who wants the same experience on Windows or macOS: LACT is specifically a Linux GPU tool.

reviews.name: awesome-copilot
reviews.verdict: Our Awesome Copilot run installed 150 packages and built in 13 seconds with 0 npm audit findings, but it exposed no test target for the catalog's promised behavior.
reviews.skip_if: Developers committed to another coding assistant: installation paths and file formats target GitHub Copilot.

reviews.name: k9s
reviews.verdict: Our K9s build completed in 241 seconds, but 3 of 21 Go packages failed their tests, so commit 24cf462 is usable for evaluation without earning a clean engineering bill.
reviews.skip_if: Kubernetes beginners seeking an explanatory control plane: K9s exposes cluster objects and actions quickly, but it assumes you understand what editing, deleting, attaching, and port forwarding do.

reviews.name: trufflehog
reviews.verdict: Our TruffleHog build succeeded, but 7 of 220 tests failed after a 521-second run, so pin and qualify the exact version before making it a mandatory gate.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that prohibit outbound credential verification: TruffleHog can test findings against provider APIs, which exposes them to the service that appears to have issued them.

reviews.name: git-ai
reviews.verdict: Our Git AI run passed 2,324 of 2,325 tests after a 293-second build, with the lone failure tied to an unsupported `git merge-tree` option in our sandbox.
reviews.skip_if: Compliance teams that require attribution to be infallible: issue 2221 reports new files created by Copilot being silently marked as human work.

reviews.name: devenv
reviews.verdict: Our devenv build reached 219 seconds before `nix-flake-c.pc` stopped it, and tests hit a separate missing Zig executable after 46 seconds, so building the project itself needs more than a Rust toolchain.
reviews.skip_if: Teams unwilling to adopt Nix: the official installation starts by installing Nix, and the main configuration is `devenv.nix`.

reviews.name: alacritty
reviews.verdict: Our Alacritty build passed in 66 seconds and 219 of 220 tests passed, with one Unix password-entry test failing on `pw not found`.
reviews.skip_if: Users who need built-in tabs or split panes: the FAQ explicitly leaves those jobs to a window manager or terminal multiplexer.

reviews.name: skills
reviews.verdict: Our Skills run installed 126 packages in 5 seconds, then passed its 9-second build and 32-second test step, making it a credible cross-agent installer with one serious current caution.
reviews.skip_if: Users who assume downloaded instructions are safe because the CLI installed them: the README documents transport and size limits, not a trust guarantee for skill content.

reviews.name: grype
reviews.verdict: Our Grype run built in 134 seconds, but 4 of 98 test packages failed in integration, so adoption should include a pinned test image and checks for scanner drift.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that need one scanner to be the final authority on every package: open issues 3674 and 3670 document an incorrect Grafana constraint and a missed vendored OpenSSL binary.

reviews.name: project-based-learning
reviews.verdict: Our Project Based Learning checkout built in 3 seconds, but its 14 files exposed no test target and almost all teaching happens on external sites.
reviews.skip_if: Beginners who need a sequenced curriculum: entries are grouped by language and topic, with no shared difficulty scale or prerequisite path.

reviews.name: supervision
reviews.verdict: Our Supervision run installed 50 packages and built in 7 seconds, while the test step ended with 2 `sklearn` collection errors after logging 3,517 passes.
reviews.skip_if: Users expecting a trained model: Supervision consumes model output and the README points to separate model packages or hosted inference.

reviews.name: system-design-primer
reviews.verdict: The System Design Primer is the definitive, free starting point for anyone serious about mastering system design for technical interviews.
reviews.skip_if: System design experts looking for cutting-edge research or highly specialized techniques; this is a primer, not an advanced academic text.

reviews.name: gh-stack
reviews.verdict: Our gh-stack run installed 203 packages and passed all 15 tests, so the extension is easy to trial but its v0.1.0 behavior still needs supervision.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that need stable automation exit codes today: issue 472 reports that `gh stack sync` can print success and exit 0 after its push fails.

reviews.name: opentofu
reviews.verdict: Our OpenTofu build succeeded in 181 seconds, but 3 of 130 Go package tests failed, so the CLI is credible for an evaluated migration rather than a blind swap.
reviews.skip_if: Organizations that require every clean checkout to pass its full test suite: 3 of 130 Go package tests failed in our sandbox.

reviews.name: traefik
reviews.verdict: Our Traefik build passed in 311 seconds, but 3 of 50 Go test groups failed after a 597-second run without a specific error in the supplied tail.
reviews.skip_if: A single static website with two upstreams: Traefik's provider model and two-layer configuration add more concepts than a short Nginx or Caddy file.

reviews.name: dbeaver
reviews.verdict: Our DBeaver source build stopped after 4 seconds because Maven could not resolve its snapshot parent POM, although the install step finished in 6 seconds.
reviews.skip_if: Contributors expecting a fresh Maven checkout to build by itself: our commit 45557da run stopped because the parent POM `com.dbeaver.common.main:2.8.0-SNAPSHOT` could not be resolved.

reviews.name: hoppscotch
reviews.verdict: Hoppscotch is an easy recommendation for developers who want a capable API client that works immediately in a browser and can later move to desktop or self-hosting.
reviews.skip_if: Community-edition teams that require SSO: the README marks single sign-on as an Enterprise Edition feature.

reviews.name: lazydocker
reviews.verdict: Our lazydocker run built in 24 seconds and passed all 6 measured tests in 11 seconds, which makes it the cleanest trial in this group.
reviews.skip_if: Shared-host operators who cannot accept broad Docker control: the container install mounts `/var/run/docker.sock`, which effectively grants control over the daemon.

reviews.name: gitea
reviews.verdict: Our Gitea checkout pulled 913 packages and occupied 579 MB, yet exposed no build or test target to the harness, so source contributors should budget for the project's separate Go and frontend workflow.
reviews.skip_if: Teams expecting source setup to be one JavaScript command: our pnpm install found no build or test target, while the README sends contributors to separate Go and frontend build guides.

reviews.name: vscode
reviews.verdict: Our VS Code checkout spent 505 seconds in `npm install` before node-gyp failed on `native-keymap`, so source contribution needs more care than installing the polished desktop product.
reviews.skip_if: Developers who only want to use VS Code: the packaged product avoids an 18,132-file source checkout and native dependency build.

reviews.name: ESP32-Bit-Pirate
reviews.verdict: ESP32 Bit Pirate is an essential tool for any modern electronics workbench.
reviews.skip_if: Beginners with zero electronics experience; while user-friendly, it assumes some knowledge of protocols like I2C or UART.

reviews.name: opik
reviews.verdict: Our Opik load-test subproject installed 108 packages and built in 28 seconds combined, but its test run timed out after 157 seconds while flushing an attachment trace.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that only need application logs or OpenTelemetry storage: Opik adds prompt management, evaluations, model integrations, and an AI-specific data model.

reviews.name: ai
reviews.verdict: Our AI SDK workspace install consumed 4,066 MB, and its build stopped after 67 of 91 tasks succeeded, so contributing to the monorepo is far heavier than installing the `ai` package.
reviews.skip_if: Projects pinned below Node.js 22: the README makes Node 22 or newer the installation baseline.

reviews.name: adk-go
reviews.verdict: Our ADK Go run installed 289 packages, built successfully, and passed all 72 tests, so the core library deserves a trial for teams committed to Go.
reviews.skip_if: Developers who want a finished assistant application: the README describes a toolkit and points to samples, so product UI, permissions, prompts, storage choices, and operations remain application work.

reviews.name: langfuse
reviews.verdict: Our Langfuse install consumed 2,182 MB, then the web build stopped in 12 seconds on environment validation, so the source checkout is not a zero-config trial.
reviews.skip_if: Teams wanting a stateless log viewer: self-hosting uses persistent application and analytics services, with Kubernetes listed as the preferred production deployment.

reviews.name: mcp-toolbox
reviews.verdict: Our mcp-toolbox run built in 261 seconds, but 49 of 452 tests failed because integration settings such as `VALKEY_ADDRESS` and `YUGABYTEDB_DATABASE` were missing.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone unwilling to let an AI-triggered service reach production data: the prebuilt sets include schema discovery and SQL execution, so database roles and exposed toolsets need careful limits.

reviews.name: openclaude
reviews.verdict: Our OpenClaude checkout installed in 47 seconds, built in 9 seconds, and completed its tests in 138 seconds, the only clean three-stage result among these seven reviews.
reviews.skip_if: Companies that require clear redistribution rights: the license says the repository contains proprietary Claude Code-derived code, lacks Anthropic authorization to distribute it, and grants MIT terms only to contributor modifications where legally possible.

reviews.name: agents
reviews.verdict: Our LiveKit Agents install took 27 seconds and only 37 MB, but pytest stopped in 6 seconds because the `livekit` package could not be imported.
reviews.skip_if: Text-only assistants that do not need WebRTC or telephony: the repository includes a text example, but most of its value and operating cost sit in real-time media.

reviews.name: transformers
reviews.verdict: Transformers remains the first library to try when a published model has a Hugging Face implementation and you need direct control over inference or training.
reviews.skip_if: Developers who only need a hosted chat API: model weights, device placement, memory use, and preprocessing become your responsibility here.

reviews.name: unsloth
reviews.verdict: Our Unsloth run installed 45 packages in 40 seconds and passed all 393 executed tests, so its Python core deserves a trial from anyone who needs local fine-tuning or a combined model workspace.
reviews.skip_if: Operators who plan to expose the default Studio service without a security review: the README says server-side tools are enabled by default and advises using a strong password or `--disable-tools`.

reviews.name: anything-llm
reviews.verdict: Our AnythingLLM run installed 288 packages in 52 seconds and passed 180 of 182 tests, but Jest still exited 1 with 34 failed suites.
reviews.skip_if: Teams expecting every provider to share one interchangeable configuration: open issue 6162 says two local AI endpoints cannot be registered together and the context window is fixed in settings.

reviews.name: LocalAI
reviews.verdict: Our LocalAI run installed 1,246 packages and built in 11 seconds, but 2 of 34 tested Go packages failed, so it is a serious platform to trial rather than a server to trust untouched.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone wanting a tiny single-purpose text server: the README covers more than 60 backends and several modalities, while our checkout contained 5,114 files.

reviews.name: llama.cpp
reviews.verdict: Our llama.cpp build finished in 10 seconds, but the test command stopped with 2 collection errors and pip-audit found 6 known vulnerabilities, so the engine is easy to try and still demands a controlled deployment.
reviews.skip_if: Teams wanting arbitrary model files to run unchanged: the model guide requires GGUF and sends other formats through conversion scripts.

reviews.name: ollama
reviews.verdict: Our Ollama build took 116 seconds and all 60 tests passed, making it an unusually low-risk way to try local models if you accept that model choice and hardware still determine the experience.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that need a source build to stay pure Go: the development guide requires CMake 3.24 or newer, a C/C++ compiler, and native CGO payloads.

reviews.name: istio
reviews.verdict: Our Istio run installed 597 packages and built successfully, but 8 of 151 tested packages failed after a 467-second test step, so source adopters need an environment-aware validation plan.
reviews.skip_if: Small deployments that can solve routing and TLS at an ingress gateway: Istio adds Istiod plus Envoy sidecars or ztunnel to the cluster.

reviews.name: coolify
reviews.verdict: Our Coolify checkout installed 55 packages in 76 seconds and built in 8 seconds, but its available package targets gave us no test suite to run.
reviews.skip_if: Shared-hosting customers or developers without root access: the installer refuses to run without root or sudo and writes under `/data/coolify`.

reviews.name: vault
reviews.verdict: Our Vault build succeeded after 550 seconds, but the test command reached 900 seconds with 15 failures, including database tests that could not reach Docker.
reviews.skip_if: Small teams with a few static secrets and no staff to operate another critical service: Vault adds initialization, unsealing, policies, storage, backups, upgrades, and incident procedures.

reviews.name: netbox
reviews.verdict: Our NetBox install added 126 packages and 371 MB, built in 10 seconds, and reported 8 known vulnerabilities, so adoption needs dependency review as well as network modeling work.
reviews.skip_if: Teams seeking a controller that directly configures network devices: the README explicitly says NetBox does not interact with nodes.

reviews.name: Stirling-PDF
reviews.verdict: Our 23-second install covered only Stirling PDF's 122-package developer-tool folder, so it proves the repo tooling is tidy but says nothing about server readiness.
reviews.skip_if: Buyers who require every useful administration feature under a conventional open-source license: the README calls the product open-core and links SSO and auditing to paid offerings.

reviews.name: envoy
reviews.verdict: Our Envoy run installed 49 Go packages and built the detected target, but all 3 attempted tests failed, so adopters should validate the exact proxy and extensions they will ship.
reviews.skip_if: Operators seeking a small static reverse-proxy configuration: Envoy's xDS control plane, filter chains, clusters, listeners, and runtime guards create a much larger operating surface.

reviews.name: discourse
reviews.verdict: Our Discourse install stopped after 68 seconds on an exact Node engine mismatch, so self-hosters should treat version pinning and operations as part of the product choice.
reviews.skip_if: Shared-hosting customers using cPanel, Plesk, or Webmin: the official install guide says only Docker-based production installs are supported.

reviews.name: bentopdf
reviews.verdict: BentoPDF is an excellent first choice for an internal PDF portal because the useful work happens in the browser and the self-hosted image does not remove PDF features.
reviews.skip_if: Proprietary products whose owners will not publish their modifications under AGPL-3.0 or buy the separate commercial license.

reviews.name: puter
reviews.verdict: Puter is unusually ambitious and, based on our clean install and build, much more tangible than its grand internet-computer label might suggest.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone seeking a small, single-purpose file server, because Puter is a full web desktop Operators who require a supplied automated test target before deployment Organizations that cannot meet AGPL-3.0 obligations Very small servers, because our npm install alone occupied 1,152…

reviews.name: hister
reviews.verdict: Hister is one of the more useful self-hosted answers to the question, 'Where did I read that?' Its binary setup, full-text capture, query language, terminal UI, and cautious MCP output make it worth trying on a private machine.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone unwilling to store copies of sensitive signed-in pages: the browser extension submits rendered text and HTML, and full HTML previews are enabled by default.

reviews.name: luci
reviews.verdict: Use LuCI when the device already runs OpenWrt and humans need to administer it.
reviews.skip_if: Developers looking for a standalone Node web app: this repository is an OpenWrt feed, and its npm dependencies are documentation and lint tooling rather than a runnable router UI.

reviews.name: nomad
reviews.verdict: Our Nomad checkout installed 1,517 pnpm packages in 47 seconds, but it exposed no build or test target, so our run did not validate the scheduler binary.
reviews.skip_if: Organizations with an OSI-open-source-only procurement rule: current Nomad uses Business Source License 1.1 and later converts each version to MPL 2.0.

reviews.name: coder
reviews.verdict: Our Coder checkout installed 189 pnpm packages in 16 seconds, but it exposed no build or test target to the harness, so we did not verify the 1.47-million-line platform.
reviews.skip_if: Solo developers who only need one remote machine: Coder adds a control plane, Terraform templates, workspace agents, and a database to that simpler job.

reviews.name: firecracker
reviews.verdict: Our Firecracker source build installed 118 packages in 38 seconds, then failed because the linker could not find `-lseccomp`, so a source checkout needs more host preparation than the successful install step suggests.
reviews.skip_if: Developers who want a complete container platform: Firecracker exposes a host API for one microVM process, while orchestration, image management, network allocation, and recovery remain outside the project.

reviews.name: plane
reviews.verdict: Plane is one of the more credible self-hosted choices for teams that have outgrown a board but resent Jira's weight.
reviews.skip_if: Small teams that only need a shared Kanban board: Plane's workspaces, modules, cycles, pages, analytics, and service stack add administration they may never use.

reviews.name: go-ethereum
reviews.verdict: Geth is a sensible default execution client when you want broad Ethereum compatibility, current protocol work, and mature operator documentation.
reviews.skip_if: Operators looking for a lightweight mainnet service: the README asks for at least four CPU cores, 8 GB RAM, 1 TB of free storage, and steady bandwidth.

reviews.name: FreeTube
reviews.verdict: Our FreeTube build reached the RPM packaging stage after 189 seconds, then failed because `rpmbuild` was absent; the ready-made downloads are the sensible installation path.
reviews.skip_if: People who expect anonymity from installation alone: the README says YouTube can still see video requests and recommends a VPN or Tor to hide the IP.

reviews.name: authelia
reviews.verdict: Our Authelia build completed in 229 seconds, but 4 of 25 test groups failed after a 510-second run, so adopters should reproduce the suite on their deployment platform before trusting an upgrade.
reviews.skip_if: Teams seeking an identity service with no infrastructure ownership: production setup includes HTTPS, proxy integration, secret files, storage, notification delivery, and access rules.

reviews.name: CPA-Manager-Plus
reviews.verdict: Our CPA Manager Plus run passed a 36-second build and a 51-second test step, but npm audit still found 13 vulnerabilities, including 10 high-severity advisories.
reviews.skip_if: Teams without CPA or CLIProxyAPI: the README says CPAMP observes and manages that gateway and does not forward model traffic itself.

reviews.name: strapi
reviews.verdict: Our Strapi monorepo installed 3,991 packages in 199 seconds, then the build timed out at 900 seconds while Node spawn calls returned EAGAIN.
reviews.skip_if: Teams expecting a complete website from the CMS alone: Strapi supplies content and APIs, so the frontend remains your job.

reviews.name: code-server
reviews.verdict: Our code-server source install ran for 447 seconds and failed in native-keymap's node-gyp step, so most users should install a release artifact rather than build this 253.5 MB checkout.
reviews.skip_if: Teams expecting user isolation, workspace lifecycle, and policy management in this one process: the README directs multi-user deployments to coder/coder.

reviews.name: rancher
reviews.verdict: Our Rancher build took 544 seconds, and its tests reached our 900-second cap with 184 passes and 19 localhost-dependent failures.
reviews.skip_if: A small team with one straightforward cluster: Rancher adds another privileged control plane, upgrade schedule, and failure domain.

reviews.name: netbird
reviews.verdict: Our NetBird build passed in 8 seconds, but the Go test command timed out at 900 seconds after recording 104 passing and 11 failing package results.
reviews.skip_if: Operators looking for a tiny two-host VPN: NetBird adds centralized management, signaling, relays, identity, policy, and an admin layer around WireGuard.

reviews.name: sourcebot
reviews.verdict: Our Sourcebot build passed in 245 seconds, but its backend workspace ended with 304 tests passed and 1 failed, so the codebase is buildable without being a clean checkout for contributors.
reviews.skip_if: Companies that require an immediately permissive license or want to sell a competing hosted service: most code uses FSL-1.1-ALv2, which restricts competing use until each version converts to Apache 2.0 after two years.

reviews.name: pocket-id
reviews.verdict: Our Pocket ID build passed in 38 seconds, but its Playwright run stopped with 2 failures and left 182 tests unrun, so test the complete sign-in path before moving real accounts.
reviews.skip_if: Organizations that must retain passwords as a fallback: the README says Pocket ID supports only passkey authentication.

reviews.name: go2tv
reviews.verdict: Our Go2TV run installed 51 packages in 9 seconds and passed all 32 tests, making it an unusually low-friction trial for direct home-network casting.
reviews.skip_if: Households that want indexed libraries, user accounts, watch history, and TV apps: Go2TV is a sender, while its web mode exposes selected folders and playback controls.

reviews.name: sing-box
reviews.verdict: Our sing-box build succeeded in 107 seconds, but 3 of 18 test groups failed, so experienced network operators should treat a source build as something to verify rather than install blindly.
reviews.skip_if: People looking for a normal click-to-connect consumer VPN: the core is driven by a large JSON configuration surface, while graphical clients and profile providers sit around it.

reviews.name: memos
reviews.verdict: Our Memos build passed in 170 seconds, but the 420-second test run ended with 11 packages passing and 1 failing, so source builders should budget time to inspect the suite.
reviews.skip_if: People who need reliable offline mobile access: open issue #6231 asks for an offline PWA because notes currently become unavailable without a connection.

reviews.name: firefly-iii
reviews.verdict: Our Firefly III checkout installed 781 npm packages in 29 seconds, but it exposed no npm build or test target, so that clean result does not prove the PHP application is ready to hold your financial history.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone wanting bank sync inside one simple application: the README sends imports to external ecosystem tools, and an open Enable Banking report describes a 422 pagination failure that silently skipped an account's remaining transactions.

reviews.name: listmonk
reviews.verdict: Our listmonk build finished in 73 seconds after installing 85 packages, but `go test` found 0 tests, so the clean compile is stronger evidence than the test count.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that want a hosted service to own sending reputation, bounce operations, upgrades, and database backups: listmonk is self-hosted and still needs SMTP or another delivery provider.

reviews.name: mattermost
reviews.verdict: Our Mattermost server build completed in 137 seconds, but 79 of 94 test package results failed or did not build, so the codebase is buildable while a bare container is not a faithful full test environment.
reviews.skip_if: Teams without an operator for PostgreSQL, Linux, backups, monitoring, and security updates: self-hosting shifts those jobs to you.

reviews.name: portainer
reviews.verdict: Our Portainer build took 90 seconds after installing 1,704 packages, and its tests completed successfully in 230 seconds, so the codebase is workable but far from tiny.
reviews.skip_if: Podman operators expecting broad, frictionless support: release 2.39.6 limits support to rootful Podman 5 on CentOS 9 and documents cross-runtime socket restrictions.

reviews.name: uptime-kuma
reviews.verdict: Our Uptime Kuma run installed 2,356 packages and built in 27 seconds, but its tests exited 1 and npm audit found 44 known vulnerabilities, so the Docker image is the better trial path than a casual source deployment.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that require NFS-backed storage: the README explicitly says NFS and similar network filesystems are unsupported for the data directory.

reviews.name: server
reviews.verdict: Our Nextcloud checkout installed 2,227 packages, occupied 1,184 MB, built in 105 seconds, and passed its test command, so the codebase cleared a clean sandbox run despite its size.
reviews.skip_if: Operators looking for a small file server with few moving parts: the repository spans about 1,884,196 lines of source, and the product extends through hundreds of apps.

reviews.name: immich
reviews.verdict: Our Immich checkout installed 2,460 packages and used 1,412 MB, but it exposed no root build or test target, so our run verified dependency setup rather than a working photo server.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone treating phone sync as the only backup: the README explicitly calls for a 3-2-1 backup plan.

reviews.name: hono
reviews.verdict: Our Hono run installed 872 packages in 35 seconds and built in 12 seconds, but Vitest failed at startup after 22 seconds, so the contributor checkout needs more scrutiny than the tiny application API suggests.
reviews.skip_if: Node.js teams expecting existing Express middleware to drop in unchanged: Hono has its own Handler and onion-style middleware model, and Node runs through a separate adapter.

reviews.name: php-src
reviews.verdict: Our php-src configure step failed in 16 seconds because re2c was absent, so a fresh compiler image was not enough to start building PHP.
reviews.skip_if: Application developers who only need to run Laravel, WordPress, or a PHP script: the README points ordinary users to prebuilt packages and binaries.

reviews.name: better-auth
reviews.verdict: Our Better Auth install occupied 2,841 MB and the test command ended with a failure after 159 seconds, so its convenient application API sits on top of a large, fast-moving codebase.
reviews.skip_if: CommonJS applications: the installation guide says CommonJS is unsupported.

reviews.name: reflex
reviews.verdict: Our Reflex build took 4 seconds, but all 200 reported test outcomes were failures or setup errors because the docs suite could not import `reflex_docs`, so the quick app path is cleaner than the contributor verification path we found.
reviews.skip_if: Frontend teams that need direct control of every React detail: custom gaps can require wrapping a React component, according to the architecture guide.

reviews.name: pdf.js
reviews.verdict: Our PDF.js install pulled 761 packages and occupied 331 MB, so use the source repository when you need control over a serious browser PDF engine, not for a basic embed.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that only need the browser's native PDF pane: the README's source path installs hundreds of packages and uses Gulp, while a small embed helper avoids owning a viewer.

reviews.name: full-stack-fastapi-template
reviews.verdict: Our template install consumed 1,118 MB, and its Playwright authentication setup failed before 61 tests could run, so this is a substantial starter that still needs an application-level shakedown.
reviews.skip_if: Backend-only services that need a few FastAPI routes: this template also brings React, Bun, Vite, Tailwind, shadcn/ui, Playwright, and email tooling.

reviews.name: docs
reviews.verdict: Our GitHub Docs build finished in 43 seconds, but 120 of 9,042 tests failed and the checkout plus installed dependencies occupied about 1.6 GB.
reviews.skip_if: Teams shopping for a documentation starter: this 13,454-file repository is GitHub's production site, while Docusaurus, Material for MkDocs, or Starlight are built for adoption.

reviews.name: medusa
reviews.verdict: Our Medusa checkout built successfully in 381 seconds, but the available Jest target ran only 1 test, so TypeScript commerce teams still need their own checkout, payment, tax, and fulfillment coverage.
reviews.skip_if: Merchants who want a finished hosted shop with themes, checkout, and operations handled for them: the local product is a Node.js backend plus admin, and the storefront is a separate optional application.

reviews.name: nitro
reviews.verdict: Our Nitro install pulled 1,173 packages and 1,109 MB, but the build passed in 13 seconds and tests passed in 142 seconds, so the cost is dependency weight rather than a broken toolchain.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that require a stable v3 API today: the README labels the branch as v3, points production users to v2, and the migration guide calls v3 beta backward-incompatible.

reviews.name: webpack
reviews.verdict: Our test command failed after 213 seconds on TypeScript errors, while the 1,459-package install consumed 714 MB, so contributing to webpack is a much heavier proposition than adding it to an application.
reviews.skip_if: Beginners who want a low-configuration development server: webpack's README calls it a low-level tool and admits it is not always the easiest entry-level option.

reviews.name: fastapi
reviews.verdict: Our FastAPI install used 41 packages and 45 MB, but pytest ran zero tests because 200 collection or setup errors required `httpx2`, so application setup looks easier than contributor verification at commit c3f316b.
reviews.skip_if: Teams seeking an included database layer, admin site, or complete account system: FastAPI's core web and data layers come from Starlette and Pydantic, while additional auth tooling remains tentative roadmap work.

reviews.name: rails
reviews.verdict: Our Rails checkout could not finish its 19-second Yarn install because Node 22.23.2 was below one dependency's Node 24 minimum, so this commit needs a newer JavaScript toolchain even before the Ruby suite is considered.
reviews.skip_if: Teams unwilling to use Ruby and Rails conventions: the README's model, view, and controller layers are the framework's basic design.

reviews.name: deno
reviews.verdict: Our Deno source build and test run each exceeded a 900-second cap, so installing the released runtime is easy but working on its 664.9 MB source tree is not.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that need exact Node.js behavior in every test hook: issue #36670 reports that `process.on('exit')` and `beforeExit` handlers do not run under `deno test` in Deno 2.9.5.

reviews.name: ui
reviews.verdict: Our run installed 1,668 packages and used 1,506 MB for shadcn/ui, then both the build and test steps stopped at a missing Bun executable.
reviews.skip_if: Teams expecting every shadcn v4 UI fix to arrive through one package upgrade: the introduction says the top component layer stays in your application for modification.

reviews.name: nuxt
reviews.verdict: Our Nuxt checkout installed 1,523 packages and built in 28 seconds, but its test command failed after `nuxt prepare` was killed with SIGABRT, so the measured commit needs a local test rerun before framework work begins.
reviews.skip_if: React, Svelte, or framework-neutral teams: Nuxt's components, composables, and ecosystem are centered on Vue.

reviews.name: core
reviews.verdict: Our Vue core install failed in 10 seconds with `ERR_UNKNOWN_BUILTIN_MODULE`, so commit e2bede9 did not reach build or tests in our sandbox despite the framework's easy application-level start.
reviews.skip_if: Products that must support Internet Explorer 11: the official FAQ says Vue 3 requires browsers with native ES2016 support.

reviews.name: no-negative-echo
reviews.verdict: Our no-negative-echo run installed 35 packages and passed 105 collected tests in 15 seconds, making it cheap to inspect and try.
reviews.skip_if: Teams expecting a deterministic semantic filter: the README calls this a prompt-level mitigation and says scanner PASS does not prove a semantic review.

reviews.name: mlflow
reviews.verdict: Our MLflow run installed 116 packages and used 601 MB, then 273 tests passed before 200 collection or setup errors stopped the suite.
reviews.skip_if: Developers seeking a small tracing library: our install pulled 116 packages, occupied 601 MB, and the repository held about 1,479,658 source lines.

reviews.name: blender-mcp
reviews.verdict: Our Blender MCP run installed 60 packages and passed all 20 tests in 35 seconds across install, build, and test steps.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone who cannot allow an agent to execute arbitrary Python inside Blender: the README labels that tool potentially dangerous and says to save first.

reviews.name: tensorflow
reviews.verdict: Our TensorFlow source install stopped in 5 seconds because Bazel was absent, so use the published wheel unless you have a specific reason to build its 485.5 MB repository.
reviews.skip_if: Contributors expecting a normal Python package build: the source checkout requires Bazel or Bazelisk, and our fresh Debian run stopped because neither command existed.

reviews.name: webbrain
reviews.verdict: Our WebBrain checkout installed 4 packages in 11 seconds and passed its available tests in 74 seconds, with 0 npm audit findings.
reviews.skip_if: Firefox users who need the full feature set: the README says Firefox lacks trusted mouse events, closed shadow-root access, full-page CDP screenshots, and reliable handling for some single-page app navigation.

reviews.name: RapidRAW
reviews.verdict: Our RapidRAW run installed 427 packages, built in 5 seconds, and found 0 npm vulnerabilities, but the repository offered no test target.
reviews.skip_if: Photographers whose delivery workflow cannot tolerate an occasional wrong batch output: issue 1571 reports 2 mismatched exports across roughly 850 files in a Windows 11 run.

reviews.name: Graft
reviews.verdict: Our Graft run built in 7 seconds and passed all 836 tests, but npm audit found 1 high-severity vulnerability, so the code earns a serious trial with a dependency review attached.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that prohibit tools from editing agent instructions or user-level configuration: `graft init` can write repo files plus Codex MCP and hook settings under `~/.codex/`, unless scoped with its flags.

reviews.name: blender-mcp
reviews.verdict: Our Blender MCP run installed 60 packages and passed all 20 tests in 69 seconds across install, build, and test steps.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone who cannot allow an agent to execute arbitrary Python inside Blender: the README labels that tool potentially dangerous and says to save first.

reviews.name: MTPLX
reviews.verdict: Our MTPLX install took 138 seconds and its package built in 15 seconds, but tests failed after 69 seconds because the Debian environment had no `mlx`, so our run says nothing about its advertised decoding speed.
reviews.skip_if: Linux, Windows, CUDA, or Intel Mac users: the README requires Apple Silicon M1 or newer and macOS 14+, and directs Linux users to vLLM.

reviews.name: watermarks-remover
reviews.verdict: Our watermarks-remover run installed 55 packages, built in 7 seconds, and passed its tests in 72 seconds with 0 known dependency vulnerabilities.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone trying to hide the origin of content they do not own: the README limits the intended use to privacy and hygiene on content you own.

reviews.name: OpenMAIC
reviews.verdict: Our OpenMAIC build passed in 116 seconds and 4,892 of 4,954 tests passed, but installation consumed 2,672 MB and one guarded-import test failed.
reviews.skip_if: Schools expecting generated lessons to be fact-checked automatically: the README describes generation and editing, not a guarantee of curricular accuracy.

reviews.name: FluidVoice
reviews.verdict: FluidVoice is one of the strongest free Mac dictation trials because installation is simple, model choice is broad, and the core speech path can remain local.
reviews.skip_if: Windows, Linux, iOS, or pre-macOS 15 users: the README supports only macOS 15 or later today, with Windows and iOS described as future work.

reviews.name: diagram-design
reviews.verdict: Our Diagram Design run installed 35 packages and built in 19 seconds combined, but no test target existed, so the strongest evidence is its inspectable templates and CI tooling rather than a passing suite.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that need a visual drag-and-drop editor: the README says there is no Figma workflow, and source edits happen in HTML and SVG.

reviews.name: t3code
reviews.verdict: Our T3 Code build succeeded in 60 seconds and 2,705 of 2,712 tests passed in 728 seconds with 0 failures, so this young control surface has unusually credible engineering evidence.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone expecting T3 Code to include an AI subscription: the README requires at least one supported provider CLI to be installed and authenticated first.

reviews.name: claude-seo
reviews.verdict: Our Claude SEO run installed 92 packages and built cleanly, but 2 tests failed when a dry-run hit an HTTP 403 rate limit.
reviews.skip_if: People who do not use Claude Code: this package requires its CLI, while the README points Codex users to a separate port.

reviews.name: sie
reviews.verdict: Our SIE run installed 704 packages and used 1,597 MB, then passed its build and tests in 31 seconds combined, so the codebase is workable but hardly small.
reviews.skip_if: Teams seeking one tiny image for every task: the README assigns dependency-incompatible model families to separate bundles, and generation uses another GPU image.

reviews.name: pocket-tts
reviews.verdict: Our Pocket TTS install took 39 seconds and 41 of 42 tests passed, but the remaining 8-bit WAV test failed because `soundfile` was unavailable.
reviews.skip_if: Narration teams that need exact pause or emotion markup: the README says text-controlled silence is unsupported, while emotion control remains an open request.

reviews.name: TradingAgents
reviews.verdict: Our TradingAgents checkout installed 130 packages, passed its build and tests in 145 seconds combined, and showed 0 known dependency vulnerabilities.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone seeking a proven trading strategy or dependable return: the README says runs vary and published backtest figures are not guaranteed to reproduce.

reviews.name: firecrawl-mcp-server
reviews.verdict: Our Firecrawl MCP Server run installed 341 packages, built in 5 seconds, and passed all 74 tests in 24 seconds, making the adapter easy to trial.
reviews.skip_if: Users who expect the local server to perform scraping by itself: it is a bridge to the Firecrawl cloud API or a separately hosted Firecrawl backend.

reviews.name: awesome-cursorrules
reviews.verdict: Our awesome-cursorrules run installed 0 packages and passed all 84 tests in 7 seconds, confirming the collection's structural checks rather than the correctness of every coding recommendation.
reviews.skip_if: Developers expecting an executable coding agent: the repository is a collection of Markdown rule files, not a model or editor.

reviews.name: agent-of-empires
reviews.verdict: Our Agent of Empires build succeeded, and 4,656 of 4,660 tests passed before four failures, including one tied directly to missing tmux, so the codebase is credible but the stated prerequisite is real.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone looking for an AI model or coding agent by itself: AoE launches separately installed agent CLIs and does not replace their accounts, credentials, or usage plans.

reviews.name: harbor
reviews.verdict: Our Harbor checkout installed 97 packages in 19 seconds and used 121 MB, but it offered no build or test target, so the easy setup does not provide a full verification result.
reviews.skip_if: Teams looking for a production deployment platform: Harbor's README explicitly describes it as a helper for local LLM development, not deployment.

reviews.name: Unity-MCP
reviews.verdict: Our Unity-MCP CLI run installed 64 packages, built in 12 seconds, and passed its tests in 33 seconds, making it an easy technical trial for a Unity team.
reviews.skip_if: Teams whose Unity project path contains spaces: the README explicitly says those paths are unsupported.

reviews.name: gptme
reviews.verdict: Our gptme run passed 9,557 tests but still ended with 27 failures and 75 errors after 632 seconds, so the project is substantial and the current checkout needs environment-specific verification.
reviews.skip_if: Users who need a narrow coding assistant with few moving parts: gptme includes shell, Python, browser, vision, desktop, subagent, server, plugin, MCP, and automation surfaces.

reviews.name: code2prompt
reviews.verdict: Our Code2Prompt build took 241 seconds, then all 168 tests passed in 56 seconds, making it the cleanest measured source run in this group.
reviews.skip_if: Repositories with secrets or regulated data unless selection is reviewed first: the tool reads files and emits their contents, while `.gitignore` is not a security policy.

reviews.name: DeepSeek-Reasonix
reviews.verdict: Our 749-second test run ended with 25 of 26 Go packages passing, so Reasonix is buildable but not clean enough at commit b9cf32f for an unquestioned rollout.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone who expects rewind to undo arbitrary shell side effects: the checkpoint documentation says Bash changes, including `rm`, database writes, and deployments, are not tracked.

reviews.name: DeepTutor
reviews.verdict: Our DeepTutor run installed 200 packages and built successfully, but pytest collected 0 tests because configuration and a test dependency were missing, while pip-audit found 4 known vulnerabilities.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone who expects the checked-out test suite to pass after the documented dependency install: our run stopped on a missing `main.yaml` and missing `pytest_asyncio`.

reviews.name: agno
reviews.verdict: Our Agno quickstart installed 135 packages into 482 MB and pip-audit found 3 known vulnerabilities, so adopting it means accepting a real platform dependency, not adding a tiny agent helper.
reviews.skip_if: Developers who only need a small function-calling loop: Agno's runtime, control plane, storage, and 100-plus integrations add a much larger dependency and operating surface.

reviews.name: marketingskills
reviews.verdict: For any technical marketer, founder, or growth engineer already using an AI coding agent, this project is an absolute must-have.
reviews.skip_if: Non-technical marketers who are not comfortable with code editors or command-line interfaces.

reviews.name: Pake
reviews.verdict: Pake is a sharp choice for turning a web service into a small desktop convenience app, especially when the CLI's presets cover the job.
reviews.skip_if: Products that need deep native behavior rather than a webview: Pake's central job is wrapping a webpage, even though it adds menus, shortcuts, tray behavior, and injected styles.

reviews.name: claude-code-router
reviews.verdict: Our Claude Code Router install pulled 1,892 packages and 493 MB, then the release build stopped at 32 seconds for a missing `GH_TOKEN`, so this is a substantial control plane rather than a tiny proxy.
reviews.skip_if: Developers using one agent with one provider: the router adds a 1,892-package control plane, local gateway, UI, and another failure boundary.

reviews.name: academic-research-skills
reviews.verdict: Our install took 10 seconds and npm audit found 0 known vulnerabilities, but there was no build or test target for our sandbox to verify.
reviews.skip_if: Researchers who want an autonomous paper generator: the README says the human must choose the question, method, interpretation, and argument.

reviews.name: claude-howto
reviews.verdict: Our run installed 35 packages in 13 seconds, built in 5 seconds, and exposed no test target, so Claude How To is easy to inspect but cannot validate itself through the path our harness found.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone who needs every configuration detail to be authoritative without checking Anthropic's docs: open issue 176 identifies an inverted skill-precedence rule and a documented `skillOverrides` behavior that does not exist as described.

reviews.name: chatbox
reviews.verdict: Our Chatbox build finished in 108 seconds and 2,692 of 2,780 tests passed, but 2 context-related tests still failed, so the pinned source was close to green rather than green.
reviews.skip_if: Users who read local storage as fully offline privacy: prompts still leave the device whenever the configured model provider is remote.

reviews.name: free-claude-code
reviews.verdict: Our FCC install took 28 seconds and its build passed, but pytest stopped before collection because it did not recognize the configured `-n` argument.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone expecting free access to Anthropic's own models: FCC maps client tiers to compatible providers, and the README says outside providers control free availability and limits.

reviews.name: last30days-skill
reviews.verdict: Our Last30Days run installed 35 packages and built successfully, but its test step failed after 457 seconds on UID lookup errors in six keychain tests.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone expecting every advertised source to work without configuration: the README says only Reddit, Hacker News, Polymarket, GitHub, and StockTwits need no credentials.

reviews.name: xiaohongshu-mcp
reviews.verdict: Our xiaohongshu-mcp run installed 67 packages in 14 seconds and passed all 8 test packages, but that clean result cannot protect browser selectors from a Xiaohongshu page change.
reviews.skip_if: Unattended brand accounts that cannot tolerate UI breakage: issue 813 reports `search_feeds` timing out after about 60 seconds while the recommendation feed still worked.

reviews.name: FunASR
reviews.verdict: Our FunASR run installed 94 packages and built in 13 seconds, but pytest executed 0 tests because collection ended with a `SystemExit: 2` error.
reviews.skip_if: Buyers who want one checkpoint with one license and one hardware path: FunASR's model families have separate language coverage, dependencies, and weight licenses.

reviews.name: Vibe-Trading
reviews.verdict: Our Vibe-Trading run passed 11,133 of 11,134 tests, with the only failure caused by a missing passwd entry for container UID 1000.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone seeking investment advice or a profitable strategy in a box: the README calls this research software and says past performance does not guarantee future results.

reviews.name: claude-plugins-official
reviews.verdict: Our Discord-plugin install took 46 seconds for 130 packages, yet the directory offered no build or test target for that measured path.
reviews.skip_if: Users who interpret directory inclusion as a runtime guarantee: the README says Anthropic does not control bundled MCP servers, files, or software and cannot verify future behavior.

reviews.name: agents
reviews.verdict: Our PluginEval run installed 42 packages, passed 111 tests in 12 seconds, and reported 0 known vulnerabilities, giving this marketplace's evaluator a clean measured baseline.
reviews.skip_if: Users who want a small curated starter set: the README lists 93 plugins, 202 agents, 181 skills, and 105 commands, which creates a real selection and audit burden.

reviews.name: AstrBot
reviews.verdict: Our AstrBot install and build finished in 82 seconds total, and pip-audit found 0 known vulnerabilities, but tests never started because `pytest_asyncio` was missing.
reviews.skip_if: Operators who need WhatsApp today: the support table labels it `Coming Soon`, while the listed Matrix, Rocket.Chat, and VoceChat adapters are community maintained.

reviews.name: agentic-awesome-skills
reviews.verdict: Our sandbox installed 11 packages in 7 seconds but could not build because the Python validator lacked `yaml`, so Agentic Awesome Skills is easier to consume than to develop from a bare Node container.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone expecting the catalog to decide which skill is best: AAS Core deliberately does not rank candidates or certify semantic fit.

reviews.name: CowAgent
reviews.verdict: Our CowAgent run installed 98 packages in 48 seconds, but 77 tests failed and pip-audit found 35 known vulnerabilities, so this is a capable personal-agent stack that needs a guarded trial.
reviews.skip_if: Security-sensitive teams that cannot sandbox file, terminal, browser, and messaging access: an open group-channel report describes local files being sent to a chat, even though later releases added permission controls.

reviews.name: mempalace
reviews.verdict: MemPalace is a thoughtful fit for developers who want the original record kept locally and searchable across coding-agent sessions.
reviews.skip_if: Users who want automatic distilled facts instead of source text: the README says MemPalace stores verbatim content and does not summarize or paraphrase it.

reviews.name: awesome-claude-skills
reviews.verdict: Our run installed the bundled Slack GIF Creator in 28 seconds and built it in 12 seconds, but found no test target, so this repository is useful for discovery rather than blanket trust.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that need one audited, uniformly licensed package: entries come from many owners, while GitHub does not detect a repository-level license.

reviews.name: netdata
