reviews.verdict: Our measured Netdata subproject built in 17 seconds, but pytest collected 0 tests and pip-audit found 1 known vulnerability, so that run cannot support a clean bill of health for the monitoring agent.
reviews.skip_if: Buyers who assume our Python result tested the agent: the measured project was only `packaging/dag/`, not the Go and C monitoring daemon.

reviews.name: generative-ai-for-beginners
reviews.verdict: Our run installed 283 packages in 26 seconds with 0 known npm vulnerabilities, but no root build or test target existed, so the course's examples were not proven as one working system.
reviews.skip_if: Learners expecting a production application template: the README points advanced users to a separate code-sample collection.

reviews.name: Fabric
reviews.verdict: Our Fabric build took 126 seconds and 32 of 33 tested packages passed, but one package still ended the run in failure without a useful assertion in the supplied tail.
reviews.skip_if: Operators who might expose the REST server without `--api-key`: the API guide says unauthenticated mode accepts all requests and includes endpoints that read and update provider configuration.

reviews.name: context7
reviews.verdict: Our Context7 install and build finished in 38 seconds combined, but the 10-second test command still exited 1 in the SDK workspace.
reviews.skip_if: Organizations that require the entire documentation pipeline on their own infrastructure: the README says the API backend, parser, and crawler are private.

reviews.name: awesome-mcp-servers
reviews.verdict: Awesome MCP Servers is the definitive, indispensable catalog for the agentic AI revolution.
reviews.skip_if: Beginners looking for a single, all-in-one, installable AI agent.

reviews.name: gemini-cli
reviews.verdict: Our Gemini CLI run installed 1,325 packages and built successfully, but 10 of 7,000 tests failed before the suite hit 900 seconds and npm audit reported 71 vulnerabilities.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that require a clean dependency audit before evaluation: our npm audit reported 71 known vulnerabilities, including 5 critical and 22 high.

reviews.name: impeccable
reviews.verdict: Our Impeccable run installed 244 packages and built in 15 seconds, but the overall test script exited 1 with a final summary of 32 failures, so adopt the workflow only after reproducing its checks in your project.
reviews.skip_if: Teams without an AI coding harness: most of the value is delivered through an installed skill, agent commands, and edit hooks.

reviews.name: superpowers
reviews.verdict: Our Superpowers install added 0 packages in 12 seconds and npm audit found 0 known vulnerabilities, but there was no build or test target to verify.
reviews.skip_if: Developers who want immediate edits from a small request: the workflow can brainstorm, seek approval, create a plan, and set up a worktree first.

reviews.name: BrowserSkill
reviews.verdict: Our BrowserSkill install added 726 packages in 45 seconds, but no root build or test target was available, so the published binaries and extension deserve a separate trust review before they touch logged-in accounts.
reviews.skip_if: Security teams that will not let a local agent drive authenticated sites: the privacy policy says any process able to reach the local port could theoretically send extension commands, and issue 118 requests a shared-secret handshake.

reviews.name: openpilot
reviews.verdict: Our openpilot install took 42 seconds and its build passed in 14 seconds, but the sandbox could not test the 335-car hardware matrix.
reviews.skip_if: Drivers seeking an autonomous car: the safety document defines openpilot as Level 2 assistance and requires constant attention.

reviews.name: novu
reviews.verdict: Our Novu install pulled 5,192 packages and used 3,845 MB before a successful 334-second build, so self-hosting is a platform commitment rather than a small dependency.
reviews.skip_if: Teams sending through one provider and one channel: Novu adds a workflow platform where a direct provider SDK may be enough.

reviews.name: browser
reviews.verdict: Our run built Lightpanda's 122-package Rust subtree in 108 seconds, but Cargo found 0 tests and did not exercise the full Zig browser.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that need Chrome-level compatibility across arbitrary sites: the README calls Lightpanda beta, says crashes still occur, and lists CORS as unfinished.

reviews.name: pi-autoresearch
reviews.verdict: Our pi-autoresearch run installed 127 packages in 35 seconds and passed all 46 tests, making it a low-friction trial for existing pi users with a numeric target.
reviews.skip_if: Developers who do not use the pi coding agent: this is a pi extension and skill package, not a standalone optimizer.

reviews.name: remotion
reviews.verdict: Our Remotion checkout installed 3,978 packages and used 4,533 MB, then build and tests both failed because `bun` was missing.
reviews.skip_if: For-profit organizations with more than 3 employees that will not buy a company license: the free license excludes them.

reviews.name: kubernetes
reviews.verdict: Our Kubernetes build took 561 seconds, and 433 of 434 reported test results passed before the command hit our 900-second cap.
reviews.skip_if: A small team running a few services on one host: Kubernetes adds a control plane, worker-node components, networking, storage, and upgrade work that Compose or a simpler scheduler may avoid.

reviews.name: semaphore
reviews.verdict: Our Semaphore UI run built in 13 seconds, but 3 of 20 test packages failed, so pin the release and rehearse repository, database, and credential paths before moving real deployments into it.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that need every checkout method to behave identically: issue 4165 reports Azure DevOps HTTPS authentication working in Docker but failing in the package installation.

reviews.name: apify-mcp-server
reviews.verdict: Our Apify MCP Server run installed 788 packages, then passed its 23-second build and 43-second test step.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone needing a fully local or offline scraper: even the local stdio server sends requests and Actor inputs to the Apify API for execution.

reviews.name: skypilot
reviews.verdict: Our SkyPilot run installed 372 packages and consumed 1,672 MB, then its tests stopped in 10 seconds on a missing UID 1000 passwd entry and pip-audit found 13 known vulnerabilities.
reviews.skip_if: Native Windows users unwilling to use WSL: the installation documentation routes Windows through WSL.

reviews.name: go-whatsapp-web-multidevice
reviews.verdict: Our GOWA build passed in 111 seconds, while its 439-second test run ended with 12 of 13 packages passing and no failing package named in the supplied log tail.
reviews.skip_if: Businesses that require a supported messaging channel: the README says the project is unofficial and recommends the WhatsApp Business Platform for production-grade integration.

reviews.name: claude-squad
reviews.verdict: Our Claude Squad run installed 48 Go packages, built successfully, and passed all 6 tests in 91 seconds combined.
reviews.skip_if: Native Windows users: open issue 275 says the published v1.0.17 Windows binary cannot create a session because its PTY dependency is unsupported there.

reviews.name: multica
reviews.verdict: Our Multica run installed 2,014 packages, used 2,385 MB, and spent 539 seconds building and testing successfully, so this is serious team infrastructure rather than a lightweight agent launcher.
reviews.skip_if: Companies planning to offer Multica to outside users without a commercial agreement: its added license conditions restrict hosted and embedded third-party services.

reviews.name: crawlee
reviews.verdict: Our Crawlee build passed in 38 seconds, but its 374-second test run finished with 1,559 passed, 192 failed, and 38 skipped out of 1,801.
reviews.skip_if: Python-only teams: this repository is the Node.js implementation, while the README points to a separate Crawlee for Python project.

reviews.name: flink
reviews.verdict: Our PyFlink run installed 35 packages in 64 seconds and built in 8 seconds, but pytest hit 87 collection or setup errors before executing one test.
reviews.skip_if: Python developers expecting a small in-process data library: our PyFlink install pulled 35 packages, while the actual work runs on Flink's distributed engine.

reviews.name: mongo
reviews.verdict: Our MongoDB checkout installed 93 Node-tooling packages in 10 seconds, but exposed no build or test target, so our run says nothing about whether the 10,060,928-line C++ server compiles or passes its suites.
reviews.skip_if: Contributors looking for a small source build: the official build guide requires Bazel, a C++20 compiler, Python, native libraries, and substantial free disk.

reviews.name: openobserve
reviews.verdict: Our OpenObserve build exceeded 900 seconds, while all 304 cargo tests passed in 195 seconds, so the code looks testable but expensive to compile on a 3-CPU box.
reviews.skip_if: Organizations that cannot use AGPL-3.0 for a network service and do not want a commercial agreement.

reviews.name: cube
reviews.verdict: Our Cube Core install added 4,062 packages and 2,065 MB, then built in 16 seconds without exposing a root test target, so this is a substantial data service that needs its own correctness suite.
reviews.skip_if: Teams expecting dashboards in the open-source package: the README says Cube Core is headless and reserves workbooks, dashboards, and other finished BI surfaces for the commercial product.

reviews.name: stdlib
reviews.verdict: stdlib is the best fit for JavaScript teams that care about numerical breadth, typed APIs, and the option to install one exact function at a time.
reviews.skip_if: Applications that need only a few functions but plan to install the whole library: the README warns that the full project is likely unnecessary and causes slower installs.

reviews.name: dolt
reviews.verdict: Dolt earns a trial when data changes need the same review and merge habits developers use for source code.
reviews.skip_if: Applications that only need a conventional transactional database: Dolt commits are separate from SQL transaction commits, so version history adds another lifecycle to understand.

reviews.name: milvus
reviews.verdict: Our Milvus build finished in 11 seconds, but 72 of 85 Go test targets failed in the same sandbox, so adopting it means accepting a serious system with a demanding contributor path.
reviews.skip_if: Small applications that only need an embedded local index: the README directs that job to Milvus Lite, while the full repository measured 5,755 files and about 2,266,769 source lines.

reviews.name: seaweedfs
reviews.verdict: Our SeaweedFS build took 306 seconds, and after 900 seconds its test run showed 13 passing and 18 failing packages, with S3 tagging calls unable to reach a localhost service.
reviews.skip_if: Small teams wanting storage they can deploy and forget: our checkout had 3,935 files, installed 1,159 packages, and its tests ran for 900 seconds without finishing.

reviews.name: ccxt
reviews.verdict: Our CCXT install finished in 41 seconds with 498 packages, then both the build and test commands stopped on the same TypeScript error.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone looking for a finished trading bot, strategy engine, or backtesting product: the project describes CCXT as library software, not a hosted service or server.

reviews.name: webclaw
reviews.verdict: Our Webclaw run installed 384 packages, built in 171 seconds, and passed all 772 tests in 105 seconds, an unusually clean result for a web extraction project.
reviews.skip_if: Buyers expecting local JavaScript rendering or managed anti-bot access: the README assigns those jobs to the hosted API.

reviews.name: juicefs
reviews.verdict: Our JuiceFS checkout installed 550 npm packages in 36 seconds, but it exposed no build or test target and npm audit found 21 known vulnerabilities, so our run did not validate the Go file-system client.
reviews.skip_if: Teams wanting a single storage daemon: the README requires a JuiceFS client, a metadata engine, and an object store.

reviews.name: nautilus_trader
reviews.verdict: Our NautilusTrader source build and test steps each hit the 900-second limit while still compiling, so this is a serious codebase that needs stronger hardware and a deliberate evaluation window.
reviews.skip_if: Teams seeking dashboards, distributed orchestration, or built-in AI and ML tools: the roadmap explicitly puts those outside the open-source project's scope.

reviews.name: sherlock
reviews.verdict: Our Sherlock run installed 46 packages and built in 9 seconds, but only 22 of 25 pytest cases passed cleanly.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone treating a matching username as proof of identity: open false-positive reports name several major sites, and unrelated people often reuse handles.

reviews.name: cocoindex
reviews.verdict: Our CocoIndex build passed in 9 seconds, but its test run finished with 309 passed, 192 failed, 125 skipped, and 8 setup or collection errors, so adoption should begin with the exact connectors you will operate.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that require the full connector suite to pass in a plain isolated Python environment: our run ended with 192 failures and 8 collection or setup errors across database and storage connectors.

reviews.name: datafusion
reviews.verdict: Our DataFusion harness installed 35 Python packages in 16 seconds, but its build failed 4 seconds later and no tests ran, so that run does not establish a working Rust build.
reviews.skip_if: Python users expecting this repository to be the supported Python package: the README sends them to the separate `apache/datafusion-python` project.

reviews.name: wealthfolio
reviews.verdict: Our Wealthfolio run passed all 1,504 tests in 261 seconds, but the 37-second frontend build failed on missing UI declarations and a TypeScript type error.
reviews.skip_if: Users who want free automatic bank and brokerage aggregation: Wealthfolio Connect is an optional subscription, and issue 1570 still requests broader banking integration.

reviews.name: cli
reviews.verdict: Our Bright Data CLI run installed 88 packages in 14 seconds, then passed its build and tests, so trying the client is cheap even though using it ties the workflow to Bright Data's remote services.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that need a self-hosted crawler: the README describes a client for Bright Data's remote APIs, and authenticated commands require a Bright Data account and API key.

reviews.name: grafana
reviews.verdict: Our Grafana checkout consumed 2,610 MB, failed its build after 166 seconds, and never finished the test command within 900 seconds, so contributing from source requires the project's exact development workflow rather than generic monorepo commands.
reviews.skip_if: Contributors expecting a quick source build: our install used 2,610 MB, the build failed after 166 seconds, and tests hit the 900-second cap.

reviews.name: meilisearch
reviews.verdict: Our Meilisearch build succeeded in 551 seconds, but 887 of 993 tests failed in the following 703-second run, so this commit needs investigation before source-based deployment.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that need community-edition sharding or S3-streaming snapshots: the README places those in the Enterprise Edition, which is not allowed in production without a commercial agreement.

reviews.name: pocketbase
reviews.verdict: Our PocketBase build finished in 56 seconds, but 1 of 33 tested packages failed after a 394-second run, so the source is easy to compile while this exact checkout does not earn a clean test result.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring horizontal database scaling: the official FAQ says PocketBase scales only on a single server.

reviews.name: Avalonia
reviews.verdict: Our sandbox did not run Avalonia at commit 38402fc because C# was outside the harness and the repository had no Dockerfile.
reviews.skip_if: WPF owners expecting a drop-in open-source port: the README says Avalonia is not a 1:1 WPF copy, while XPF is a separate commercial product licensed per app and platform.

reviews.name: likec4
reviews.verdict: Our LikeC4 run passed a 148-second build and 71-second test step after installing 1,608 packages, so the project earns trust but demands real workspace capacity.
reviews.skip_if: Teams whose diagrams must be edited mainly by mouse: LikeC4 is a DSL, and Draw.io is an import or export format rather than the primary editor.

reviews.name: cli
reviews.verdict: Our `docker-trust` run installed 176 packages and built in 68 seconds, but its tests stopped with 3 of 7 packages failing to compile.
reviews.skip_if: Users looking for a container engine in one binary: this repository is the client, so most commands still need a reachable daemon.

reviews.name: googletest
reviews.verdict: Our GoogleTest install stopped after 7 seconds because CMake could not find Abseil, so commit 36ba75f is a poor blind clone-and-build choice in fresh Debian.
reviews.skip_if: Codebases stuck below C++17: the 1.18.x branch requires C++17, so upgrading the test framework can also force a compiler and language-standard change.

reviews.name: grpc
reviews.verdict: Our gRPC source install ran for 900 seconds without finishing, so adopting the protocol is far easier than becoming a contributor to this 632.7 MB repository.
reviews.skip_if: Small browser-first applications that only need ordinary JSON endpoints: the README routes WebJS users to the separate grpc-web project.

reviews.name: FreeCAD
reviews.verdict: Our 34-second Pivy install and 8-second build succeeded, but all 4 test modules stopped at setup because `pivy.coin` was missing.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that require browser-based simultaneous editing: the README documents desktop builds for Windows, macOS, and Linux, not a hosted collaborative editor.

reviews.name: flow
reviews.verdict: Our sandbox installed Flow's 126 Yarn packages in 20 seconds, but the checkout exposed no build or test target to run.
reviews.skip_if: Greenfield teams whose dependencies already publish TypeScript declarations: Flow's docs say most library definitions are not bundled and instead come from flow-typed.

reviews.name: ghostty
reviews.verdict: Our Ghostty install failed after 7 seconds because CMake could not find `zig`, so source development starts with matching the documented toolchain before any build or test can run.
reviews.skip_if: Windows users seeking a finished Ghostty desktop app: the README documents macOS and Linux applications, while Windows support is described for `libghostty-vt`.

reviews.name: insomnia
reviews.verdict: Our Insomnia run installed 1,750 packages, passed all 18 available tests, and still reported 39 known dependency vulnerabilities, so it is easy to try but costly to adopt casually as source.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that require a small source checkout and dependency tree: our install added 1,750 packages and occupied 989 MB before an application build.

reviews.name: awesome-react-native
reviews.verdict: We could not run commit 6733606 because this 28,684-byte README has no supported software ecosystem or Dockerfile, so Awesome React Native should be used as a reading list, never as tested tooling.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that need package-by-package compatibility data: the README links projects, while React Native Directory is the listed source with maintenance and New Architecture signals.

reviews.name: token-monitor
reviews.verdict: Our Token Monitor run installed 340 packages, passed all 3,674 tests, and still found 1 high-severity advisory, so it earns a trial with an audit review before wider deployment.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone who needs billing-grade totals: open issue 375 reports a 51.7% Claude shortfall when most transcripts lived outside the scanned roots.

reviews.name: archify
reviews.verdict: Our run installed Archify in 22 seconds, but 2 of 710 tests failed, so it is promising rather than friction-free.
reviews.skip_if: Teams wanting automatic runtime discovery with no agent analysis or authored input Buyers who require a fully green test suite before adoption People who only need a quick static flowchart and would find the verification workflow excessive Organizations that need…

reviews.name: cmux
reviews.verdict: Our cmux checkout installed 457 packages and used 510 MB, but it exposed no build or test target in the measured Bun project.
reviews.skip_if: Linux or Windows users: the FAQ says the desktop app is macOS only.

reviews.name: radare2
reviews.verdict: Our radare2 npm install ran for 415 seconds before a `wasm-pack` download timed out, so that packaging route is a poor first choice on restricted networks.
reviews.skip_if: Beginners expecting a guided graphical decompiler: the README teaches terse commands such as `aaa`, `afl`, and `pdf`, while the official Qt interface is a separate plugin.

reviews.name: lima
reviews.verdict: Our Lima build succeeded in 62 seconds, but 31 of 89 Go test packages failed in the same sandbox, so contributors should reproduce the suite before treating a checkout as ready.
reviews.skip_if: Developers who only want Docker on a Mac with minimal choices: Lima's own README points to Colima as the simpler container environment built on top of it.

reviews.name: gleam
reviews.verdict: Our Gleam build took 235 seconds and 12,129 of 12,137 tests passed, so the compiler is substantial and close to green in our sandbox, but contributors should reproduce the 8 failures before trusting a change.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that require a fully green upstream test run in a plain Rust container: our sandbox run ended with 8 failures out of 12,137 tests.

reviews.name: zoetrope
reviews.verdict: Our build took 30 seconds and all 380 tests passed in 13 seconds, making Zoetrope unusually easy to trust for a first release.
reviews.skip_if: Codex, OpenCode, or other agent users today: the README describes Claude Code's transcript layout, and Codex rollout support is still an open request.

reviews.name: graal
reviews.verdict: Our Graal checkout built its detected target in 7 seconds with 0 audit findings, but no test target was available, so the run is a tooling check rather than proof of a complete GraalVM build.
reviews.skip_if: Java developers who only want to try Native Image: the README points them to GraalVM downloads, while this repository is a 266 MB source checkout with about 3,515,494 lines.

reviews.name: intellij-community
reviews.verdict: Our 999.3 MB checkout contained 276,721 files, while the measured 12 passing tests covered only a small Go packer, so this repository demands more than its green lab result suggests.
reviews.skip_if: Developers who only want to use IntelliJ IDEA: the repository is a 999.3 MB source checkout, while JetBrains ships ready-made IDE downloads.

reviews.name: bazel
reviews.verdict: Our 220.3 MB Bazel checkout exposed no test target to the generic harness, and the 6-second step it built was not the main Java build system.
reviews.skip_if: Small single-language projects already served by their native build tool: Bazel adds WORKSPACE or module metadata, BUILD files, rules, and a separate query language.

reviews.name: kotlin
reviews.verdict: Our 19-second install succeeded with 24 npm packages, but there was no build or test target in the measured WASM browser workspace.
reviews.skip_if: Beginners looking for a small repository to learn compiler internals from Teams expecting the whole project to build from a single lightweight npm command Projects that need a tiny dependency footprint or quick source builds Organizations unwilling to manage multiple…

reviews.name: sentry
reviews.verdict: Our Sentry build succeeded in 93 seconds, but its test run passed the 900-second cap, so this is mature product infrastructure with a contributor loop sized for dedicated teams.
reviews.skip_if: Small teams that only need basic exception alerts: the repository is 226.8 MB with 20,540 files, and its product surface includes far more than crash reporting.

reviews.name: rust
reviews.verdict: Our harness installed 138 Yarn packages in 33 seconds but compiled no Rust code and ran no Rust tests, so it says nothing about rustc health.
reviews.skip_if: Developers who only want to write Rust applications: the README recommends the normal installation path and says source installation is not recommended.

reviews.name: skills-manager
reviews.verdict: Skills Manager is worth using once the same skill library has to serve several agents or computers.
reviews.skip_if: Developers who only use one agent and keep a few skills: a plain Git repository or symlink is easier to inspect and has fewer moving parts.

reviews.name: compound-engineering-plugin
reviews.verdict: Our test command ran for 455 seconds and reported 177 failures at commit 26bf5b1, so Compound Engineering should earn trust in a trial repository before its autonomous workflow receives permission to commit or push.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that require a green upstream test suite before adoption: our run ended with 177 failed tests at commit 26bf5b1.

reviews.name: gitoxide
reviews.verdict: Our gitoxide build completed in 204 seconds and all 10 available cargo tests passed in 13 seconds after a 406-package install.
reviews.skip_if: Shell scripts looking for a drop-in `git` replacement: the README says the `gix` and `ein` binaries may remain unstable and must not be relied on in scripts.

reviews.name: lavish-axi
reviews.verdict: Our Lavish AXI run installed 390 packages in 24 seconds and passed all 1,141 tests, making it an easy trial for developers who already review agent-made HTML.
reviews.skip_if: Firefox users who need dependable rendering today: open issue 201 reports a blank page, and an August 20 maintainer check says it remains unfixed on current main.

reviews.name: vorssaint-utils
reviews.verdict: Vorssaint is compelling if five or six of its modules match utilities you already keep running.
reviews.skip_if: Intel Mac owners or anyone staying on macOS 13 or earlier: the stated floor is Apple Silicon with macOS 14.

reviews.name: loop-engineering
reviews.verdict: Our Loop Engineering checkout installed 8 packages in 3 seconds but offered no root build or test target, so it is easiest to assess as a pattern library rather than one verified application.
reviews.skip_if: Developers seeking a hosted agent service that runs jobs for them: the repository supplies patterns and local CLIs, while scheduling and operation remain your responsibility.

reviews.name: jj
reviews.verdict: Our Jujutsu run installed 33 packages in 11 seconds and built in 1 second, but its tests were skipped because the harness found no test script or target.
reviews.skip_if: Repositories that depend on Git submodules: the README says support is incomplete, and issue #494 remains open with unresolved user-experience questions in the roadmap.

reviews.name: oxc
reviews.verdict: Our Oxc install took 31 seconds, but the build failed in 7 seconds and the test command failed in 5 seconds before running any tests, so the source checkout did not validate in a Node-only sandbox.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring complete ESLint plugin and configuration parity: issue 22117 says `--print-config` drops JavaScript-plugin rules, and issue 26115 reports incorrect disable-prefix handling.

reviews.name: tuios
reviews.verdict: Our TUIOS run built successfully and passed all 32 tests, but the test step took 248 seconds and does not cover every terminal protocol.
reviews.skip_if: Users who need daemon restarts to preserve live work: resurrection restores layout and fresh shells, not running programs, screen contents, or scrollback.

reviews.name: OpenLogi
reviews.verdict: Our OpenLogi build took 82 seconds, and cargo test exited successfully after 52 seconds while discovering 0 tests, so package readiness is ahead of independent behavioral coverage in that command.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone requiring stable configuration compatibility: the README says OpenLogi is under active development and its features and config may change.

reviews.name: moby
reviews.verdict: Our Moby build took 188 seconds, while tests hit the 900-second cap with 19 passing and 4 failing out of 23 recorded.
reviews.skip_if: Developers who only want to run containers: the README says Moby targets engine developers, while Docker products target end users.

reviews.name: kanata
reviews.verdict: Our Kanata build finished in 34 seconds, but 3 of 32 tests failed because their configuration files were not found.
reviews.skip_if: macOS users who need mouse buttons as input: the v1.12.0 release says macOS does not support mouse input, and the maintainer says they lack macOS hardware to validate concise instructions.

reviews.name: polkadot-sdk
reviews.verdict: Our 3-CPU sandbox spent 900 seconds on the build and another 900 seconds on tests without reaching either finish line, so Polkadot SDK is for teams that can fund serious Rust build infrastructure.
reviews.skip_if: Application teams that only need to deploy a contract: this repository contains 1,810,702 lines of source, while ink!

reviews.name: wails
reviews.verdict: Our Wails v2 build finished in 33 seconds, but 4 of 28 tested packages failed in the 25-second suite, so adopters should reproduce the full cross-platform matrix before shipping.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that need identical rendering across every desktop: Wails uses each operating system's native webview, so engines and installed runtimes differ.

reviews.name: sniffnet
reviews.verdict: Our Sniffnet build stopped after 249 seconds because the linker could not find `libpcap`, so source users should install the documented native capture packages before judging the Rust code.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone who needs to block traffic: firewall support is still an open feature request, while Sniffnet currently observes and flags connections.

reviews.name: harper
reviews.verdict: Our Harper install pulled 2,562 packages and used 1,629 MB, while the repository offered no root build or test target for us to verify.
reviews.skip_if: Multilingual writers: the README says Harper currently supports English only.

reviews.name: swc
reviews.verdict: Our SWC install finished in 53 seconds, but the build failed after 16 seconds and the test run hit 900 seconds while Cargo-backed plugin work remained, so contributing requires the full Rust and WebAssembly environment.
reviews.skip_if: Teams expecting a TypeScript type checker: SWC's migration guide says it only transpiles and recommends continuing to run `tsc` for type errors.

reviews.name: cloud-hypervisor
reviews.verdict: Our Cloud Hypervisor build took 176 seconds, and 295 of 323 tests passed before 28 io_uring-related failures ended the suite, so the code compiles but this checkout did not clear our test gate.
reviews.skip_if: Desktop users seeking a general emulator for old operating systems or hardware: the project supports 64-bit guests and intentionally minimizes legacy devices.

reviews.name: skills
reviews.verdict: Use this collection if you already trust coding agents with real repository work and want their process written down where you can inspect and change it.
reviews.skip_if: Teams expecting the repository itself to enforce quality: our run found no build or test target, and the instructions depend on the calling agent to follow them.

reviews.name: cypress
reviews.verdict: Our Cypress run consumed 3,249 MB and 525 seconds for installation, built in 211 seconds, then failed with 5 of 7 parsed Mocha tests failing after 106 seconds.
reviews.skip_if: Contributors seeking a light source checkout: our install took 525 seconds, pulled 4,291 packages, and used 3,249 MB.

reviews.name: bruno
reviews.verdict: Our Bruno source install took 97 seconds, pulled 3,430 packages, and left 1,956 MB on disk, so developers should use a packaged release unless they intend to contribute.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that require live cloud synchronization inside the client: the README says Bruno is offline-only and has no plans to add cloud sync.

reviews.name: cli
reviews.verdict: Our HTTPie CLI run passed 1,016 of 1,019 tests, but the same environment reported 16 known vulnerabilities, so convenience does not erase the need to review its installed dependency set.
reviews.skip_if: Security-sensitive environments that require a clean dependency audit: our source environment reported 16 known vulnerabilities.

reviews.name: promptfoo
reviews.verdict: Our Promptfoo checkout installed 2,415 packages and passed 23,460 tests, but its source build failed after 79 seconds, so it fits teams willing to own a large evaluation stack better than developers seeking a light dependency.
reviews.skip_if: Teams pinned to Node.js 20 or an earlier runtime: npm and npx use requires Node.js 22.22.0 or newer.

reviews.name: agentgateway
reviews.verdict: Our Agentgateway build took 362 seconds, then all 78 measured tests passed in 193 seconds, which is a credible result for a large gateway codebase.
reviews.skip_if: Teams with one application and one model key that do not need centralized policy: the gateway adds another network hop and configuration surface.

reviews.name: sglang
reviews.verdict: Our Rust-subproject run built in 178 seconds and passed all 580 tests, which makes SGLang credible for an experienced inference team despite its size.
reviews.skip_if: Developers who want a small local chat app: SGLang is an API-serving framework, and its documented quick start launches a model server rather than a user interface.

reviews.name: deepagents
reviews.verdict: Our Deep Agents install added 82 packages and built in 30 seconds combined, but pytest collected 0 tests and exited 4 on an unknown asyncio option.
reviews.skip_if: Applications that need a small deterministic tool-calling loop: the README directs those users to LangChain's lighter `create_agent` or a custom LangGraph graph.

reviews.name: claude-code-templates
reviews.verdict: Our Claude Code Templates install took 11 seconds and its configured tests returned success, but npm audit found 12 vulnerabilities and the test script runs no behavioral tests.
reviews.skip_if: Security-sensitive teams that cannot review community automation before it runs: issue 776 says a fork pull request can skip the SkillSpector enforcement gate after a comment step fails.

reviews.name: engram
reviews.verdict: Our Engram run built in 40 seconds, but 2 of 22 test results failed after a 476-second suite, including one plugin check that required `jq` and `curl`.
reviews.skip_if: Remote agents that require network MCP: the README says MCP is stdio-only, and the HTTP server binds to `127.0.0.1` without a bind-address option.

reviews.name: claude-code-system-prompts
reviews.verdict: This is the best kind of unofficial reference: current, granular, diffable, and honest in its repository guidance about not being the real source code.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone requiring official Anthropic documentation or source code: the repository is maintained by Piebald AI, and its own `CLAUDE.md` says Claude Code's source is not publicly available.

reviews.name: bifrost
reviews.verdict: Our Bifrost run installed 138 packages and built in 96 seconds, but 1 of 38 Go test packages failed after 330 seconds.
reviews.skip_if: Organizations expecting clustering, adaptive routing, advanced identity, guardrails, and other Enterprise features in the Apache-licensed edition: the README places them behind the Enterprise offering.

reviews.name: agent-skills
reviews.verdict: Our Agent Skills install added only 2 packages in 8 seconds and npm audit found 0 known vulnerabilities, but the repository exposed neither build nor test targets.
reviews.skip_if: Teams wanting a general-purpose skill catalog: the documented collection is concentrated on Vercel, React, React Native, web design, and writing.

reviews.name: awesome-free-llm-apis
reviews.verdict: Awesome Free LLM APIs is an excellent first stop and a poor final authority.
reviews.skip_if: Production teams that need guaranteed-current quotas: open August 2026 reports say GitHub Models was retired and SambaNova no longer offers free models, while both remain in the README.

reviews.name: cc-skills-golang
reviews.verdict: cc-skills-golang is a valuable accelerator for Go work because it packages specific, inspectable advice instead of promising model magic.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that expect an authoritative replacement for official Go guidance: an open issue identifies a nil-slice rule that contradicts Go's published review comments.

reviews.name: dspy
reviews.verdict: Our DSPy build finished in 10 seconds, yet 46 tests failed and 16 more hit collection or setup errors, so its ideas are easier to recommend than this exact checkout as a clean drop-in.
reviews.skip_if: Teams without examples or a meaningful metric: DSPy's optimizers need a way to judge candidate programs.

reviews.name: hindsight
reviews.verdict: Our Hindsight checkout consumed 1,704 MB for 2,141 npm packages, reported 23 audit findings, and offered no measured build or test target.
reviews.skip_if: Simple n8n-style workflows with little state: the README itself says Hindsight may be excessive for them.

reviews.name: agency-agents
reviews.verdict: Our Agency Agents run installed 35 packages and built in 17 seconds total, but it exposed no test target, so the collection is easy to install and hard to verify as a whole.
reviews.skip_if: Teams expecting the files to add tools, credentials, or domain knowledge by themselves: these are instructions consumed by a separate coding assistant.

reviews.name: prime-agent
reviews.verdict: Our Prime Agent test command ran for 567 seconds and exited 1 despite reporting 750 passed and 0 failed, while npm audit found 2 high and 2 moderate vulnerabilities.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone who needs the agent itself to be a security boundary: the README says generated Python and commands run with the user's permissions and explicitly says the worker and kernel are not a sandbox.

reviews.name: crewAI
reviews.verdict: Our CrewAI checkout installed 34 packages in 29 seconds, but its build and test steps both failed, so the quick application path is more convincing than the contributor path we measured.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that need every step to be deterministic: the README separates autonomous Crews from Flows because agent decisions and model output need explicit workflow boundaries.

reviews.name: dify
reviews.verdict: Our Dify install pulled 1,342 packages, used 1,408 MB, and exposed no root build or test target, so adoption starts with a large working surface and incomplete evidence from the default workspace command.
reviews.skip_if: Small teams seeking a light library: our checkout contained 13,460 files and about 2,126,431 source lines before 1,342 packages were installed.

reviews.name: llama_index
reviews.verdict: LlamaIndex is a strong first choice for a Python team whose main problem is connecting private data to models.
reviews.skip_if: Teams wanting a small, stable dependency surface: the project splits core from more than 300 integration packages, and provider combinations must be selected and pinned.

reviews.name: langchain
reviews.verdict: Our 79 MB LangChain core install finished in 21 seconds, but its configured test command stopped after 9 seconds on an unrecognized pytest argument, so adding it is easier than verifying its checkout.
reviews.skip_if: Small applications that call one stable model API and need little orchestration: the README's basic example wraps a single provider call, which is simpler to write with that provider's SDK.

reviews.name: stable-diffusion-webui
reviews.verdict: Stable Diffusion WebUI remains a capable workbench for people who know which models and settings they want.
reviews.skip_if: People who want a current Python install with few version constraints: the Windows guide still specifies Python 3.10.6 and says newer Python versions do not support its Torch path.

reviews.name: opencost
reviews.verdict: Our OpenCost run installed 458 packages, built successfully in 207 seconds, and passed all 54 measured Go tests, which makes the source a credible base for a Kubernetes cost service.
reviews.skip_if: Organizations without Kubernetes: the supported installation is an official Helm chart for Kubernetes 1.20 or newer, even if cloud-service costs are part of the desired view.

reviews.name: jumpserver
reviews.verdict: Our JumpServer run installed 34 packages in 55 seconds and built in 10 seconds, but the repository offered no test target, so the clean build is weaker evidence than a passing suite.
reviews.skip_if: Small teams that only need SSH keys or a VPN: the quick start asks for a clean 64-bit Linux server with at least 4 CPU cores and 8 GB of RAM.

reviews.name: macos
reviews.verdict: Our sandbox did not run dockur/macos because its Shell-based Docker workflow falls outside our supported harness, so there is no install or test result to lean on.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone planning to run macOS on ordinary PC or cloud hardware: the README says Apple's license permits this setup only on Apple hardware.

reviews.name: erpnext
reviews.verdict: Our ERPNext checkout installed 470 packages in 103 seconds, then its build failed in 5 seconds because `/sites/common_site_config.json` was missing.
reviews.skip_if: A small team seeking a single-container accounting app: the README routes self-hosting through a separate Frappe Docker project, and manual development starts with Bench plus a new site.

reviews.name: Sunshine
reviews.verdict: Our Sunshine build completed in 10 seconds and npm audit found 0 known vulnerabilities, while the current release spans 4 host operating systems and several hardware encoders.
reviews.skip_if: Buyers choosing hardware solely from the compatibility tables: the README warns that its requirement tables are a work in progress and says not to purchase hardware from them.

reviews.name: odoo
reviews.verdict: Our Odoo install took 196 seconds, pulled 95 packages, and produced a successful build, but the 1,103.7 MB checkout makes clear that this is a business platform, not a lightweight app.
reviews.skip_if: Small teams wanting one narrow app with little operational weight: our checkout occupied 1,103.7 MB and contained 48,042 files.

reviews.name: onyx
reviews.verdict: Our Onyx workspace install pulled 451 packages and occupied 688 MB before any database, index, model, or connector was running, so Standard Onyx is an infrastructure commitment.
reviews.skip_if: Small teams that only need a local chat screen: Standard Onyx adds vector and keyword indexes, background workers, model inference, Redis, and MinIO.

reviews.name: evcc
reviews.verdict: Our evcc Node setup installed 682 packages and used 469 MB, but no build or test target ran and npm audit found 2 high plus 2 moderate vulnerabilities.
reviews.skip_if: Buyers whose exact hardware combination is absent from the device documentation, even if the same brand appears elsewhere in the long support list.

reviews.name: signal-cli-rest-api
reviews.verdict: Use signal-cli-rest-api when you specifically need a self-hosted HTTP boundary around Signal and accept responsibility for the account, keys, receiving loop, and network security.
reviews.skip_if: People seeking an official Signal business API, because this is a community wrapper around signal-cli Anyone unwilling to operate a stateful service containing account keys and registration data Teams that expect authentication, public-internet hardening, and managed delivery guarantees out of…

reviews.name: optimism
reviews.verdict: Our Optimism checkout installed 464 Go packages and built in 9 seconds, but 3 of 146 Go test packages failed, so source users should validate the exact released components they plan to run.
reviews.skip_if: Application developers who only want to deploy a contract on OP Mainnet: the README directs that audience to the public Optimism documentation rather than this monorepo.

reviews.name: dynamo
reviews.verdict: Our Dynamo run installed 35 packages and built in 37 seconds combined, but pytest stopped after 6 seconds because its configured `pydantic` warning module could not be imported.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone serving one model on one GPU: the README says the inference engine alone is probably sufficient.

reviews.name: warpgate
reviews.verdict: Our Warpgate checkout installed 27 frontend packages with 0 npm advisories, but it exposed no npm build or test target and our run never compiled the Rust service.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring a documented, proven active-active design: issue #2488 asks what node-local state must be shared after target-specific failures behind an AWS load balancer.

reviews.name: gateway
reviews.verdict: Our Envoy Gateway run built in 215 seconds, but 5 of 58 Go test results failed, so commit d32f282 did not clear a fresh-container contributor check.
reviews.skip_if: Small deployments that only need a simple reverse proxy: the controller, CRDs, Envoy data plane, and policy model add operating work.

reviews.name: tg-ws-proxy
reviews.verdict: Our TG WS Proxy run installed in 29 seconds and passed its build and tests, but pip-audit found 34 known vulnerabilities.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone needing a full VPN: the proxy handles Telegram MTProto traffic and does not change other applications.

reviews.name: lago
reviews.verdict: Our Lago events-processor build passed in 74 seconds, but 2 of 6 test packages failed because the linker could not find `expression_go`.
reviews.skip_if: Small products that only need one fixed Stripe subscription: Lago adds a billing platform and several services to operate.

reviews.name: zitadel
reviews.verdict: Our ZITADEL checkout installed 2,123 pnpm packages and consumed 1,873 MB, but it exposed no root build or test target, so our run cannot certify the Go server.
reviews.skip_if: Small applications that only need social login and a user table: ZITADEL's 9,927-file repository and multi-tenant model add a platform where a library may suffice.

reviews.name: talos
reviews.verdict: Our Talos checkout built in 255 seconds after a 673-second, 1,610-package dependency step, but 3 of 173 test-package results failed.
reviews.skip_if: Administrators whose incident process depends on SSH, a package manager, or ad hoc host changes: Talos intentionally removes those interfaces.

reviews.name: velero
reviews.verdict: Our Velero build took 233 seconds and its test run ended with 59 of 65 passing, so adoption should begin with a restore drill rather than a successful install.
reviews.skip_if: Teams seeking a database-consistent backup without application hooks or database-native dumps: Velero captures Kubernetes objects and configured volume data, while workload consistency remains an application concern.

reviews.name: arcane
reviews.verdict: Our Arcane install pulled 480 packages and occupied 1,352 MB, but the root workspace offered no build or test target for us to verify.
reviews.skip_if: Operators unwilling to give a web application powerful Docker access: the documented installation mounts the Docker socket, which can control the host.

reviews.name: omniget
reviews.verdict: Our OmniGet run installed 367 packages, passed its build and tests, and still reported 9 dependency vulnerabilities, so it is easy to try but needs security review before managed deployment.
reviews.skip_if: Organizations that cannot accept unsigned desktop binaries: the README says macOS needs manual quarantine removal and ad hoc signing, while Windows may show SmartScreen.

reviews.name: WeKnora
reviews.verdict: Our WeKnora build passed after 252 seconds, but the test run ended with 4 failures out of 77, so v0.7.2 needs an environment-specific acceptance run before production.
reviews.skip_if: Teams planning to expose the default deployment directly to the internet: the security notice recommends an internal or private network.

reviews.name: hysteria
reviews.verdict: Our Hysteria checkout installed 33 packages in 15 seconds and built in 7 seconds, but the harness found no test target, so the clean build is the only code-level check we completed.
reviews.skip_if: Networks that block or heavily throttle UDP: Hysteria transports traffic over QUIC, so a TCP-only path defeats its core design.

reviews.name: openclaw
reviews.verdict: Our OpenClaw build took 545 seconds, and 16,128 of 16,165 tests passed before the suite hit our 900-second cap.
reviews.skip_if: Teams seeking adversarial multi-user isolation: the security policy says one shared Gateway is not a multi-tenant boundary and recommends separate hosts or OS users.

reviews.name: UpSnap
reviews.verdict: Our UpSnap run installed 85 packages, built in 49 seconds, and passed its single discovered test, making it an easy trial for a trusted LAN.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone planning to publish the dashboard directly to the internet: the README warns against this because shutdown actions can pass custom commands to a shell, potentially as root.

reviews.name: authentik
reviews.verdict: Our authentik workspace install pulled 1,602 packages and used 528 MB, while the root exposed no build or test target for the harness, so this is an infrastructure product rather than a casual source install.
reviews.skip_if: Small installations that only need password protection for one web app: authentik's flows, providers, sources, outposts, workers, and database add real operating work.

reviews.name: vaultwarden
reviews.verdict: Our Vaultwarden install took 52 seconds, but its plain build and test commands both stopped because no database backend was enabled.
reviews.skip_if: Organizations that require official Bitwarden support or a vendor contract: Vaultwarden is independent, and its maintainers tell users not to contact Bitwarden support for its bugs.

reviews.name: outline
reviews.verdict: Our Outline build finished in 38 seconds, but 2,287 of 4,925 tests failed in the same fresh container, so source contributors should reproduce the project's full test environment before trusting a local green build.
reviews.skip_if: Organizations that require an OSI-approved permissive license: Outline uses Business Source License 1.1, not MIT or Apache 2.0.

reviews.name: actual
reviews.verdict: Our Actual Budget checkout installed 2,608 packages and used 1,678 MB, then its all-platform build failed at missing `xcodebuild` and its test command ended with recorded timeouts, so contributors should expect a large multi-platform codebase rather than a tiny budget…
reviews.skip_if: Anyone who expects bank connections to work without provider setup: the current issue and pull request activity includes missing GoCardless server credentials and EU account-listing failures.

reviews.name: twenty
reviews.verdict: Our Twenty install took 445 seconds, pulled 5,270 packages, and used 4,822 MB, while the repository exposed no build or test target to our harness.
reviews.skip_if: Small teams wanting a low-maintenance contact list: our install pulled 5,270 packages and used 4,822 MB before any CRM data existed.

reviews.name: photoprism
reviews.verdict: Our frontend install pulled 1,070 packages and used 660 MB, while npm audit found 1 high-severity advisory and the workspace exposed no build or test target.
reviews.skip_if: People wanting automatic phone backup as a complete first-party mobile experience: the README points to compatible apps such as PhotoSync for background iOS and Android uploads.

reviews.name: jellyfin
reviews.verdict: Jellyfin is the definitive choice for building a personal media server if you believe in the principles of free and open-source software.
reviews.skip_if: Users seeking a simple, one-click appliance with zero technical overhead.

reviews.name: gods-eye-view
reviews.verdict: Our build succeeded in 27 seconds, and the full test command succeeded in 118 seconds.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone needing verified intelligence decisions, because attractive visualization does not validate a source Teams seeking a supported, versioned production product, because there are no listed releases Nontechnical users expecting a one-click installer, because setup still requires Node.js, npm, and a…

reviews.name: open-slide
reviews.verdict: Our Open Slide run installed 897 packages, built in 39 seconds, and passed all 313 Vitest tests, making it the easiest of these agent-led tools to trust for a real trial.
reviews.skip_if: Designers who need arbitrary page sizes or portrait social decks: the canvas is fixed at 1920 by 1080, and issue 404 requests configurable ratios.

reviews.name: chromium
reviews.verdict: Our Chromium evaluation stopped at the clone step, leaving 0 install, build, and test results to report.
reviews.skip_if: Developers expecting `git clone` followed by a normal package build: the README explicitly says not to clone the GitHub mirror and requires `depot_tools`.

reviews.name: excalidraw
reviews.verdict: Our Excalidraw checkout could not finish its 40-second install because Yarn ran under Node 18.20.8 and `marked@16.4.2` required Node 20 or newer, so source contributors should verify the runtime before judging the code.
reviews.skip_if: Non-React applications seeking a framework-neutral widget: the quick start requires React and React DOM.

reviews.name: penpot
reviews.verdict: Our Penpot checkout installed 144 pnpm packages in 12 seconds, but it exposed no repository-level build or test target, so that clean install is weak evidence for operating the full platform.
reviews.skip_if: Small teams that only want a sketchpad: the official production path brings a backend, exporter, PostgreSQL, Valkey, asset storage, and proxy configuration.

reviews.name: astryx
reviews.verdict: Astryx is unusually complete for a beta and deserves a trial if you are starting a React 19 product or replacing an internal design-system sprawl.
reviews.skip_if: React 18 or older applications: the core package requires React 19 or later.

reviews.name: tauri
reviews.verdict: Our Tauri checkout built in 450 seconds, then its only CLI template test failed after 32 seconds, so adopting the framework is easier than contributing to this large monorepo.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that need identical browser behavior on every machine: Tauri uses WKWebView, WebView2, WebKitGTK, and Android System WebView rather than one bundled engine.

reviews.name: bun
reviews.verdict: Our install of Bun's 194.8 MB source checkout failed in 9 seconds before any build or test result, so contributors should expect a native runtime project rather than the one-command release experience.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring exact Node.js behavior without a compatibility test phase: issue 40535 shows Bun 1.4.0 returning a relative path where Node v24.15.0 returns an absolute path for one `node:fs` case.

reviews.name: Graft
reviews.verdict: Our Graft run installed 86 packages, passed all 938 tests, and reported 0 known vulnerabilities, making it an unusually low-friction trial for teams whose coding agents keep rediscovering the same code.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that cannot send source-derived content to an outside model provider: the structural graph stays local, but `graft build --deep` sends files through the provider and model you configure.

reviews.name: AutoResearchClaw
reviews.verdict: Our AutoResearchClaw checkout installed 156 packages, used 911 MB, and passed 2,951 tests, so the repository is much more than a paper-generation prompt.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone expecting a submitted paper from one prompt without expert review: the README labels the project as seeking testers, and the pipeline generates code, claims, and experiments that still need scientific scrutiny.

reviews.name: dsh-desktop
reviews.verdict: Our dsh-desktop run built in 22 seconds and passed 790 of 796 tests, with 1 lifecycle test timing out at 5,000 ms.
reviews.skip_if: Linux desktop users seeking an official installer today: the README lists Windows x64 and macOS Universal packages, while Linux packaging appears in an open pull request.

reviews.name: opensre
reviews.verdict: Our OpenSRE run installed 201 packages and passed 15,768 tests, but 23 failures kept the suite red after 823 seconds, so this is a serious evaluation target rather than a safe default for production response.
reviews.skip_if: Small teams wanting a light diagnostic script: our install added 201 packages and occupied 863 MB before any external service was connected.

reviews.name: Speech
reviews.verdict: Our build succeeded in 9 seconds, but the tests were still at 17% when the 900-second cap ended, with nine export-related failures visible.
reviews.skip_if: Small teams wanting a lightweight speech API with minimal local infrastructure CPU-only teams planning to train models, because an NVIDIA GPU and CUDA are required for training Beginners expecting a quick pip install and a short, fully passing test suite…

reviews.name: oh-story-claudecode
reviews.verdict: Use it if you write Chinese web fiction and already live in Claude Code, Codex, or a similar file-aware agent: the workflow is unusually specific, actively maintained, and more disciplined than a folder of prompts.
reviews.skip_if: Writers who want an English-first interface and examples, because the primary documentation and workflow vocabulary are Chinese Anyone expecting a polished desktop writing app with no terminal or agent configuration Authors who want autonomous publication, because this is a writing…

reviews.name: VoiceStudio
reviews.verdict: VoiceStudio is a convincing choice for a technically comfortable creator who wants several private speech workflows in one local app.
reviews.skip_if: Intel Mac owners who need the backend on the same computer: the macOS guide says current PyTorch wheels do not support that path, so they must use a remote backend.

reviews.name: kagent
reviews.verdict: Our Kagent run built successfully, but 7 of 73 tests failed after a 162-second test step.
reviews.skip_if: Multi-tenant operators who need enforced per-user permissions today: open issue #1270 says the API, UI, and CLI lack user authorization and that all users can access resources across namespaces.

reviews.name: dashi-ppt-skill
reviews.verdict: Our Dashi PPT install took 18 seconds, but the project supplied no build target and no test target, so the lab could not verify rendering or export.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone needing a corporate PowerPoint master imported automatically: issue 14 requests that capability, and the README only documents built-in themes.

reviews.name: strix
reviews.verdict: Our Strix run passed 390 tests but failed 200 before pytest stopped, and pip-audit reported 3 known vulnerabilities.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that cannot isolate an offensive tool: Strix runs shell commands, intercepts HTTP traffic, writes exploit code, and actively attacks the target you give it.

reviews.name: modlens
reviews.verdict: Our modlens run installed 120 packages, built in 5 seconds, and passed 818 of 823 tests with 5 skipped, so its repository mechanics are unusually easy to verify.
reviews.skip_if: Security teams that require an OS sandbox around untrusted images: the security guide says subprocess isolation reduces exposure but is not a security boundary.

reviews.name: Soup
reviews.verdict: Our Soup install used 5,370 MB and its test suite reached only 31% before a 900-second timeout, so contributors should budget for a large environment and a long verification loop.
reviews.skip_if: Python 3.13 or newer environments: the README supports only Python 3.10 through 3.12 because that PyTorch stack has not been validated.

reviews.name: upscayl
reviews.verdict: Our Upscayl install consumed 1,418 MB and npm audit found 44 known vulnerabilities, even though its 51-second build succeeded.
reviews.skip_if: CPU-only machines and most integrated GPUs: the README says Upscayl needs Vulkan and will not work on most CPUs or iGPUs.

reviews.name: MoneyPrinterTurbo
reviews.verdict: MoneyPrinterTurbo covers an impressive amount of the short-video pipeline and passed our install, build, and test steps.
reviews.skip_if: Security-sensitive deployments that need a clean dependency audit: our pip audit found 28 known vulnerabilities.

reviews.name: gstack
reviews.verdict: Our gstack run installed 234 packages and built in 7 seconds, then the 264-second test step failed across 3 shards.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring a green upstream suite before adoption: our run ended with failing shards, including 41 failures in one shard and 35 in another.

reviews.name: InsForge
reviews.verdict: Our InsForge run installed 2,284 packages and used 752 MB, then passed its build and tests in 177 seconds combined while npm audit reported 5 vulnerabilities.
reviews.skip_if: Operators seeking a small single-binary backend: the deployment guide requires 4 services and recommends 4 GB or more of RAM.

reviews.name: index-tts
reviews.verdict: Our IndexTTS environment consumed 8,413 MB and pip-audit found 32 known vulnerabilities, even though the 9-second build and 52-second tests passed.
reviews.skip_if: Small CPU-only deployments: the README centers CUDA 12.8 or newer, GPU diagnostics, BF16 or FP16, and optional DeepSpeed.

reviews.name: ppt-master
reviews.verdict: PPT Master is one of the more serious open workflows for generating a deck that remains genuinely editable in PowerPoint.
reviews.skip_if: People expecting a one-click perfect deck: the README says final polishing remains the user's job and quality depends heavily on the chosen model.

reviews.name: openpencil
reviews.verdict: Our OpenPencil build took 448 seconds and all 547 tests passed, making commit 9c81077 a credible engineering base for teams willing to test prerelease desktop behavior themselves.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring a stable release channel: GitHub's newest downloadable build, v0.8.4, is marked prerelease.

reviews.name: baoyu-skills
reviews.verdict: Our Baoyu Skills run passed 234 of 236 tests and reported 7 high-severity dependency findings, so it is useful publishing automation that still needs an install review.
reviews.skip_if: Users who want one small plugin: the README warns that installing all 20-plus skills adds context overhead.

reviews.name: gbrain
reviews.verdict: Our GBrain run built in 7 seconds and Bun counted 7,152 passing tests, but the full command still exited 1 after 869 seconds, so this commit did not clear its test gate.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone wanting a small personal-notes utility: our checkout had about 812,029 source lines, and the installed project occupied 237 MB.

reviews.name: kandev
reviews.verdict: Our Kandev install took 48 seconds and 978 MB, but the build failed after 7 seconds because the desktop Tauri step could not run `cargo metadata`; no tests ran.
reviews.skip_if: Developers who only run one agent in one terminal: Kandev adds a server, database, board, workflow model, worktrees, and another interface to maintain.

reviews.name: dyad
reviews.verdict: Our Dyad run built in 143 seconds, but 9 of 6,350 tests failed and npm audit found 80 vulnerabilities, so this is a promising local builder with concrete maintenance work attached.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring every shipped feature under Apache-2.0: code in `src/pro` uses the Functional Source License 1.1, while the rest uses Apache-2.0.

reviews.name: ai-website-cloner-template
reviews.verdict: Our copy installed 886 packages and built in 17 seconds, but it had no test target, so AI Website Cloner Template is a credible starting workflow rather than verified cloning software.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone copying a site without permission: the README excludes phishing, impersonation, passing off another design, and reproduction that violates site terms.

reviews.name: daily_stock_analysis
reviews.verdict: Our Daily Stock Analysis run installed 35 packages and built successfully, but its tests stopped after 8 seconds because `anyio` was missing, so commit e45d5ce is not ready for unattended use from the documented dependency set.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone seeking regulated financial advice or an autonomous trading system: the README says the output is for learning and research and does not constitute investment advice.

reviews.name: skills
reviews.verdict: If your organization lives and breathes Google Cloud, `google/skills` is an essential toolkit for building the next generation of infrastructure automation.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone working primarily with AWS, Azure, or other cloud providers, as the skills are entirely GCP-specific.

reviews.name: qwen-code
reviews.verdict: Our Qwen Code run installed 1,937 packages in 348 seconds, used 1,475 MB, and built successfully, but tests were still running at the 900-second cap and npm audit found 9 known vulnerabilities.
reviews.skip_if: Small environments where a large dependency tree is unacceptable: our install added 1,937 packages and occupied 1,475 MB.

reviews.name: agentmemory
reviews.verdict: Our agentmemory run passed build and tests, but its 299-package install used 1,235 MB and npm audit reported 14 known vulnerabilities, including 6 high-severity findings.
reviews.skip_if: Users who cannot allow coding-session data into a persistent local store: hooks can capture prompts, tool use, summaries, and project paths.

reviews.name: lumen
reviews.verdict: Our Lumen build took 305 seconds and 134 of 135 tests passed, with one merge-base test unable to find `refs/heads/main`.
reviews.skip_if: Reviewers who cannot risk losing draft comments: annotations currently live only in memory, and open issue 135 requests persistence across exits.

reviews.name: zcf
reviews.verdict: Our ZCF run installed 899 packages in 27 seconds, then passed its 13-second build and 50-second test command, so the code is easy to verify but the resulting 319 MB toolchain is not truly zero configuration.
reviews.skip_if: Developers who want to keep agent configuration hand-audited and minimal: full initialization can install tools, import workflows, write provider settings, and configure MCP in one pass.

reviews.name: aichat
reviews.verdict: Our AIChat run installed 425 packages and passed all 21 tests after a 152-second build, so the checked-out Rust client is easy to trust for a personal trial.
reviews.skip_if: Users who want a frequently tagged release cadence: the latest release is from July 2025, the last push was February 2026, and issue 1517 asks whether the project is being sunset.

reviews.name: CodeWhale
reviews.verdict: Our CodeWhale install took 13 seconds and found 0 known npm vulnerabilities, but the package offered no build or test target, so the easy install is stronger evidence than the local verification story.
reviews.skip_if: Security teams that require an OS sandbox on every supported platform: the README describes OS sandboxing as optional and available only where supported.

reviews.name: PageIndex
reviews.verdict: Our PageIndex run passed 345 tests with 0 failures in 181 seconds, while 50 tests were skipped and pip-audit found 1 vulnerability.
reviews.skip_if: Local-only users processing scans or image-heavy PDFs: the README reserves OCR and image understanding for PageIndex Cloud.

reviews.name: mem0
reviews.verdict: Our Mem0 run installed 62 packages in 30 seconds and built in 7 seconds, but the suite ended with 36 failures and 117 collection or setup errors, so adoption should begin with backend-specific tests.
reviews.skip_if: Developers expecting an offline library with no model services: the README says Mem0 needs an LLM, defaults to OpenAI models, and uses an embedding model too.

reviews.name: firecrawl
reviews.verdict: Our Firecrawl build failed in 9 seconds on an unresolved Rust-backed module, and 183 of 2,166 tests failed, so self-hosters should treat adoption as a platform project.
reviews.skip_if: Developers expecting a small local scraper: the self-host stack runs an API, workers, Playwright, Redis, RabbitMQ, and PostgreSQL.

reviews.name: NextChat
reviews.verdict: NextChat is a good fit for a personal or small-team model console when browser-local storage, provider choice, and quick deployment matter.
reviews.skip_if: Organizations that need real identity, roles, and audit controls in the open-source edition: the documented `CODE` setting is a shared page password, while the README reserves administration and security auditing for an enterprise product.

reviews.name: ponytail
reviews.verdict: Ponytail is a sharp corrective for agents that turn a date input into a component project.
reviews.skip_if: Teams whose main risk is under-engineering: an always-on minimalism instruction can pressure an agent away from useful structure even though the rules exempt security, validation, and accessibility.

reviews.name: caveman
reviews.verdict: Our Caveman run installed 399 packages, passed all 167 tests in 33 seconds, and found 0 known vulnerabilities, but the install still used 961 MB and offered no build target.
reviews.skip_if: Users who assume fewer output tokens always cut total cost: the README says the skill adds input tokens and can go net-negative on already-terse work.

reviews.name: osaurus
reviews.verdict: Our sandbox passed 1 of 1 tests for the Go helper in 31 seconds, but it did not build the 848,110-line Swift-centered Mac application that users actually install.
reviews.skip_if: Windows, Linux, or Intel Mac users: the application requires Apple Silicon and macOS 15.5 or later.

reviews.name: mcp
reviews.verdict: Our run built the 71 MB repository's Docusaurus site in 59 seconds, but it ran no server tests and npm audit found 31 advisories, so that pass says nothing about the operational safety of each MCP package.
reviews.skip_if: Teams choosing a new production agent platform: the README explicitly recommends Agent Toolkit for AWS and says useful projects will move there over time.

reviews.name: QuantDinger
reviews.verdict: Our QuantDinger run passed 1,415 pytest cases after a 69-second, 159-package install, yet open precision and lot-size reports touch the credibility of backtests.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone seeking investment advice or a profitable black box: the README rejects that framing and leaves strategy and risk decisions with the operator.

reviews.name: mcp-use
reviews.verdict: Our mcp-use Python build succeeded and pip-audit found 0 known vulnerabilities, but only 159 of 337 pytest cases passed while 135 failed and 43 hit errors, so adopt it behind your own tool-level integration tests.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that only need protocol primitives and want the smallest abstraction: the official TypeScript and Python MCP SDKs have a narrower job.

reviews.name: ida-pro-mcp
reviews.verdict: Our IDA Pro MCP run installed 35 packages in 22 seconds and built in 8 seconds, but pytest ended with 29 collection or setup errors after 136 tests passed.
reviews.skip_if: IDA Free users: the README requires IDA Pro 8.3 or newer and says the free edition is unsupported.

reviews.name: nginx-ui
reviews.verdict: Our nginx-ui source install failed in 6 seconds before any build or test could run, so use a pinned release binary or image for evaluation and treat source reproducibility as unresolved.
reviews.skip_if: Developers who need the source checkout to install cleanly with npm: our run stopped on an invalid `@uozi-admin/curd@4.19.5>xlsx` tag.

reviews.name: XHS-Downloader
reviews.verdict: Our XHS-Downloader run installed 106 packages in 81 seconds and built in 9 seconds, but it offered no test target, so the code is easy to try and hard to independently regression-check.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone needing a stable official RedNote API: open issues report downloads breaking after site changes, including issue 441 for video extraction and issue 423 for the userscript.

reviews.name: OpenMetadata
reviews.verdict: Our root run installed 110 packages in 18 seconds but `yarn test` failed in 4 seconds because no test is specified, while the real Docker quickstart requires 6 GiB and 4 vCPUs.
reviews.skip_if: Small teams wanting a lightweight catalog on a modest laptop: the Docker quickstart requires at least 6 GiB of memory and 4 vCPUs.

reviews.name: Skill_Seekers
reviews.verdict: Our Skill Seekers run passed 4,058 tests, but 14 failed and 16 more hit setup or collection errors after an 837-second test run, so generated assets deserve inspection before agent installation.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone expecting a deterministic documentation converter: optional AI enhancement writes skill material, and issue 453 reports a unified build that dropped PDF content and produced ungrounded filler.

reviews.name: trigger.dev
reviews.verdict: Our Trigger.dev checkout installed 2,536 packages and occupied 1,984 MB, then both build and test commands stopped at the database package, so this is a platform commitment rather than a small job runner.
reviews.skip_if: Teams needing a tiny self-hosted queue: the Docker guide includes a web app, worker, PostgreSQL, Redis, a registry, object storage, secrets, and worker authentication.

reviews.name: mcp-for-beginners
reviews.verdict: Our `05-AdvancedTopics` run installed 64 packages and built in 8 seconds, but it exposed no test target, so the measured code path has no suite result.
reviews.skip_if: Learners wanting one short, linear tutorial: the repository has modules 00 through 12, many sub-lessons, 50-plus translations, and several language stacks.

reviews.name: nuclear
reviews.verdict: Our Nuclear build completed 8 of 9 tasks, then failed after 67 seconds because `cargo metadata` was unavailable, while all 5 Vitest tests passed.
reviews.skip_if: Phone and tablet listeners: the download table provides Windows, macOS, and Linux builds, with no mobile package documented.

reviews.name: context-mode
reviews.verdict: Our context-mode run installed 201 packages and built in 64 seconds combined, but its test suite was still running when our 900-second cap ended.
reviews.skip_if: Security-sensitive teams before issue 1075 is resolved: the report says some absolute permission patterns never match, causing explicit denies to fail open.

reviews.name: MaxKB
reviews.verdict: Our MaxKB install pulled 224 packages, occupied 1,794 MB, and returned 7 known vulnerability findings, while the repository exposed no test target.
reviews.skip_if: Small servers or ephemeral review environments: our install added 224 packages and consumed 1,794 MB before model files or user documents.

reviews.name: mastra
reviews.verdict: Our Mastra test command was still running when it hit 900 seconds, after a successful 645-second build, so adopting the full monorepo requires serious CI time.
reviews.skip_if: Python-first AI teams: Mastra's primary API, examples, tooling, and framework integrations are TypeScript-centric.

reviews.name: page-agent
reviews.verdict: Our Page Agent build and tests passed, but npm audit reported 17 known vulnerabilities, including 3 critical and 9 high, so dependency review comes before embedding it in a signed-in application.
reviews.skip_if: Server-side scraping or unattended browser jobs: the README explicitly describes Page Agent as client-side web enhancement rather than server automation.

reviews.name: xiaozhi-esp32
reviews.verdict: Our XiaoZhi ESP32 setup failed in 1 second because plain CMake could not load the ESP-IDF project file or recognize an ESP-IDF command.
reviews.skip_if: Developers expecting a normal desktop CMake project: our plain CMake run failed because ESP-IDF's project file and commands were unavailable.

reviews.name: playwright-mcp
reviews.verdict: Our Playwright MCP build took 6 seconds, but its tests stopped in another 6 seconds because the process used Node 18.20.8 and Playwright required Node 20 or newer.
reviews.skip_if: Coding-agent users optimizing context cost: the project's own README recommends Playwright CLI with skills because MCP tool schemas and accessibility trees consume more tokens.

reviews.name: codebase-memory-mcp
reviews.verdict: Our graph UI build passed in 15 seconds and its tests passed in 10 seconds after a 352-package install, but we did not execute the native indexer those screens control.
reviews.skip_if: Users unwilling to let an installer edit agent configuration and add instructions, skills, or lifecycle hooks: the README says the install command does all of these where supported.

reviews.name: hyperframes
reviews.verdict: Our HyperFrames install consumed 1,641 MB, the build passed in 98 seconds, and the 317-second test command still exited 1 despite reporting 607 passing tests.
reviews.skip_if: React teams already productive with Remotion and its mature cloud renderer: HyperFrames' main distinction is plain HTML, so switching may buy little.

reviews.name: nanobot
reviews.verdict: Our sandbox installed Nanobot in 45 seconds and built it in 9, but 195 tests failed and pip-audit found 42 known vulnerabilities, so we would not deploy commit 3852956 without investigation.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that require a clean source test run before evaluation: at commit 3852956, our sandbox recorded 195 failed tests, 5 collection or setup errors, and 42 known vulnerabilities.

reviews.name: headroom
reviews.verdict: Headroom solves a real cost and context problem, and its reversible retrieval design is more thoughtful than blindly truncating prompts.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone who cannot tolerate lossy changes to fresh tool output: an open August 2026 issue showed the Responses API path compressing file reads despite a protection setting.

reviews.name: Agent-Reach
reviews.verdict: Our Agent Reach run installed 45 packages, used 66 MB, and completed its test command successfully, so the core is cheap to trial.
reviews.skip_if: Users expecting every channel to work anonymously: the English README says Reddit has no zero-configuration path, while Twitter, XiaoHongShu, Facebook, and Instagram need cookies or an existing browser session.

reviews.name: worldmonitor
reviews.verdict: Our World Monitor install consumed 2,346 MB, npm audit found 38 known vulnerabilities, and the repository exposed no test target, even though its 112-second production build passed.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone who needs a decision-grade source of truth: open pull request 7148 fixes airports with no provider data being reported as normal.

reviews.name: graphify
reviews.verdict: Our Graphify run passed 4,541 tests, but 24 Terraform cases failed because `tree_sitter_hcl` was unavailable, so the base tool looks well exercised while optional-language packaging still needs verification.
reviews.skip_if: Developers who need graph output to be authoritative without checking source: Graphify labels inferred edges, and open issue 3123 shows type-only TypeScript imports producing false runtime cycles.

reviews.name: faceswap
reviews.verdict: Faceswap remains a strong choice when you want to train and inspect the whole face-swapping pipeline, not merely upload a portrait and press a button.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone seeking a quick face filter: the documented workflow requires gathering footage, extracting faces, training a model, and converting the result.

reviews.name: firecrawl
reviews.verdict: Firecrawl is a convincing hosted choice when a product needs search, scraping, crawling, and browser interaction behind one API.
reviews.skip_if: Self-hosters expecting every cloud feature: the README explicitly separates the open-source and hosted editions.

reviews.name: Figma-Context-MCP
reviews.verdict: Our Framelink MCP run installed 354 packages, built in 18 seconds, and passed its tests in 29 seconds.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that cannot provide a Figma personal access token: the README makes that credential mandatory.

reviews.name: goose
