reviews.verdict: Our Goose build and test commands each exceeded 900 seconds, so the packaged app is easier to recommend than source contribution on a 3-CPU machine.
reviews.skip_if: People who run recipes from strangers without inspection: open issue 10325 demonstrates a shared recipe executing shell commands through extension and retry fields without a CLI consent prompt in version 1.37.0.

reviews.name: servers
reviews.verdict: Our build finished in 18 seconds, but no test target existed and npm audit found 5 known vulnerabilities, including 4 high-severity advisories.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone looking for a catalog of installable MCP integrations: the README directs that job to the MCP Registry.

reviews.name: skills
reviews.verdict: Anthropic Skills is a useful reference shelf, especially for seeing how a short instruction file can expand into scripts and supporting material.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone seeking one uniformly open-source package: many skills use Apache 2.0, while the DOCX, PDF, PPTX, and XLSX skills are explicitly source-available rather than open source.

reviews.name: taste-skill
reviews.verdict: Taste Skill is an essential tool for anyone serious about using AI for frontend development.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that require pixel-perfect, hand-crafted UIs built to a rigid, pre-existing design system.

reviews.name: cli
reviews.verdict: Our googleworkspace/cli install took 10 seconds and 36 MB, but its test command failed in 6 seconds because Cargo was absent from the Node image.
reviews.skip_if: Organizations requiring an officially supported Google product: the README explicitly says this is not one.

reviews.name: nanoclaw
reviews.verdict: Our NanoClaw build finished in 13 seconds, but 95 of 2,044 tests failed after a 762-second run, so the current checkout belongs in a trial environment before it gets access to messages, files, or scheduled jobs.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring a green test suite before adoption: our run ended with 95 failures out of 2,044 tests, mostly after repeated 5-second timeouts in the log tail.

reviews.name: generator-jhipster
reviews.verdict: Our JHipster run built in 44 seconds and passed 10,348 tests, but 888 failures still made the 141-second test command exit 255.
reviews.skip_if: Small backend services that only need a Spring Boot skeleton: JHipster brings a full generator and front-end choices where Spring Initializr may be enough.

reviews.name: whatsapp-web.js
reviews.verdict: Our run installed 427 packages in 36 seconds, then the tests failed after 9 seconds and npm audit found 20 vulnerabilities, so whatsapp-web.js needs active ownership even before WhatsApp Web changes underneath it.
reviews.skip_if: Businesses that require an authorized WhatsApp integration: the README says the project is unofficial, WhatsApp does not allow bots or unofficial clients, and blocking is still possible.

reviews.name: camofox-browser
reviews.verdict: Our Camofox Browser build passed in 7 seconds with 0 known npm vulnerabilities, but Jest stopped before executing tests because `jest-junit` was missing.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that only need ordinary browser testing: Playwright is simpler and covers Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit.

reviews.name: claude-ads
reviews.verdict: Our Claude Ads run installed 60 packages, passed its build, and reported 506 passing tests, but pip-audit still found 3 known vulnerabilities.
reviews.skip_if: Buyers who need identical behavior in every coding agent: the README calls Claude Code the canonical runtime and says other hosts work only where their skill runtime supports the files.

reviews.name: OpenWA
reviews.verdict: Our OpenWA run passed 5,897 of 5,903 Jest tests after a 59-second install, but npm audit still found 5 high-severity vulnerabilities.
reviews.skip_if: Regulated, authentication-critical, or revenue-critical messaging: the README explicitly directs those workloads to Meta's official Cloud API.

reviews.name: agent-deck
reviews.verdict: Our Agent Deck build succeeded in 64 seconds, but 5 of 26 Go test packages failed during a 568-second run, including a watcher queue assertion.
reviews.skip_if: Windows users who cannot use WSL: native Windows is not listed, and the README recommends WSL2 for full MCP socket-pool support.

reviews.name: skill-up
reviews.verdict: Our npm run installed 150 packages in 35 seconds, but the package exposed no build or test target, so it did not verify the Go evaluator.
reviews.skip_if: Teams expecting a credential-free evaluator: real agent runs need the chosen engine CLI, model access, and provider credentials.

reviews.name: actions-runner-controller
reviews.verdict: Our ARC checkout built successfully in 196 seconds, but only 7 of 12 test packages passed because the end-to-end path expected a kubeconfig that the sandbox did not have.
reviews.skip_if: Small teams satisfied with GitHub-hosted runners: ARC adds a Kubernetes control plane and operational ownership.

reviews.name: loopx
reviews.verdict: Our LoopX checkout installed only 3 npm packages in 6 seconds, but its 3,053 files and roughly 859,791 source lines describe a control system that requires deliberate operating habits.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone seeking a ready-made autonomous worker: the README explicitly keeps dangerous permissions, publishing, production writes, and final ownership with a person Teams that only run short, supervised prompts: LoopX adds goals, todos, leases, gates, quotas, and writeback around work that…

reviews.name: huginn
reviews.verdict: Our Huginn run installed 80 npm packages in 17 seconds and built in 10 seconds, but it exposed no test target, so the clean result does not prove the Rails application passes its own specs.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone expecting a one-command local source install: the README requires an app secret, MySQL or PostgreSQL, database creation and migration, seeded data, and Foreman.

reviews.name: activepieces
reviews.verdict: Our Activepieces install took 367 seconds, added 3,143 packages, and used 2,670 MB, so self-hosting it is a platform commitment rather than a small automation experiment.
reviews.skip_if: Buyers who require every feature under one permissive license: the README says the Community Edition is MIT, while enterprise features use a commercial license.

reviews.name: opentelemetry-collector-contrib
reviews.verdict: Our root test command finished in 6 seconds with 0 tests because it matched no Go packages, so this repository must be evaluated through its multi-module Make targets rather than `go test ./...`.
reviews.skip_if: Teams assuming every contrib component is production-stable: the README says one component can be stable for traces, alpha for metrics, and development for logs.

reviews.name: influxdb
reviews.verdict: Our InfluxDB 3 Core build spent 567 seconds compiling before `libpython3.11` stopped both build and tests, so source adopters should provision the documented Python and protobuf dependencies first.
reviews.skip_if: Flux-dependent InfluxDB 2.x users: the README assigns Flux to the `main-2.x` branch, while v3 Core lists SQL and InfluxQL.

reviews.name: martin
reviews.verdict: Martin is an excellent fit when one deployment must cover live PostGIS tiles and archive formats while retaining serious MBTiles tooling.
reviews.skip_if: Developers expecting a source build to work in a plain Debian Rust container: our build stopped because CMake could not find `libuv`.

reviews.name: dbgate
reviews.verdict: DbGate is a good fit for developers who want one familiar interface across SQL, document, and key-value databases, especially when both desktop and self-hosted web access matter.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that need every listed connector in the free edition: the README marks Redshift, CosmosDB, Firestore, and Turso support as Premium.

reviews.name: awesome-free-apps
reviews.verdict: Awesome Free Apps is a very good browsing shelf and a poor substitute for product research.
reviews.skip_if: Security-sensitive users who treat inclusion as a safety audit: an open report says one listed app's expired domain now leads to an illegal gambling site.

reviews.name: kibana
reviews.verdict: Our Kibana install took 761 seconds and 3,122 MB, then the distributable build failed after 38 seconds, so building this source tree is specialist work even before Elasticsearch enters the picture.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that do not use Elasticsearch: Kibana is coupled to it and rejects several version mismatches.

reviews.name: OpenViking
reviews.verdict: Our OpenViking build took 10 seconds, but its test command stopped in 7 seconds before collection because `pytest_asyncio` was missing, so commit 234a2d9 needs a dependency fix before its suite can support a production decision.
reviews.skip_if: SaaS vendors unable to meet AGPLv3 network-use obligations: the main project is AGPLv3, although the Rust CLI and examples use Apache-2.0.

reviews.name: dbx
reviews.verdict: Our DBX run built in 16 seconds and passed 10,947 of 10,950 tests, but 2 failures kept the 746-second suite red.
reviews.skip_if: Database administrators who need to trust structure-only transfer against production today: issue 7312 says a v0.5.96 PostgreSQL transfer omitted non-primary indexes.

reviews.name: flights
reviews.verdict: Our fast-flights run installed 37 packages and passed all 8 tests in 35 seconds across install, build, and test steps.
reviews.skip_if: Booking or customer-facing systems that need a supported data contract: fast-flights parses undocumented Google data, and issue #101 reports missing best-flight results.

reviews.name: liteparse
reviews.verdict: Our LiteParse source build spent 378 seconds compiling before a Tesseract language-data download timed out, and the test step failed on the same download path.
reviews.skip_if: Teams expecting high-fidelity Markdown from dense tables, multi-column pages, charts, handwriting, or scans: the README directs those cases to the hosted LlamaParse service.

reviews.name: txtai
reviews.verdict: Our txtai install took 369 seconds, consumed 6,602 MB, and built successfully, but pytest collected 0 tests and pip-audit found 1 known vulnerability.
reviews.skip_if: Projects needing a small base environment: our standard install pulled 282 packages and occupied 6,602 MB before optional features or model weights.

reviews.name: nocodb
reviews.verdict: Our NocoDB install consumed 3,019 MB across 3,948 packages, then exposed no root build or test target for the harness, so source adoption needs more scrutiny than the one-command Docker demo suggests.
reviews.skip_if: Teams seeking a permissive open-source license for a commercial product: the Sustainable Use License limits use to internal business, personal, or non-commercial purposes and restricts distribution.

reviews.name: superset
reviews.verdict: Our Superset build finished in 13 seconds, but the test run stopped at 200 setup errors because SQLite lacked the `css_templates` table, so a source deployment needs the documented initialization path rather than a generic pytest command.
reviews.skip_if: Small teams seeking a single-process dashboard tool: the production architecture includes a metadata database and can add Redis, Celery workers, and async query services.

reviews.name: airbyte
reviews.verdict: Our Airbyte documentation install pulled 1,892 packages, and its production build was killed after 179 seconds, so even the docs slice carries monorepo-scale weight.
reviews.skip_if: Teams expecting a small single-container utility: the self-managed platform uses Kubernetes tooling, multiple services, persistence, connector workloads, and substantial local resources.

reviews.name: surrealdb
reviews.verdict: Our SurrealDB checkout spent 900 seconds on the build and another 900 seconds on tests without finishing compilation, so source validation is expensive on a 3-CPU box.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that need a permissive database license: the repository uses Business Source License 1.1, so commercial deployment terms deserve legal review.

reviews.name: supabase
reviews.verdict: Our Supabase install pulled 3,094 packages and used 2,934 MB, then the build failed at the federated-content task after 36 seconds.
reviews.skip_if: Teams seeking a small self-hosted database appliance: the official Compose stack includes Postgres, Auth, Realtime, Storage, Studio, Envoy, an edge runtime, logging, a pooler, and more.

reviews.name: Tech-OA-Interview-Questions
reviews.verdict: Our build finished in 4 seconds after a 12-second install, but there was no test target to establish correctness.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone expecting a self-contained offline problem set, because many rows send you to FastPrep Candidates who need verified official questions, because the material is rebuilt from candidate reports Teams seeking a tested Python library or stable API Users who require…

reviews.name: iroh
reviews.verdict: Our Iroh checkout installed 461 packages, but both the 20-second build and 9-second test run failed when Clang rejected the configured `lld` linker selection.
reviews.skip_if: Teams wanting a language-neutral drop-in library: the README calls Rust the easiest route and sends other languages to the separate `iroh-ffi` repository.

reviews.name: theia
reviews.verdict: Our npm install failed after 275 seconds at the native-keymap 2.5.0 node-gyp rebuild, so Theia is not a low-friction trial in the measured environment.
reviews.skip_if: Individual developers who only want a ready-to-use editor with minimal setup Small teams that cannot maintain a large TypeScript monorepo Buyers who require a one-command container deployment from the main repository Projects that need every VS Code extension to behave…

reviews.name: go-modern-guidelines
reviews.verdict: Our run installed 3 packages and passed all 6 tests in 32 seconds total, so trying Modern Go Guidelines is cheap for a Go team that already uses coding agents.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that want a deterministic source rewriter: the project gives an agent instructions, while issue 9 asks it to use Go 1.26's `go fix` before model-led edits.

reviews.name: oh-my-codex
reviews.verdict: Our oh-my-codex test command hit the 900-second cap with 35 tests passed and none failed, while npm audit reported 6 known vulnerabilities.
reviews.skip_if: Native Windows or Codex App users who need first-class support: the README says those paths may break and receive less support than macOS or Linux CLI use.

reviews.name: BMAD-METHOD
reviews.verdict: Our BMAD-METHOD run installed 786 packages in 26 seconds but failed its tests after 21 seconds, while npm audit reported 8 high-severity vulnerabilities.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that need their clean checkout to pass its own test command today: our commit 11bfd36 run exited 1, and the log only concluded that installation component tests failed.

reviews.name: garden-skills
reviews.verdict: Our Garden Skills run installed 0 packages in 21 seconds, but it had no build or test target, so adoption depends on reading and trialing the individual instructions rather than trusting a passing suite.
reviews.skip_if: Teams expecting a tested software package: our checkout had no build or test target, so there is no executable suite proving that all five instruction packs behave as written.

reviews.name: nuclei-templates
reviews.verdict: Our sandbox produced no install, build, or test result for commit ed8fed8 because this is a scanner-content repository without a supported runnable ecosystem or Dockerfile.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone looking for a standalone scanner: the README says this repository stores templates and that the separate Nuclei project is the engine.

reviews.name: iina
reviews.verdict: Our 3-CPU, 8 GB Debian run produced no build or test result because IINA targets macOS and supplies no Dockerfile.
reviews.skip_if: Windows or Linux users, because IINA is designed for macOS 11.0 and newer Anyone wanting a server, media library backend, or multi-device streaming platform Teams expecting a Linux-friendly source build or container image Users who need a tiny issue tracker…

reviews.name: triton
reviews.verdict: Our Triton source install reached the 900-second cap and ended with a failed CMake build, so this is specialist compiler work even though the user wheel installs with pip.
reviews.skip_if: Application teams that only need to train or serve standard models: Triton is a kernel compiler, not a model framework or inference server.

reviews.name: nvm
reviews.verdict: Our Linux build completed in 48 seconds, but all 13 Go test targets failed during setup or compilation, so the source builds while its test path is not portable to our sandbox.
reviews.skip_if: macOS or Linux users: the README says this is a separate Windows-only project, not a port of `nvm-sh/nvm`.

reviews.name: codex-plugin-cc
reviews.verdict: Our sandbox installed 3 packages in 16 seconds and passed all 91 tests, but the build stopped after 9 seconds because the `codex` command was unavailable.
reviews.skip_if: Developers who do not use Claude Code: the README packages the project around Claude Code commands, hooks, agents, and its plugin marketplace.

reviews.name: whatsmeow
reviews.verdict: Our whatsmeow run installed 39 packages, built successfully, and passed 2 of 2 tests in 71 seconds total, which makes the code easy to trial but leaves live WhatsApp behavior untested.
reviews.skip_if: Products that require voice or video calls: the README lists calls as unimplemented.

reviews.name: anchor
reviews.verdict: Our Anchor checkout completed its npm install path in 9 seconds with 0 packages added, but exposed no build or test target for the harness.
reviews.skip_if: Developers seeking a JavaScript smart-contract language: on-chain programs are written in Rust, while TypeScript is a client and test option.

reviews.name: purple
reviews.verdict: Our Purple run built in 97 seconds and passed 5,834 of 5,840 tests, but all 6 failures hit Vault SSH proxy-chain behavior, exactly where a wrong hop can block or misdirect access.
reviews.skip_if: Windows users: the README documents macOS and Linux, with no Windows installation path.

reviews.name: printing-press-library
reviews.verdict: Our Printing Press Library test run failed in 8 seconds because its compiled test glob was not found, even though installation and build both succeeded and npm audit found 0 vulnerabilities.
reviews.skip_if: Security-sensitive operators expecting secret redaction to hide an entire token: issue 1595 says the shared masking code leaves the real last 4 characters visible in errors, URLs, and dry runs.

reviews.name: ui-skills
reviews.verdict: Our ui-skills install used 687 MB, then built in 42 seconds and passed all 58 tests in 13 seconds with 0 known vulnerabilities.
reviews.skip_if: Teams looking for a component library, design tokens, or generated assets: the registry mainly supplies prose instructions for agents.

reviews.name: cli
reviews.verdict: Our Entire CLI run built in 84 seconds, but 3 of 85 test packages failed, so the tested commit is easy to compile and not clean enough to adopt without reproducing those failures.
reviews.skip_if: Public-repository teams unwilling to publish agent conversations: the README says transcripts live in the repository and are visible when that repository is public.

reviews.name: open-code-review
reviews.verdict: Our OpenCodeReview checkout could not install because its `0.0.0` package version produced a GitHub asset URL that returned 404 after 12 seconds.
reviews.skip_if: Repositories whose code cannot be sent to the configured model endpoint: normal mode gives an LLM diffs, full files, searches, and related context.

reviews.name: warp
reviews.verdict: Our Warp build took 860 seconds, and the test command failed with exit code 101 after 674 seconds without naming the failed case in the supplied tail.
reviews.skip_if: Users seeking a tiny, terminal-only program: our checkout occupied 388.9 MB before dependencies and installed 1,397 Rust packages.

reviews.name: SenPaiScanner
reviews.verdict: Our SenPai Scanner run installed 251 Go packages, built in 75 seconds, and passed all 7 tests in 25 seconds.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone expecting a general port or vulnerability scanner: the README limits SenPai to Cloudflare reachability and supported proxy links.

reviews.name: dsh-web
reviews.verdict: Our dsh-web-ui run built in 32 seconds, but its recursive test command stopped after `dsh-ssh` reported 139 of 140 tests passing.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone who does not already run DeepSeek Harness: the README requires a working `dsh web` installation.

reviews.name: webvm
reviews.verdict: Our WebVM checkout installed 233 packages and built in 61 seconds combined, but it offered no test target for checking the virtualization layer.
reviews.skip_if: Organizations assuming Apache 2.0 covers the complete deployed stack: the README says organizational use of the public CheerpX deployment requires a license, and separate hosting of a downloaded CheerpX build needs a commercial license.

reviews.name: wgcf
reviews.verdict: Our wgcf run installed 63 packages in 35 seconds, built in 39 seconds, and passed all 3 tests in 11 seconds.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone who requires vendor support or a stable public API: the README calls wgcf unofficial, and v2.2.32 had to restore a TLS fingerprint after Cloudflare returned HTTP 429.

reviews.name: agentsview
reviews.verdict: Our AgentsView run built in 3 seconds but only 17 of 46 Go test packages passed, so the current checkout needs investigation before team deployment.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that need aggregate analytics without exposing employee transcripts: issue 901 requests metadata-only sharing and role-based session visibility because the shared dashboard does not provide those controls.

reviews.name: rhwp
reviews.verdict: Our rhwp build completed in 168 seconds and its test run recorded 3,880 passes with zero failures before the 900-second cap, which is strong evidence for a v0.8.4 project but not a completed suite.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that require pixel-identical output for every HWP document today: open renderer issues describe pagination gaps, clipped table text, and line placement outside the page.

reviews.name: shannon
reviews.verdict: Our Shannon run installed 413 packages and built in 12 seconds, but the repository supplied no test target, so build success is the strongest automated result we can report.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone scanning production or a system without explicit written authorization: the README warns that exploits can create users, submit forms, mutate data, and trigger outbound requests.

reviews.name: takumi
reviews.verdict: Our Takumi checkout installed 950 packages and used 1,687 MB, then its root build and example-heavy test command both failed within 12 seconds.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone converting arbitrary web pages pixel for pixel: the README says Takumi supports less CSS than Chrome and recommends Puppeteer for complex pages.

reviews.name: treehouse
reviews.verdict: Our Treehouse build passed in 111 seconds and all 10 Go tests passed in 232 seconds.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that need to choose an arbitrary base branch at acquisition: issues 67 and 58 request configurable base-ref behavior.

reviews.name: gpui-component
reviews.verdict: Our GPUI Component build ran for 431 seconds before the linker rejected missing `xkbcommon-x11`, and tests hit that same library after 14 seconds, so Linux teams should run the project's bootstrap before judging the Rust code.
reviews.skip_if: Web-first teams: the project targets desktop applications, and its interaction rules intentionally differ from browser conventions.

reviews.name: plugins
reviews.verdict: Cursor Plugins is the right first stop for extending Cursor because it combines an official catalog with source you can inspect before granting access.
reviews.skip_if: Developers using another editor as their primary host: installation and lifecycle instructions are specific to Cursor Settings and `/add-plugin`.

reviews.name: CloudflareSpeedTest
reviews.verdict: Our CloudflareSpeedTest run installed 9 packages, built in 26 seconds, and completed `go test` in 4 seconds, but the test command exercised 0 tests.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone optimizing Cloudflare WARP: the README explicitly says the tool is for websites and does not support choosing WARP IPs.

reviews.name: nvm
reviews.verdict: Our Linux run built NVM for Windows in 1 second, then all 6 test packages failed because Windows syscall symbols were unavailable, so that failure describes platform coupling rather than a broken Windows release.
reviews.skip_if: macOS or Linux users: the README explicitly directs them to the separate `nvm-sh/nvm` project.

reviews.name: tree-sitter
reviews.verdict: Our Tree-sitter build finished in 60 seconds, but 266 of 305 tests failed in 9 seconds with no cause visible in the supplied log tail.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that need semantic analysis, type checking, or code generation out of the box: Tree-sitter produces concrete syntax trees, not a complete compiler frontend.

reviews.name: actors
reviews.verdict: Our Rivet checkout installed 2,928 packages and used 3,846 MB, then both the 15-second build and 20-second test run failed in example workspaces.
reviews.skip_if: Contributors who require the entire monorepo to build and test cleanly in a fresh Node environment: both stages failed in our sandbox.

reviews.name: fff
reviews.verdict: Our npm check completed in 6 seconds with 0 installed packages and 0 known vulnerabilities, but it built and tested none of FFF's Rust or native deliverables.
reviews.skip_if: One-off shell searches where a persistent index and watcher have no time to repay their startup and integration cost.

reviews.name: zed
reviews.verdict: Our source build failed after 844 seconds, and the test attempt failed after 271 seconds at the same timed-out WebRTC download, so contributors need a more reliable dependency path than our fresh sandbox had.
reviews.skip_if: Browser or Chromebook users: the README says a web version is not available and links only to a tracking discussion.

reviews.name: docker-agent
reviews.verdict: Our Docker Agent run built in 213 seconds, then 267 of 271 tests passed before the suite exited with 4 failures, so teams should trial it behind explicit safety and cost limits before standardizing on it.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring a green full test run before adoption: our commit b407a13 run ended with 4 failures out of 271 tests, and the supplied log tail did not identify their cause.

reviews.name: atlassian-mcp-server
reviews.verdict: Our repository run installed only 2 packages and passed 17 of 17 tests, confirming that the open checkout is a small integration package rather than the hosted Atlassian service.
reviews.skip_if: Jira Server or Data Center customers: the README requires an Atlassian Cloud site.

reviews.name: Megatron-LM
reviews.verdict: Megatron-LM belongs on the shortlist for teams with NVIDIA clusters and engineers who understand distributed training failures.
reviews.skip_if: Developers looking for a CPU-first training library or a useful laptop demo: the installation guide recommends NVIDIA Turing or later, and the project is designed around GPU-distributed work.

reviews.name: awesome-llm-apps
reviews.verdict: Our tarot-folder run installed 93 packages in 49 seconds and built in 4 seconds, but it had no test target, so the result supports learning and inspection rather than production trust.
reviews.skip_if: Teams expecting one maintained application with a single install and test command: the repository is a collection of independent projects with separate requirements and instructions.

reviews.name: marin
reviews.verdict: Our Marin run installed 225 packages and used 1,954 MB, yet pytest stopped after 13 seconds on its configured arguments, so this platform belongs with research teams prepared to own the environment.
reviews.skip_if: Application developers who only need to fine-tune or serve an existing model: Marin's README centers the project on foundation-model research and training.

reviews.name: ai-gateway
reviews.verdict: Our Envoy AI Gateway build succeeded, but only 6 of 12 Go packages passed before the 668-second test run failed.
reviews.skip_if: Small teams seeking a single-process OpenAI proxy: the documented path requires Kubernetes, Helm, Envoy Gateway, two AI Gateway charts, and several custom resources.

reviews.name: adk-samples
reviews.verdict: Our adk-samples run built in 5 seconds and passed 900 tests, but the suite still exited 1 because 9 collection and setup checks could not import `tomlkit`.
reviews.skip_if: Teams seeking a supported production product: the repository says it is not officially supported by Google and describes recipes as demonstrations and starting points.

reviews.name: LightRAG
reviews.verdict: Our LightRAG build installed 85 packages and completed, but pytest stopped with 60 collection or setup errors, so this is not a clean drop-in for a fresh Debian box.
reviews.skip_if: Small search applications that only need the closest matching chunks: LightRAG adds entity extraction, relationship merging, graph storage, and extra model calls.

reviews.name: agent-framework
reviews.verdict: Our Agent Framework install pulled 233 packages and occupied 912 MB, then the full test run failed after 72 seconds, so adopting it requires a team willing to verify its exact workflow path.
reviews.skip_if: Small applications that need one stateless model call: the README positions this framework for orchestration beyond a simple chat loop, while our install pulled 233 packages.

reviews.name: colibri
reviews.verdict: Our Colibri run installed 34 Python packages, built in 10 seconds, and found 0 known vulnerabilities, but it ran no tests and loaded no model weights.
reviews.skip_if: Users expecting a quick local chatbot download: the README's reference GLM container is about 372 GB, while Kimi K3 is about 1.6 TB.

reviews.name: zeroclaw
reviews.verdict: Our ZeroClaw build took 431 seconds and 407 of 408 tests passed; the lone failure came from a release script calling an absent `jq`, so serious self-hosters have a promising build with one concrete packaging prerequisite to fix.
reviews.skip_if: People seeking a simple chat application: the minimum V3 configuration still needs provider, agent, and risk-profile sections, while useful deployments add channel credentials and service management.

reviews.name: semantic-router
reviews.verdict: Our Semantic Router run installed 78 packages and built successfully, but its test command ended with 73 passes and 6 collection or setup errors.
reviews.skip_if: Applications with one model endpoint and no routing policy: the local stack starts Router, Envoy, Dashboard, and supporting services before it reaches the backend.

reviews.name: ai-memory
reviews.verdict: Our ai-memory run passed 764 of 767 tests after a 238-second build, while the packaging failures included a missing Docker executable and a refused checksum update.
reviews.skip_if: Native macOS users who require dependable hook delivery today: issue 493 reports v1.32.1 spooling events without transmitting them.

reviews.name: distilly
reviews.verdict: Our Distilly run installed 42 packages, built in 5 seconds, and passed all 35 tests with 0 audit findings, so the code is easy to trial.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone creating a relationship or colleague profile without informed consent: the workflow can ingest private chats, email, documents, and third-party messages.

reviews.name: embabel-agent
reviews.verdict: Our Embabel run passed 2,025 of 2,123 tests, skipped 98, and failed none, which makes version 1.5.1 a credible trial for a serious Spring team.
reviews.skip_if: Python-first teams or developers seeking a small scriptable agent loop: Embabel is a large Maven and Spring codebase with about 297,419 source lines in our checkout.

reviews.name: OpenHands
reviews.verdict: Our OpenHands run installed 1,998 packages and used 1,043 MB, then its build and tests passed, so this is a serious control plane with a heavy local footprint.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone unwilling to give an agent broad code access: the direct install runs the agent server on the host with full filesystem access, a risk the README warns about twice.

reviews.name: cline
reviews.verdict: Our Cline run installed 2,435 packages and used 3,838 MB, then its test command failed after 500 seconds, so this is a capable agent platform with a costly contributor setup.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that require every client to be open source: the project index says the JetBrains plugins are currently closed source.

reviews.name: OpenHands
reviews.verdict: Our OpenHands run installed 1,998 packages and used 1,043 MB, then its build and tests passed, so this is a serious control plane with a heavy local footprint.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone unwilling to give an agent broad code access: the direct install runs the agent server on the host with full filesystem access, a risk the README warns about twice.

reviews.name: LibreChat
reviews.verdict: Our LibreChat install completed in 78 seconds and occupied 2,295 MB, but the source build failed 20 seconds later in `librechat-data-provider`, so we would not adopt it without pinning a revision and reproducing the build in CI.
reviews.skip_if: Developers wanting a small UI for one local model: our install pulled 2,678 packages and occupied 2,295 MB.

reviews.name: lobehub
reviews.verdict: Our npm install failed after 303 seconds on `workspace:*`, so LobeHub is a poor choice for teams unwilling to follow its pnpm-based monorepo workflow.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone seeking a small codebase to modify casually: our checkout contained 15,260 files and about 2,097,297 lines of source.

reviews.name: ComfyUI
reviews.verdict: Our ComfyUI checkout installed 124 packages and used 5,903 MB, then 44 tests failed and 65 hit collection or setup errors, so adopting it means accepting a large environment whose tested commit was not clean on our box.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone who wants a simple prompt box with no graph to learn: ComfyUI exposes the pipeline as connected nodes and expects the user to manage models and inputs.

reviews.name: open-webui
reviews.verdict: Our Open WebUI build passed after 180 seconds, but the 1,263-package install carried 29 known vulnerabilities and no test target was available.
reviews.skip_if: Companies that require standard permissive licensing for every current file: the README says newer code carries an Open WebUI license with a branding-preservation requirement.

reviews.name: higress
reviews.verdict: Our Higress install ran for 78 seconds and failed before build or tests because the expected `external/go-control-plane/go.mod` file was missing.
reviews.skip_if: Developers expecting a normal `go mod` install from a plain clone: our install failed because `go.mod` points at `external/go-control-plane`, while the repository prepares that path through submodules and a prebuild script.

reviews.name: securo
reviews.verdict: Our build completed in 5 seconds, and all 3165 reported pytest tests passed with 0 failures.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone who wants a fully managed service with no server maintenance Users who require guaranteed support for every bank, because sync depends on external providers and credentials Organizations unwilling to comply with AGPL-3.0 obligations when modifying or providing the software…

reviews.name: jellyfin-web
reviews.verdict: Our Jellyfin Web install consumed 1,183 MB and exposed 59 audit findings, although all 162 tests passed in 18 seconds, so adopting it means accepting a large, actively maintained frontend rather than a tidy React starter.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone seeking a complete media server in this repository: Jellyfin Web is a frontend and needs a compatible Jellyfin server for useful operation.

reviews.name: ente
reviews.verdict: Our Ente install pulled 1,114 Rust packages, but its build failed after 423 seconds and its test command failed after 45 seconds at the same native CMake step.
reviews.skip_if: Self-hosters who expect maintainer help for routine deployment problems: the server README says support queries cannot currently be prioritized and asks users to use Discussions.

reviews.name: infisical
reviews.verdict: Our sandbox install succeeded in 10 seconds with 0 known npm vulnerabilities, but it found no root build or test target.
reviews.skip_if: Solo developers who only need encrypted configuration files and do not want to run a service Teams expecting this repository root to install, build, and test like a small npm package Buyers who require license certainty from repository metadata alone,…

reviews.name: Cap
reviews.verdict: Our Cap checkout occupied 4,123 MB after installing 2,914 packages, then both its build and test commands failed, so developing the whole stack demands more setup than the polished recorder suggests.
reviews.skip_if: Linux users expecting the same documented desktop path as macOS and Windows: the README's user setup names only those two platforms.

reviews.name: postiz-app
reviews.verdict: Postiz is a credible choice for an agency or technical marketing team that wants a shared scheduler without handing the whole workflow to a SaaS vendor.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone expecting every channel to work after one Docker command: most providers require a developer app and environment variables, and the docs say unconfigured providers still appear but fail when clicked.

reviews.name: nocobase
reviews.verdict: Our NocoBase source install failed after 309 seconds because Yarn saw Node 18.20.8 while one dependency required Node 20 or newer, so contributors should verify the runtime before taking on its 26,552-file monorepo.
reviews.skip_if: Companies building a public no-code, low-code, or AI platform SaaS or PaaS: the supplemental license forbids that use of the original or modified software.

reviews.name: neko-master
reviews.verdict: Our Neko Master build passed in 87 seconds, but the install pulled 898 packages and occupied 973 MB before any traffic data was stored.
reviews.skip_if: Users of sing-box or dae who need native collection today: open issues 72 and 59 request those backends, while the docs list only Clash, Mihomo, and Surge.

reviews.name: ODS
reviews.verdict: Our ODS installer project added 151 packages, used 99 MB, and built in 29 seconds with 0 npm audit findings, but it exposed no test target.
reviews.skip_if: Intel Mac users: current macOS support requires Apple Silicon and Docker Desktop.

reviews.name: komodo
reviews.verdict: Our Komodo run built successfully in 548 seconds and passed all 5 tests, which is a clean result but a thin safety net for roughly 185,300 source lines controlling many servers.
reviews.skip_if: Kubernetes-first organizations: Komodo manages Docker, Compose, and Swarm rather than Kubernetes resources.

reviews.name: CubeSandbox
reviews.verdict: Our CubeAPI run built in 108 seconds and passed all 120 Rust tests, the cleanest measured result in this batch.
reviews.skip_if: Developers limited to macOS, Windows, or Linux without KVM: the quick start requires x86_64 Linux with KVM and labels the development VM path as poor-performing.

reviews.name: cliamp
reviews.verdict: Our cliamp build succeeded in 43 seconds, but 11 of 44 tested packages failed, including several core playback and UI packages.
reviews.skip_if: Linux users who cannot install ALSA development headers or a PipeWire or PulseAudio ALSA bridge: the README requires the headers for builds and names the bridge as the fix for silent playback.

reviews.name: Motrix
reviews.verdict: Motrix v2 is appealing if you want the same download core on a desktop and a NAS, especially with CLI pairing and plugin isolation.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone who cannot risk prerelease data behavior: Motrix says v1 migration has not been validated and recommends a separate account, machine, or Docker data directory for v2 beta testing.

reviews.name: Xray-core
reviews.verdict: Our Xray-core build finished in 76 seconds, but 3 of 80 tested packages failed, so adopting it means owning a real verification job.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that require a clean test run before adoption: in our sandbox, 3 of 80 tested packages failed even though installation and compilation succeeded.

reviews.name: ToolJet
reviews.verdict: Our ToolJet checkout was 1,711.1 MB, and its root build failed after 146 seconds without a clear exception in the log tail, while no test target was available.
reviews.skip_if: Teams expecting the Community edition to include AI app generation, AI queries, agents, GitSync, audit logs, white-labeling, or multi-environment management: the README assigns those to ToolJet AI Enterprise.

reviews.name: cpa-usage-keeper
reviews.verdict: Our CPA Usage Keeper test run took 719 seconds and ended with 9 passing packages and 1 failure, even though installation and the 84-second build succeeded.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone who does not run CLIProxyAPI: Keeper depends on CPA's management API, usage statistics, and queue rather than acting as a general model gateway dashboard.

reviews.name: neko
reviews.verdict: Our Neko server built in 43 seconds, but its Go test step produced build failures in 17 of 18 package results, so source adopters need to reproduce that command before trusting a fork.
reviews.skip_if: Administrators who cannot expose or relay WebRTC traffic: the sample Compose file maps UDP ports 52000 through 52100 and requires a client-reachable NAT address.

reviews.name: TokenHub
reviews.verdict: Our TokenHub backend built in 82 seconds, but its only discovered test package failed after 452 seconds with response-worker goroutines in the log tail.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that require a green backend suite before evaluation: our only discovered Go test package failed after 452 seconds, with response workers still shown in the log tail.

reviews.name: EasyTier
reviews.verdict: Our EasyTier checkout installed 799 packages in 67 seconds, but it offered no root build or test target and we did not establish a privileged VPN tunnel.
reviews.skip_if: Administrators who cannot safely grant network privileges: the quick start uses root or administrator access, and containers need TUN plus network capabilities.

reviews.name: WatchYourLAN
reviews.verdict: Our WatchYourLAN run built successfully after installing 188 packages, but its test step found 0 tests, so the project earns a cautious trial rather than blind trust.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone who needs built-in authentication: the README says there is none, and host networking exposes port 8840 unless a firewall or proxy blocks it.

reviews.name: hyperswitch
reviews.verdict: Our run installed 138 npm packages in 22 seconds with 0 audit findings, but the repository exposed no npm build or test target, so we did not verify the 1.3-million-line Rust payment server.
reviews.skip_if: Small products happy with one processor: the README's common starting points are multi-processor routing and direct acquirer connections, which add little value to a simple Stripe setup.

reviews.name: web-check
reviews.verdict: Our Web-Check install pulled 1,209 packages and occupied 1,506 MB, while the repository provided no test target, so this friendly dashboard carries more dependency and verification risk than its one-command demo suggests.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone planning to expose the default API publicly, because open PR 315 documents SSRF access to private networks across shared handlers Teams needing authenticated, recurring asset management rather than one-domain snapshots Auditors who need findings backed by exploit validation, because…

reviews.name: cloudreve
reviews.verdict: Our Cloudreve checkout built in 17 seconds, but only 6 of 35 test packages passed, so the source is easy to compile and hard to accept without more investigation.
reviews.skip_if: Teams wanting a managed drive with no server work: Cloudreve leaves availability, backups, upgrades, and storage policy to the operator.

reviews.name: macro
reviews.verdict: Our Macro install pulled 1,686 packages and used 1,876 MB, while the repository exposed no top-level build or test target for the lab to run.
reviews.skip_if: Teams looking for a small self-hosted groupware package: local development starts Postgres, Redis, LocalStack, OpenSearch, Kafka, FusionAuth, and many Rust services.

reviews.name: open-notebook
reviews.verdict: Our Open Notebook run built in 8 seconds and passed 374 tests, but 200 async tests failed before the suite stopped, so the current source path needs repair before production approval.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring a passing source test suite before evaluation: our run stopped after 200 async-test failures, although 374 tests passed.

reviews.name: pangolin
reviews.verdict: Our Pangolin checkout pulled 1,637 packages and 1,580 MB, then failed its build after 30 seconds with module-not-found errors.
reviews.skip_if: Self-hosters without a public Linux server, domain, root access, or the required TCP and UDP firewall ports: the quick-install guide requires all of them.

reviews.name: OpenList
reviews.verdict: Our OpenList build passed in 106 seconds, but 5 of 35 tested Go packages failed in the same sandbox, so it deserves a provider-specific trial rather than immediate trust with backups.
reviews.skip_if: Backup operators who need strict S3 compatibility without qualification: issue #2947 reports 302 redirects causing Restic unlock and initialization retries on a mounted provider.

reviews.name: anubis
reviews.verdict: Our Anubis install stopped after 24 seconds because its prepare script reached a Go version and `tool` block the sandbox parser did not accept, so source contributors need the exact documented toolchain before they begin.
reviews.skip_if: Sites that need every small browser, archive, feed reader, or script client to work by default: the README calls Anubis a nuclear response and warns that good bots may be blocked.

reviews.name: 3x-ui
reviews.verdict: 3X-UI is a capable personal control panel for an administrator who already understands Linux networking and Xray.
reviews.skip_if: Production operators: the README explicitly says the project is for personal use and should not be used in a production environment.

reviews.name: homebox
reviews.verdict: Our Homebox build succeeded in 166 seconds, but its Go test run ended with 13 packages passed and 1 failed in `internal/sys/validate`.
reviews.skip_if: Organizations that need mature role and account administration: open issue 439 collects unfinished user-management work, so this is not an enterprise asset system.

reviews.name: rustdesk
reviews.verdict: Our RustDesk build pulled 720 packages, ran for 165 seconds, and then failed because `gstreamer-1.0` was missing, so source deployment demands the full native dependency checklist.
reviews.skip_if: Developers expecting `cargo build` to work after Rust packages alone: our build stopped because the system `gstreamer-1.0` library was unavailable.

reviews.name: clash-verge-rev
reviews.verdict: Our Clash Verge Rev install added 710 packages, but the build failed after 95 seconds because the Linux image lacked gdk-3.0; all 15 tests passed.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone looking for a proxy service or included access credentials: the application is a client, and the README's provider promotions are separate commercial offers.

reviews.name: dokploy
reviews.verdict: Our Dokploy run built successfully in 281 seconds, but 5 of 886 tests failed, so v0.30.2 deserves a staged pilot rather than control of critical workloads on day one.
reviews.skip_if: Operators who want a standard unprivileged app install: the documented path runs a remote shell script on a VPS, configures Docker Swarm, and needs host ports available.

reviews.name: grok2api
reviews.verdict: Our Grok2API run built in 99 seconds, but 8 of 121 tests failed after an 894-second test run, so the current commit needs investigation before it carries shared production traffic.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone unwilling to accept account-policy risk: the README labels the project for technical research and tells users to comply with Grok's terms and local law.

reviews.name: invidious
reviews.verdict: Our Invidious checkout installed in 19 seconds and built in 8, but pytest collected 0 tests and exited with code 5, so that run does not prove behavioral correctness.
reviews.skip_if: Casual self-hosters expecting one low-maintenance container: the installation guide requires Invidious, PostgreSQL, and Invidious Companion, then recommends restarting Invidious at least daily.

reviews.name: logseq
reviews.verdict: Our Logseq install pulled 1,151 packages and occupied 834 MB, while its tests stopped after 12 seconds because `clojure` was missing, so contributors should expect a polyglot toolchain rather than a routine Node project.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone who cannot tolerate data-loss risk: the README calls database graphs beta, mobile and real-time collaboration alpha, and recommends a separate test graph plus backups.

reviews.name: joplin
reviews.verdict: Our Joplin source install reached Yarn's link step but did not finish within 900 seconds, so users should favor the packaged apps and contributors should budget for a demanding monorepo setup.
reviews.skip_if: Businesses expecting the bundled server code to have the repository's general AGPL terms: `packages/server` has a separate personal-use license and directs organizations to Joplin Server Business.

reviews.name: kaneo
reviews.verdict: Our Kaneo run installed 1,476 packages, then passed its 39-second build and 64-second test step.
reviews.skip_if: Users who need a database-free local app: Kaneo requires PostgreSQL, and open issue 1637 requests local-storage support.

reviews.name: ant-design
reviews.verdict: Our Ant Design checkout installed 3,053 packages and used 2,288 MB, then its build failed and its tests exceeded 900 seconds, so contributing demands more patience than the one-line application install suggests.
reviews.skip_if: Vue, Svelte, or server-rendered HTML teams: the README defines Ant Design as a React library and its usage example imports React components.

reviews.name: qwik
reviews.verdict: Our Qwik checkout installed 2,079 packages and occupied 1,584 MB, then both its build and test commands exited 1.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring a stable major release today: the main branch README says Qwik 2 is beta and sends Qwik 1 users to a separate branch.

reviews.name: Kazumi
reviews.verdict: Our lab could not run Kazumi at commit 4520136 because it had no Dart harness and the repository supplied no Dockerfile, leaving its build and tests unverified here.
reviews.skip_if: English-only users: the README, Q&A, issue traffic, release notes, and linked documentation are primarily Chinese, with no English guide linked.

reviews.name: remote-jobs
reviews.verdict: Our 43-second build succeeded, but npm audit found 6 high-severity advisories and the repository offered no test target, so a public fork needs dependency review and its own checks.
reviews.skip_if: Applicants who need live roles, salaries, seniority, or closing dates: profiles describe companies, and the apply link only leads to a careers page or company website.

reviews.name: dsh-deep-whale
reviews.verdict: Our Maid Atelier run installed 111 packages in 38 seconds and passed all 140 tests, so this is a tested skin package rather than a folder of loose CSS.
reviews.skip_if: Commercial products: the two skins use CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 and the README explicitly prohibits commercial use.

reviews.name: ai-guide
reviews.verdict: Our ai-guide install pulled 1,072 packages in 40 seconds, but no build or test target ran, so judge this repository by its writing and maintained links rather than software checks.
reviews.skip_if: English-only learners seeking the whole library: the English translation directory covers the Vibe Coding tutorial, not every top-level section.

reviews.name: router
reviews.verdict: Our TanStack Router run built in 13 seconds and reached 870 passing tests with 0 failures, but the full command still had not finished at the 900-second cap after a 2,365-package install.
reviews.skip_if: Small React or Preact sites where a tiny router is enough: issue 7090 reports a 29 KB increase in one Solid build.

reviews.name: kilocode
reviews.verdict: Our install completed in 80 seconds, but it pulled 1,964 packages and the root test command failed by design after 18 seconds.
reviews.skip_if: Teams expecting a small, easy-to-audit dependency, the checkout is large and the install footprint is heavy Anyone who expects a root-level test command to validate the whole monorepo, it deliberately exits with an error Users unwilling to trust an agent…

reviews.name: eino
reviews.verdict: Our Eino run built in 45 seconds and passed all 90 tests in 92 seconds, so the measured v0.9.15 commit earns a serious trial for Go-native agent work.
reviews.skip_if: Python or TypeScript teams that do not want a Go service boundary: Eino's public framework is written for Go.

reviews.name: cognee
reviews.verdict: Our Cognee install consumed 1,126 MB and its tests were still unfinished at the 900-second cap, so adopting it means budgeting for a large, moving system rather than a small memory helper.
reviews.skip_if: Buyers who need the single-Postgres graph backend under the same open license for production: the README labels the open implementation a demo and points production users to a licensed product.

reviews.name: tinygrad
reviews.verdict: Our tinygrad run installed 137 packages and consumed 7,916 MB, then pytest finished with 125 failures and 75 errors, so the simple source install did not produce a ready contributor workstation.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that require a green test baseline in a plain Debian environment: our run ended with 125 failures and 75 collection or setup errors.

reviews.name: fireworks-open-eli5
reviews.verdict: Our Fireworks Open ELI5 run installed 0 packages and passed all 22 tests in 6 seconds, making it an easy trial for Codex or Claude Code users who need source-aware technical explainers.
reviews.skip_if: Writers wanting a free-form page builder: the skill supports four defined story grammars and validates their semantic contract.

reviews.name: FrontierAgent
reviews.verdict: Our FrontierAgent run passed 1,686 tests in 162 seconds after a 31-second install, making it a credible trial for technical users who want research and file work in one terminal agent.
reviews.skip_if: Users expecting a model to be included: the quick start requires an OpenAI-compatible endpoint and API key, while local serving adds SGLang and NVIDIA compatibility work.

reviews.name: ip-as-logo-skill
reviews.verdict: IP as Logo contains 1 instruction document and no executable generation or validation code, so its value rests entirely on the quality of its art direction.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that need vector masters, typography, lockups, or a full identity system: the skill produces square raster character images and explicitly avoids SVG fallback.

reviews.name: Pentest-Swarm-AI
reviews.verdict: Pentest Swarm AI is worth trying in a lab if you want to examine genuinely decentralized agent coordination, and its clean build plus passing test suite make that experiment easier to justify.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone scanning systems without explicit written authorization, because that can be illegal Teams seeking a proven replacement for an experienced penetration tester Buyers who need stable APIs, polished support, or a mature release history Operators unwilling to review scope, tool…

reviews.name: OpenBidKit_Yibiao
reviews.verdict: Our Yibiao run installed 721 packages in 62 seconds and built in 20 seconds, but npm audit found 32 known vulnerabilities and there was no test target.
reviews.skip_if: Procurement teams that require an automated regression suite and a clean dependency audit: our measured commit had no test script, and npm audit reported 32 known vulnerabilities.

reviews.name: buildwithclaude
reviews.verdict: Build with Claude is useful as a search layer and a starting point for teams already committed to Claude Code.
reviews.skip_if: Developers who want a small dependency footprint: our checkout used 879 MB after installing 925 packages.

reviews.name: CopilotKit
reviews.verdict: Our CopilotKit install took 275 seconds and 3,935 MB, then both the build and test commands exited 130, so adopting it means accepting a large, fast-moving platform rather than adding a small chat widget.
reviews.skip_if: Small apps that only need a text box and streamed tokens: our install pulled 4,602 packages and occupied 3,935 MB for a much wider platform.

reviews.name: stitch-skills
reviews.verdict: Use Stitch Skills if Google Stitch is already part of your workflow and you want Codex or another supported agent to carry designs into code with repeatable instructions.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone wanting a standalone visual design app, because this package depends on Google Stitch Teams unwilling to configure credentials, environment variables, and a remote MCP endpoint Buyers needing independently verified build or test results, because our sandbox could not run…

reviews.name: claude-quickstarts
reviews.verdict: Our Claude Quickstarts install added 34 packages in 16 seconds and built in 4 seconds, but it exposed no repository-wide test target, so this is reference code to dissect rather than a verified application base.
reviews.skip_if: Teams seeking one maintained starter with one setup path: the repository contains separate Python and TypeScript applications with different prerequisites.

reviews.name: FastVideo
reviews.verdict: Our FastVideo install took 96 seconds, consumed 6,659 MB, and reached 0 runnable tests because pytest hit 138 collection or setup errors.
reviews.skip_if: CPU-only Linux and Windows users: the documented local paths target NVIDIA CUDA, while the non-NVIDIA route is for Apple Silicon through MLX.

reviews.name: OBLITERATUS
reviews.verdict: Our OBLITERATUS run passed 2,328 tests but failed 3, including a CUDA contract and a UI path assertion, so it is a serious research workbench with unfinished environment edges.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone who cannot independently safety-test the output: the README says produced models have had safety guardrails removed and makes the operator responsible for their use.

reviews.name: autonomous-os
reviews.verdict: Our Autonomous OS checkout installed 65 packages and passed all 34 tests, which makes the Go core unusually easy to evaluate for a robot stack of this size.
reviews.skip_if: Laptop-only contributors expecting a complete simulator: issue 250 says HAL simulation works, but the server plus an agent runtime have not been proven off-device.

reviews.name: modular
reviews.verdict: Our Modular checkout built in 11 seconds, but the 1,150,824-line repository offered no lab test target, so that result is an entry check rather than platform validation.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring one permissive license for the entire platform: repository code uses Apache 2.0 with LLVM Exceptions, while MAX usage and distribution follow the Modular Community License.

reviews.name: anime-find
reviews.verdict: Our anime-find run installed 50 packages and passed all 102 tests in 5 seconds, making it a credible small add-on for an existing DeepSeek Harness Web setup.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone who does not already use DeepSeek Harness Web: anime-find is a plugin and has no standalone interface or command-line search mode.

reviews.name: letta-code
reviews.verdict: Our Letta Code run installed 593 Bun packages in 82 seconds and built in 19 seconds, but no test target was available to confirm its memory, hooks, channels, or scheduling behavior.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that require all state to remain local: the documented remote environments, cross-machine secrets, browser access, and shared cloud agents require signing in with Letta.

reviews.name: TauriTavern
reviews.verdict: Our TauriTavern install finished in 16 seconds and 910 Node tests passed, but the native build failed on missing `gdk-3.0` and the overall test command still exited 101.
reviews.skip_if: Users who depend on SillyTavern's Node-only backend plugins: the README explicitly says those extensions are unsupported.

reviews.name: deepseek-harness-orange-book
reviews.verdict: Use this if you read Chinese and want to understand what DeepSeek Harness actually does on a machine before trusting it with files, tools, or money.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone needing a full English edition, because only a short English summary is provided Teams seeking stable, vendor-maintained reference documentation Readers who only want the Harness source code or a ready-to-run package Buyers who need long-term benchmarks across versions, since…

reviews.name: pi-from-scratch
reviews.verdict: Our PI from Scratch run installed 54 packages in 11 seconds, then passed its 9-second build and 25-second test run.
reviews.skip_if: English-only readers: the README, two tutorial chapters, interface text, and most code comments are in Chinese, with no English tutorial in the repository.

reviews.name: Retrieval-based-Voice-Conversion-WebUI
reviews.verdict: Our RVC run installed 35 packages in 12 seconds and built in 4 seconds, but the checkout supplied no automated test target, so that speed is not evidence that training or conversion is correct.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone seeking text-to-speech: RVC transforms an existing vocal performance and does not generate speech from text.

reviews.name: cua
reviews.verdict: Our Cua root run installed only 2 packages in 11 seconds, then found no build or test target, so it validated a thin pnpm surface rather than this 4,255-file cross-OS platform.
reviews.skip_if: Developers expecting one small package to represent the whole project: the README describes separate drivers, SDKs, benchmarks, servers, and virtualization tools with different setup paths.

reviews.name: mlx-audio
reviews.verdict: Our MLX-Audio run built in 13 seconds, but only 29 of 194 test outcomes passed before `libmlx.so` failures dominated the unsupported Debian environment.
reviews.skip_if: Linux or Windows deployments: the README requires an Apple Silicon Mac, and our Debian test collection stopped because `libmlx.so` was unavailable.

reviews.name: awesome-gpt-image-2
reviews.verdict: Our awesome-gpt-image-2 run passed all 28 tests after a 55-second install, but npm audit found 4 high-severity vulnerabilities in the installed tree.
reviews.skip_if: Commercial teams assuming every gallery asset is cleared for reuse: the disclaimer says third-party commercial rights are not guaranteed and must be obtained separately.

reviews.name: VidBee
reviews.verdict: Our VidBee install pulled 1,400 packages and occupied 1,579 MB, then built in 17 seconds with no test target available, so this is a capable trial with a large trust gap.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone who needs downloads from every advertised site to work consistently: current issues show HTTP 403 or extractor failures for Rumble, YouTube, TikTok, and Instagram.

reviews.name: CLI-Anything
reviews.verdict: Our CLI-Hub build passed in 11 seconds, but 7 of 164 tests failed because analytics code could not determine a home directory in the sandbox.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone expecting generated code to be trustworthy without review: the README says weaker models can produce incomplete or incorrect CLIs and repeated refinement may be needed.

reviews.name: scientific-agent-skills
reviews.verdict: Our build finished in 8 seconds, but the 14-second test run could not collect 105 skills together because their script modules collide, so buyers should validate the exact subset they install.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone expecting the agent to make clinical decisions: the README limits health skills to research, aggregate analysis, and drafts for qualified review.

reviews.name: claurst
reviews.verdict: Our npm-path install used 35 MB and reported 0 vulnerabilities, but it exposed no build or test target and therefore supplied no evidence about the Rust agent.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that require a production-stable agent: the README labels v0.1.7 beta and marks sharing, free mode, goals, and ultracode experimental.

reviews.name: next-ai-draw-io
reviews.verdict: Our install consumed 2,041 MB and npm audit found 35 known vulnerabilities, including 1 critical and 25 high, even though the 48-second build and 9-second tests passed.
reviews.skip_if: Public or sensitive deployments that cannot accept unresolved security exposure: open reports cover unauthenticated SSRF in `/api/parse-url` and stored XSS in the MCP server history flow.

reviews.name: freebuff
reviews.verdict: Freebuff is an appealing low-cost way to test capable coding agents across several interfaces, but the price is paid through limits, ads, and data-use terms rather than an API bill.
reviews.skip_if: Organizations that cannot allow prompts or pasted content to influence ad personalization: the README says Freebuff may analyze them for that purpose.

reviews.name: BrowserOS
reviews.verdict: Our BrowserOS package install took 35 seconds and pip-audit found 0 known vulnerabilities, but the build exited 1 after 6 seconds and no tests ran.
reviews.skip_if: Linux users who specifically want BrowserOS neo: the README supports neo on macOS and Windows, and Linux support remains an open request.

reviews.name: holaOS
reviews.verdict: Our holaOS install consumed 3,425 MB for 2,035 packages, then built in 73 seconds while the workspace test command still exited 1, so this is a substantial desktop platform with unfinished verification edges.
reviews.skip_if: Vendors planning to resell, host, or embed the source in a commercial product without a separate license: the modified Apache terms prohibit those uses by default.

reviews.name: OpenKB
reviews.verdict: Our OpenKB run installed 132 packages and built successfully, but 104 of 1,079 tests failed and 4 more ended in collection or setup errors, so it is a promising research tool rather than a safe unattended knowledge pipeline.
reviews.skip_if: Teams backfilling a dense archive: issue 203 reports that repeatedly rewriting growing pages made a roughly 1,100-document corpus impractical and approximated quadratic work.

reviews.name: LTX-2
reviews.verdict: Our LTX-2 checkout installed 34 packages and built in 33 seconds combined, but it provided no test target and did not exercise the roughly 66 GiB model set.
reviews.skip_if: Developers looking for a CPU-friendly local generator: the quick start downloads roughly 66 GiB of weights and documents CUDA optimization or CPU and disk offload for memory pressure.

reviews.name: KrillinAI
reviews.verdict: Our KrillinAI run fetched 239 packages, built in 35 seconds, and then finished with 12 passing and 3 failing Go package results, so the pipeline is buildable but did not clear its own tests in our sandbox.
reviews.skip_if: Editors who need broadcast-ready output without review: issue 291 reports malformed LLM JSON causing missing translations or poor sentence splits.

reviews.name: needle
reviews.verdict: Our Needle run installed 66 packages and built successfully, but 1 of 40 tests failed because the schema test could not import `pydantic`.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that need a turnkey Swift SDK today: open issue #92 asks for one, while the README documents the Python package and downloadable engine targets.

reviews.name: screenpipe
reviews.verdict: Our Screenpipe install pulled 1,144 packages, then the 846-second build and 278-second test run both stopped because `libpipewire-0.3` was unavailable.
reviews.skip_if: Commercial users assuming source access grants open-source rights: the README says commercial use requires a license.

reviews.name: sdnext
reviews.verdict: Our SD.Next frontend installed 591 packages and built in 29 seconds combined, but the test command failed in 6 seconds because no Python virtual environment existed.
reviews.skip_if: Users expecting the pnpm workflow to produce a runnable server: our tests stopped because the required Python `venv` did not exist.

reviews.name: BabelDOC
reviews.verdict: Our BabelDOC environment built in 8 seconds and pip-audit found 0 known vulnerabilities, but Pytest discovered 0 tests and exited 5, so source-level confidence must come from your own PDF fixtures.
reviews.skip_if: End users expecting support for the standalone CLI: the README calls it a debugging interface and directs self-hosters to PDFMathTranslate-next.

reviews.name: agent-governance-toolkit
reviews.verdict: Our measured Antigravity CLI subproject installed 7 packages and passed 22 tests, but npm audit found 2 high-severity vulnerabilities, so even the small path needs dependency review before use.
reviews.skip_if: Windows teams relying on the Claude Code plugin today: issue 3831 reports that governance hooks never fired while status still showed enforce mode, leaving no audit log or enforcement.

reviews.name: deer-flow
reviews.verdict: Our DeerFlow backend installed 33 packages and built in 16 seconds, but pytest ran 0 tests and stopped after 200 collection or setup errors, so commit 13f0a7f is a trial candidate rather than a verified deployment.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone planning to expose the default instance directly to a LAN or the internet: the README says it is designed for a trusted localhost environment and warns that unauthorized users could trigger commands or file operations.

reviews.name: opensrc
reviews.verdict: Our opensrc run installed 536 packages and occupied 851 MB, then built in 45 seconds but failed its 6-second test step because a workspace reported missing `node_modules`.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that cannot expose third-party source text to an autonomous agent: issue 59 raises the unresolved risk of prompt instructions embedded in code comments.

reviews.name: openscience
reviews.verdict: Our OpenScience test command was still running at the 900-second cap after an 81-second successful build, so adopting this workbench means budgeting for a large and slow-moving verification surface.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone requiring a completely account-free first launch: the README says normal use links a free Synthetic Sciences account and stores a revocable device credential.

reviews.name: Hyper-Extract
reviews.verdict: Our Hyper-Extract run installed 118 packages and built successfully, but 4 of 318 pytest cases failed because `langchain_anthropic` could not be imported.
reviews.skip_if: Teams expecting deterministic extraction without output checks: open issue #78 says one failed graph chunk can still abort graph-family parsing paths.

reviews.name: byterover-cli
reviews.verdict: Our ByteRover run passed all 8,910 tests, but installing it pulled 1,673 packages and npm audit found 46 known vulnerabilities, including 16 high-severity findings.
reviews.skip_if: Companies planning to resell ByteRover as a hosted service: Elastic License 2.0 forbids providing a substantial set of its features as a managed service.

reviews.name: emdash
reviews.verdict: Our Emdash checkout built in 170 seconds and Vitest reported 331 passing tests, yet the overall 500-second test task exited 1 with `@emdash/core:test` named as failed.
reviews.skip_if: Repositories with hundreds of worktrees until issue 2987 is resolved: its reporter measured about 250 concurrent Git queries and a load average above 200.

reviews.name: ccg-workflow
reviews.verdict: Our CCG run installed 617 packages and passed its build and tests in 34 seconds combined, so the repository is straightforward to verify even though the installed workflow is broad.
reviews.skip_if: Developers using another editor or agent as the primary interface: the default engine requires Claude Code, and Codex-led mode has current hook trouble in issue 136.

reviews.name: whichllm
reviews.verdict: Our WhichLLM checkout could not install because its exact uv 0.11.33 requirement rejected the sandbox's uv 0.12.5 after 37 seconds.
reviews.skip_if: Buyers who need measured performance on their exact machine: the README says its speed range is a planning estimate, not a live benchmark.

reviews.name: superset
reviews.verdict: Our Superset checkout installed 3008 packages and occupied 5661 MB, then failed both its 244-second build and 49-second test step.
reviews.skip_if: Windows users: the README says a Windows build is not available.

reviews.name: oh-my-pi
reviews.verdict: Our Oh My Pi checkout pulled 412 packages and 1,517 MB, then its native build failed after 225 seconds and all 12 test files errored, so source contributors should use the pinned Nix environment before judging the code.
reviews.skip_if: Developers who want a narrow prompt-and-patch tool: the README exposes shells, debuggers, browsers, desktop control, memory, collaboration, MCP, and provider routing in one product.

reviews.name: ai-agents-for-beginners
reviews.verdict: Our run installed 172 packages and 1,301 MB in 207 seconds, then built in 18 seconds but failed before any test ran because `demo_tool_agent` was missing during collection.
reviews.skip_if: Complete AI beginners: the README sends first-time generative AI builders to a separate 21-lesson prerequisite course.

reviews.name: Prompt-Engineering-Guide
reviews.verdict: Our Prompt Engineering Guide build took 224 seconds after installing 551 packages, while npm audit reported 26 vulnerabilities and the repository offered no test target.
reviews.skip_if: Teams seeking an executable evaluation framework: the repository has no test script or tests directory, and our lab skipped tests.

reviews.name: open-design
reviews.verdict: Our OpenDesign install pulled 1,293 packages and used 2,644 MB, then exposed no root build or test target.
reviews.skip_if: Product teams needing multiplayer vector editing, component inspection, and designer handoff like Figma or Penpot: OpenDesign produces agent-written files and rendered artifacts, not a shared vector canvas.

reviews.name: ragflow
reviews.verdict: RAGFlow is a strong candidate when document parsing and chunk inspection are central to the product, and the team wants a usable interface as well as APIs.
reviews.skip_if: Developers seeking a lightweight library inside an existing app: the documented deployment is a multi-service system with substantial CPU, memory, disk, and operational requirements.

reviews.name: new-api
reviews.verdict: Our New API run installed 828 packages and built in 8 seconds, but 1 of 34 tested packages failed, so adopt it only if you can investigate the suite and operate the gateway as infrastructure.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that cannot comply with the AGPL-3.0 license for a modified network service.

reviews.name: prompts.chat
reviews.verdict: Our prompts.chat install stopped after 164 seconds because `DATABASE_URL` was required during postinstall, so the documented manual order does not work in a blank environment.
reviews.skip_if: Teams expecting a static prompt list with no services: self-hosting requires Node.js 24.x and PostgreSQL.

reviews.name: AutoGPT
reviews.verdict: Our AutoGPT Classic run passed 277 of 380 tests, failed 65, hit 38 setup or collection errors, and exposed 55 known vulnerabilities, matching the maintainers' warning that Classic is unsupported.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone planning to deploy AutoGPT Classic: its own README says the experiment is unsupported, dependencies will not be updated, and known vulnerabilities remain.

reviews.name: orca
reviews.verdict: Our Orca checkout installed 1,265 packages and used 2,452 MB, then type checking was killed after 108 seconds and tests exceeded 900 seconds, so source contribution is a serious workstation workload.
reviews.skip_if: Contributors with a small machine or tight CI budget: our install used 2,452 MB, type checking ended in SIGKILL, and tests hit 900 seconds.

reviews.name: sub2api
reviews.verdict: Our run passed all 48 Go tests, but Sub2API's own README warns that relaying subscription access may breach upstream terms, so technical readiness does not settle whether you should deploy it.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone planning to resell consumer subscription capacity without provider approval: the README says this use may violate upstream terms and says the developers have not authorized commercial operation.

reviews.name: oh-my-claudecode
reviews.verdict: Our run installed 326 packages and built successfully, but 38 of 12,127 tests failed and npm audit found 14 vulnerabilities, so oh-my-claudecode is best treated as a powerful local operator that needs review before adoption.
reviews.skip_if: Developers who do not use Claude Code: the README lists Claude Code as a requirement, and the in-session workflows depend on it.

reviews.name: CLIProxyAPI
reviews.verdict: Our CLIProxyAPI build took 155 seconds, but 2 of 58 test packages failed, so it belongs behind a careful compatibility trial before it carries daily coding traffic.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that cannot store provider OAuth credentials on the gateway: the documented account flows and multi-account routing depend on those files.

reviews.name: cherry-studio
reviews.verdict: Our Cherry Studio install consumed 3,552 MB, the build failed on a missing DSH bridge module, and tests were still running at the 900-second cap.
reviews.skip_if: Contributors who need a clean source build from the measured commit: TypeScript could not resolve `@cherrystudio/dsh-bridge` in our run.

reviews.name: taste-skill
reviews.verdict: Taste Skill is an essential, brilliantly conceived tool for anyone serious about using AI to generate front-end code.
reviews.skip_if: Developers who need pixel-perfect, deterministic control over their UI; this is a guide for an LLM, not a traditional component library.

reviews.name: claude-mem
reviews.verdict: Our Claude-Mem checkout used 1,149 MB and built in 7 seconds, but its test script stopped after 5 seconds because Bun was missing, so this is a substantial local service with an unverified lab suite.
reviews.skip_if: Users seeking a small plugin with no background stack: our install added 799 packages and 1,149 MB, while the runtime uses Bun, a worker service, SQLite, and Chroma through Python tooling.

reviews.name: hermes-agent
reviews.verdict: Hermes is compelling for an experienced self-hoster who wants one agent to persist across a terminal, a server, and messaging apps.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone who cannot safely grant an AI shell and filesystem access: Hermes can execute commands, write files, schedule unattended work, and talk through remote messaging channels.

reviews.name: unstract
reviews.verdict: Our Unstract build passed in 14 seconds, but its test command collected no runnable tests because 2 suites stopped on a missing `yaml` module.
reviews.skip_if: Developers who only need PDF-to-text or Markdown: Unstract also runs a frontend, Django backend, workers, FastAPI service, Redis, RabbitMQ, and PostgreSQL.

reviews.name: Auto-claude-code-research-in-sleep
reviews.verdict: Our Feishu bridge run installed 43 packages and built in 33 seconds combined, but pytest collected 0 tests and exited 5.
reviews.skip_if: Researchers who cannot inspect generated code and claims before using them: the full pipeline can write scripts, run experiments, rewrite a paper, and continue at selection checkpoints when `AUTO_PROCEED=true`.

reviews.name: n8n-mcp
reviews.verdict: Our n8n-MCP run installed 2,761 packages and passed 6,387 of 6,660 tests, while 220 failed and npm audit reported 133 known vulnerabilities.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone planning to let an agent edit production workflows unattended: the README explicitly says to copy, back up, test, and validate workflows first.
