reviews.name: gpt-researcher
reviews.verdict: Our GPT Researcher run installed 230 packages and passed 398 of 412 tests, but the build and full test step both ended with exit code 1.
reviews.skip_if: Buyers expecting research without paid provider credentials: the quick start requires OpenAI and Tavily keys, while other provider choices still need configuration.

reviews.name: composio
reviews.verdict: Our Composio checkout installed 910 packages and occupied 2,280 MB, then both build and tests failed because Bun was missing.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that require the action layer to run entirely on their own infrastructure: the quickstart requires a Composio API key, and MCP sessions use a hosted endpoint.

reviews.name: nacos
reviews.verdict: Our Nacos console build completed in 48 seconds, but it installed 1,399 packages and npm audit found 99 vulnerabilities, including 40 critical or high.
reviews.skip_if: Small AI projects that only need an MCP server list: Nacos brings a 6,491-file service-management platform and a large console dependency tree.

reviews.name: PDFMathTranslate
reviews.verdict: Our PDFMathTranslate run built in 13 seconds, but tests ended with 3 failures and 5 errors while pip-audit found 45 vulnerabilities, so this checkout is suitable for supervised evaluation rather than blind document processing.
reviews.skip_if: Workflows that require a green dependency and test baseline: our run found 45 known vulnerabilities, 3 failed tests, and 5 collection or setup errors.

reviews.name: ai-engineering-from-scratch
reviews.verdict: Our install consumed 5,609 MB across 204 packages and the repository exposed no unified test target, so this is a serious study archive rather than a tidy course package.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone wanting a short introduction: the README lists 511 lessons across 20 phases and about 329 hours.

reviews.name: TrendRadar
reviews.verdict: Our TrendRadar install pulled 119 packages, and pip-audit found 25 known vulnerabilities, so adoption requires active dependency review from day one.
reviews.skip_if: English-only operators who need every instruction and support thread in English: translated docs exist, but the main README, changelog, and most issue discussion are Chinese.

reviews.name: Scrapling
reviews.verdict: Our Scrapling run installed in 24 seconds and passed 258 tests, but 5 failed and 110 more hit setup errors, with the log showing `curl_cffi` was missing.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that only parse stable HTML already fetched elsewhere: Beautiful Soup or Parsel has a smaller dependency and behavior surface.

reviews.name: cc-switch
reviews.verdict: Our CC Switch install failed after 11 seconds because its pnpm configuration set two conflicting built-dependency policies, so we could not reach a build or test result.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone who wants a source install that works in a clean pnpm environment today: our install stopped after 11 seconds on conflicting built-dependency settings.

reviews.name: ECC
reviews.verdict: ECC makes sense for a heavy Claude Code user who wants one maintained opinion about planning, verification, memory, and agent roles.
reviews.skip_if: Developers who prefer a small, inspectable instruction set: ECC spans thousands of files and roughly a quarter-million source lines.

reviews.name: aider
reviews.verdict: Our Aider run passed 473 tests, but 10 failed, 9 ended in setup errors, and pip-audit reported 126 known vulnerabilities after a 772 MB install.
reviews.skip_if: Security-sensitive teams that cannot review dependency advisories: our pip audit reported 126 known vulnerabilities in the installed environment.

reviews.name: claude-code
reviews.verdict: Claude Code offers a compelling vision for the future of AI development in the terminal, with a slick setup and powerful agentic features.
reviews.skip_if: Corporate or enterprise developers, as the 'license unknown' status makes it legally unusable for most companies.

reviews.name: Archon
reviews.verdict: Our build finished in 59 seconds, but the full test command ended with 26 failures after 353 seconds.
reviews.skip_if: Developers wanting a model-independent, zero-configuration coding assistant, because the documented setup depends on Claude Code Teams that need a proven clean test run before adoption, because our sandbox run ended with 26 failing core tests Small projects where a shell…

reviews.name: link-cli

reviews.name: karpenter
reviews.verdict: Our Karpenter run installed 204 packages and built successfully, but only 15 of 25 test suites passed before Go exited 1 after 88 seconds.
reviews.skip_if: Teams looking for a standalone controller: the README calls this a multi-cloud core and directs users to separate provider implementations.

reviews.name: ongrid
reviews.verdict: Our Ongrid run built in 104 seconds and passed all 117 discovered tests, which supports a serious read-only pilot for a Linux fleet.
reviews.skip_if: Teams ready to permit autonomous production changes: open issue 337 says shell redirection and compound syntax could bypass the proposal and confirmation path when write actions were enabled.

reviews.name: sim

reviews.name: OpenMausBot

reviews.name: md2wechat-skill

reviews.skip_if: English-only teams: the README and linked user guides are Chinese, with no full English usage guide listed.

reviews.name: midscene
reviews.verdict: Our Midscene checkout built in 13 seconds, but its 2,236-package install used 2,057 MB and the full test target exited 1 despite 88 reported passes and 0 failed cases.

reviews.name: spiderfoot

reviews.skip_if: Anyone scanning targets without clear authorization: modules include port scans, DNS brute force, bucket discovery, breach searches, and external tool calls.

reviews.name: paperclip
reviews.verdict: Our Paperclip build passed in 121 seconds, but its test command was still running when our 900-second limit expired.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone managing one occasional agent: Paperclip's own README says a single agent probably does not need it.

reviews.name: k-skill

reviews.skip_if: English-only users: the main README, catalogue, and linked feature guides are primarily Korean and no English README is offered.

reviews.name: MinerU

reviews.name: crawl4ai

reviews.skip_if: Teams expecting a small dependency footprint: our install used 5,368 MB for 158 packages.

reviews.name: SpacetimeDB

reviews.name: developer-portfolios

reviews.skip_if: Readers seeking a small editorial selection of the best portfolios: the README lists 1,949 entries alphabetically without ratings or design analysis.

reviews.name: ai-data-extraction
reviews.verdict: Our sandbox installed 35 packages and passed all 6 tests in 19 seconds combined, so the code is cheap to inspect and trial.
reviews.skip_if: Organizations that need a clear reuse license: GitHub reported no repository license when we fetched the project.

reviews.name: timesfm
reviews.verdict: Our TimesFM run passed 26 tests with 0 assertion failures, but 6 modules could not collect because `pandas` was missing and the audit found 5 known vulnerabilities.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that need an officially supported Google product: the README says the open release is not one and points support-sensitive users toward Google products such as BigQuery ML.

reviews.name: chinese-poetry-api
reviews.verdict: Our Chinese Poetry API build passed in 66 seconds, but 1 of 2 test groups failed because the SQLite runtime lacked FTS5.
reviews.skip_if: English-only operators: the README, Makefile help, release notes, and issue discussion are primarily Chinese.

reviews.name: lancedb
reviews.verdict: Our LanceDB build ran for 806 seconds and failed because `-lpython3.11` was missing, then the test command hit the same linker error after 758 seconds, so this source checkout did not clear either gate.
reviews.skip_if: Contributors expecting the root Rust workspace to build in a plain toolchain image: our build and test commands both stopped because the linker could not find `-lpython3.11`.

reviews.name: check-if-email-exists
reviews.verdict: Our run built in 311 seconds and passed all 33 Rust tests, so the code is a credible base for teams that understand SMTP verification.
reviews.skip_if: Applications that need a guaranteed yes or no for every mailbox: the API explicitly returns `safe`, `risky`, `invalid`, or `unknown`.

reviews.name: drawdb
reviews.verdict: Our drawDB build finished in 7 seconds with 0 audit findings, but installing its 1,890 packages used 618 MB and no test target checked SQL round trips.
reviews.skip_if: Teams needing built-in collaboration from the frontend alone: the README requires the separate drawDB server and environment variables for sharing.

reviews.name: Legendary_OSINT
reviews.verdict: Legendary_OSINT is a well-organized and highly useful directory for discovering intelligence-gathering tools.
reviews.skip_if: Users looking for a single, installable software package; this is a list of links, not a program.

reviews.name: pdf-inspector
reviews.verdict: Our PDF Inspector run passed 100 of 101 tests, with the lone failure raising an encrypted-PDF error after a 474-second install.
reviews.skip_if: Pipelines that must accept encrypted PDFs without a separate password and fallback path: our fixture test raised `ValueError: PDF is encrypted`.

reviews.name: context-engineering-kit
reviews.verdict: Our Reflexion hook install added 59 packages in 35 seconds, then all 41 tests passed in 7 seconds, so that executable slice is easy to trial and has a working check.
reviews.skip_if: Codex, Cursor, and OpenCode users expecting the same subagent workflows as Claude Code: the README says the shared skills installer cannot provide the full experience.

reviews.name: folly
reviews.verdict: Our build completed in 7 seconds, but the test step ended with 2 collection errors and zero tests executed.
reviews.skip_if: Beginners who want a small, conventional C++ utility library Teams that require ABI stability across upgrades Projects wanting a dependency-light, package-manager-first setup Python users expecting the repository's Python subtree to work as a standalone package without extra integration

reviews.name: try-omarchy
reviews.verdict: Our Try Omarchy run installed 35 packages and built in 3 seconds, but 1 of 30 tests failed when a generated Python cache entered an overlay.
reviews.skip_if: Intel Mac, Windows, or Linux users: the README requires an Apple Silicon Mac running macOS 15 or newer.

reviews.name: luvus
reviews.verdict: Our Luvus build passed in 77 seconds and 1,838 of 1,840 tests passed, but the 2 failures make copy-mode and viewport behavior worth retesting before daily use.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that require a completely green checkout: our run passed 1,838 tests but failed 2, including a copy-mode viewport case.

reviews.name: argent
reviews.verdict: Our Argent run installed 501 packages, built in 30 seconds, and exposed 11 known vulnerabilities while providing no test target, so it needs a security and behavior review before an agent touches a real app.
reviews.skip_if: Organizations requiring every distributed component under an open-source license: the README says several simulator, accessibility, and native-devtools binaries are proprietary and restricted.

reviews.name: plannotator
reviews.verdict: Our Plannotator install pulled 1,031 packages and 2,263 MB, then build and test both stopped because Bun was missing, so source contributors must treat the Bun toolchain as a hard prerequisite.
reviews.skip_if: Source contributors without Bun on the build path: both our build and test commands exited 127 with `bun: not found`.

reviews.name: beads
reviews.verdict: Our Beads run installed 668 packages and built in 162 seconds, but 17 of 150 test groups failed after 464 seconds.
reviews.skip_if: Teams wanting a conventional web issue tracker with permissions and a polished shared UI: Beads is CLI-first and lists UIs as community tools.

reviews.name: ipatool
reviews.verdict: Our ipatool run built in 46 seconds, but only 4 of 15 package test results passed before 11 build failures, so unattended use needs its own recovery checks.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone trying to download paid apps they do not own: the FAQ says the Apple account must already hold a license.

reviews.name: traycer
reviews.verdict: Our Traycer run installed 1,828 packages and built in 59 seconds, but its test command was still running when our 900-second cap ended it despite thousands of passing assertions already printed.
reviews.skip_if: Organizations requiring a fully self-hosted collaboration control plane: this repository documents open clients, CLI, and protocol, while account sync and team services depend on Traycer.

reviews.name: gitbutler
reviews.verdict: Our GitButler install failed after 9 seconds before it produced a build or test result, so source contributors should expect to fix the runtime and pnpm configuration before judging the code.
reviews.skip_if: Companies building a competing Git client or service: the FSL-1.1-MIT license bars competing use until each version reaches its two-year conversion date.

reviews.name: claude-plugins-community
reviews.verdict: Use this marketplace when you want broad Claude plugin choice and are prepared to inspect each plugin before installation.
reviews.skip_if: Authors who want to submit or fix a listing with a normal pull request: the README says direct pull requests are closed automatically and submissions must use Anthropic's form.

reviews.name: security-audit-skill
reviews.verdict: Use this skill when you already trust your coding agent with a repository and want a disciplined, adversarial workflow for finding new bugs that scanners may miss.
reviews.skip_if: Agent hosts without reliable parallel subagents: the README makes them a requirement, and issue #11 reports that Antigravity terminates the parallel workers.

reviews.name: nodeterm
reviews.verdict: Our nodeterm build passed in 38 seconds, but 36 of 8,973 tests failed, so the packaged app is easier to recommend for a trial than the current checkout is for contribution.
reviews.skip_if: Windows users who need a native desktop build: published downloads cover macOS and x64 Linux.

reviews.name: DSH-better-sidebar
reviews.verdict: Our DSH Better Sidebar install stopped after 8 seconds inside pnpm, so the source checkout never reached a build or test on our box.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone not already using a supported DSH release: this is a plugin, not a standalone editor or web IDE.

reviews.name: fscan
reviews.verdict: Our fscan run built in 47 seconds and passed all 21 tests in 136 seconds, so the checked Go code has a clean baseline.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone without written authorization for every target: the tool includes password attempts, command execution, persistence, credential access, and trace-cleaning modules.

reviews.name: dsh-anchored-standard
reviews.verdict: Our dsh-anchored-standard run needed 0 installed packages and passed all 205 tests in 9 seconds, but its current generic preset has no matching 98/99 benchmark.
reviews.skip_if: Teams seeking an actively evaluated preset: the maintainer says active development stopped on August 17, 2026 and only feasible maintenance remains.

reviews.name: cli-printing-press
reviews.verdict: Our CLI Printing Press build passed after 176 seconds, but the 614-second test run finished with 22 packages passing and 2 failing.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone expecting a small OpenAPI code generator: the repository spans research, browser traffic capture, generation, scoring, dogfooding, publishing, and a public CLI library.

reviews.name: gortex
reviews.verdict: Our Gortex run spent 271 seconds building and 596 seconds testing before 80 of 81 test groups passed, so this is a substantial code-intelligence system with one unresolved lab failure.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that require every literal search to be complete: issue 672 shows `search_text` silently capping results and reporting the cap as the count.

reviews.name: zero
reviews.verdict: Our npm-path run installed 83 packages in 10 seconds, exposed no build or test target, and reported 2 moderate vulnerabilities.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that require a small, settled codebase: our checkout contained about 384,283 source lines, and GitHub listed 115 combined issues and pull requests.

reviews.name: atlas
reviews.verdict: Our Atlas build completed in 55 seconds and its tests passed in 14 seconds after a 958-package, 1,271 MB install.
reviews.skip_if: Linux or Windows users expecting supported binaries: the README says those platforms build from the same Tauri codebase but remain untested.

reviews.name: deepsec
reviews.verdict: Our Deepsec run built in 58 seconds and passed 2,379 of 2,411 tests, but one assertion failed, so the codebase is close to green rather than clean at commit a008d3e.
reviews.skip_if: Teams looking for predictable low-cost scanning: the README says large-codebase runs can cost thousands or tens of thousands of dollars at high thinking levels.

reviews.name: bilibili-video-downloader
reviews.verdict: Our run installed 385 packages in 18 seconds and built in 28 seconds, but the project supplied no automated test target for its 22,766 lines of source.
reviews.skip_if: Users who need English setup and support documentation: the README, issue titles, and contribution guidance are primarily Chinese Anyone unwilling to trust Bilibili session access to a desktop app: account features use cookie or QR-code login for favorites, history, watch-later…

reviews.name: mubeng
reviews.verdict: Our Mubeng run built in 47 seconds and passed all 3 tests in 17 seconds, so trying the 1.2 MB checkout is cheap.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone who needs a SOCKS listener: the README says rotation is exposed only through an HTTP proxy, even when upstream entries use SOCKS.

reviews.name: iii
reviews.verdict: Our iii run installed 820 packages, then produced 0 successful build tasks and repeated the same docs failure during the test command, so platform teams should trial the runtime from a pinned release before standardizing on it.
reviews.skip_if: Organizations requiring every runtime component under Apache-2.0 or another approved open-source license: the engine uses Elastic License 2.0, while the SDKs and console use Apache-2.0.

reviews.name: OpenCADStudio
reviews.verdict: Our Open CAD Studio build took 459 seconds and succeeded, but its tests stopped after 71 seconds because `mesh_from_solid` was missing during test compilation.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone who cannot risk a drawing being misread or damaged: the README explicitly says to keep backups of important production drawings.

reviews.name: Lighthouse
reviews.verdict: Our Lighthouse checkout installed in 15 seconds and built in 5 seconds, but pytest collected 0 tests, so the source passed compilation without giving us an automated gameplay safety net.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone without a legally obtained supported Banjo-Kazooie ROM: Lighthouse ships no copyrighted assets and cannot generate its game archive without one.

reviews.name: aisuite
reviews.verdict: Our aisuite run installed 136 packages in 78 seconds, but 43 tests failed with repeated messages that async test functions were not natively supported.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that require automatic tool loops to behave identically across providers: open issue 369 reports that `max_turns` fails in different ways with Groq and Ollama.

reviews.name: opencode-mem
reviews.verdict: Our run installed 128 packages and 510 MB, then the build failed and 9 tests failed, so this commit is a trial candidate rather than a default recommendation.
reviews.skip_if: Users who do not want conversation content sent to another model: automatic capture and profile learning require an AI provider, even though manual memory operations can stay local.

reviews.name: adk-python
reviews.verdict: Our ADK install pulled 331 packages and used 1,696 MB, while pytest stopped at 200 collection or setup errors, so this is a serious framework that deserves a trial before adoption.
reviews.skip_if: Small scripts that only make one model call: ADK 2.0 brings agents, workflows, events, sessions, and a large dependency tree to a problem a model SDK may already solve.

reviews.name: CodexPlusPlus
reviews.verdict: Our Codex++ build failed after 212 seconds because its expected frontend `dist` directory was absent, and tests hit the same error after 78 seconds.
reviews.skip_if: Mac users who require signed and notarized software: the README says current unsigned builds may trigger Gatekeeper.

reviews.name: sf-skills
reviews.verdict: Our sf-skills checkout installed 248 packages in 20 seconds, but npm offered no build or test target for its 7,244 files.
reviews.skip_if: Commercial adopters who need unambiguous licensing before use: at commit 2476476, `LICENSE.txt` said Apache-2.0 while `package.json` declared CC-BY-NC-4.0, the mismatch tracked in issue 316.

reviews.name: dsh-desktop
reviews.verdict: Our DSH Desktop checkout built in 25 seconds and 770 of 776 tests passed after a 1,352-package install, leaving one lifecycle-evidence failure to investigate.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone assuming it is an official DeepSeek product: the README repeatedly says there is no affiliation, authorization, endorsement, or upstream staff participation.

reviews.name: NemoClaw
reviews.verdict: Our NemoClaw install pulled 387 packages in 47 seconds, but the 36-second test step failed because TypeScript could not resolve `json5` and `tar`.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring a stable support contract from the open repository: the README calls NemoClaw alpha and says responses are best effort.

reviews.name: munder-difflin
reviews.verdict: Our Munder Difflin build passed, but its 781-package install used 1,062 MB and npm audit found 28 vulnerabilities, including 1 critical and 23 high.
reviews.skip_if: Redistributors unwilling to preserve LimeZu credit: the code is MIT-licensed, but the bundled commercial-use pixel-art license separately requires attribution.

reviews.name: slime
reviews.verdict: Our slime run installed 191 packages and built successfully, but pytest finished with 26 failures and 29 errors after 392 seconds.
reviews.skip_if: Developers seeking a laptop RL tutorial: the quick start uses GPU containers, model and dataset downloads, Megatron conversion, Ray, and multi-GPU layouts.

reviews.name: omlx
reviews.verdict: Our oMLX environment occupied 5,842 MB and built in 8 seconds, but tests stopped after 7 seconds because `libmlx.so` could not be loaded on Debian.
reviews.skip_if: Linux, Windows, Intel Mac, or macOS 14 users: the documented target is Apple Silicon on macOS 15 or newer.

reviews.name: Automodel
reviews.verdict: Our AutoModel environment occupied 5,703 MB and 1,980 tests passed, but 153 failed and 47 hit collection/setup errors, so adoption requires a pinned recipe-specific environment rather than blind trust in the default checkout.
reviews.skip_if: CPU-only developers seeking a small fine-tuning package: our default install used 5,703 MB before any model weights, and useful recipes are built around GPU training.

reviews.name: baml
reviews.verdict: Our BAML checkout installed 2,528 packages and consumed 3,740 MB, then both build and test failed at the Python language-client task, so source contributors need more patience than the user quickstart suggests.
reviews.skip_if: Teams unwilling to add a language and generated-client step to their build: BAML functions live in `baml_src`, and generated client code is not meant to be edited.

reviews.name: omnigent
reviews.verdict: Our Omnigent checkout pulled 1,712 packages and used 2,086 MB, then offered no root build or test target, so adopting it means evaluating a large alpha platform beyond the quick-start path.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that require a stable production contract today: the README labels Omnigent alpha, and the repository had 1,207 combined issues and pull requests when fetched.

reviews.name: claude-obsidian
reviews.verdict: Our claude-obsidian run passed 458 of 463 tests but failed 5 after 579 seconds, so its careful write design did not produce a clean baseline at commit 1c1bc49.
reviews.skip_if: People seeking automatic PDF, EPUB, OCR, URL, or YouTube extraction: the README says several paths capture metadata only or require an external runner.

reviews.name: code-graph-rag
reviews.verdict: Our Code-Graph-RAG run installed 150 packages and built in 10 seconds, but pytest stopped at 200 Docker connection errors after only 24 passes, so Docker is a real prerequisite rather than an optional extra.
reviews.skip_if: Developers who cannot run Docker: the README requires it for Memgraph, and open issue #386 tracks an embedded alternative as unfinished work.

reviews.name: jcode
reviews.verdict: Our jcode run built in 660 seconds, then 5 of 231 tests failed, so this is an ambitious coding environment that still asks adopters to tolerate breakage at the edges.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone who requires a clean upstream test run before adoption: our checkout passed 226 tests but failed 5 provider, auth, report, and follow-up tests.

reviews.name: browser-use
reviews.verdict: Our Browser Use install occupied 535 MB, reported 19 known vulnerabilities, and never reached tests because pytest rejected a configured argument.
reviews.skip_if: Deterministic scraping or testing jobs with stable selectors: Playwright code is easier to assert, replay, and audit than model-selected clicks.

reviews.name: FlightScnr_Pi
reviews.verdict: Our FlightScnr Pi run installed 67 packages in 27 seconds and built in 6 seconds, but the repository gave us no test target to check.
reviews.skip_if: Commercial builders: the firmware uses CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, and commercial use needs separate permission.

reviews.name: jan
reviews.verdict: Our Jan checkout pulled 4,020 packages and 2,201 MB, then failed both its 35-second build and 120-second test command, so source adopters should wait for a clean run on their target branch.
reviews.skip_if: Source contributors who need a clean checkout to build immediately: our build failed on unresolved `@janhq/core` imports and TypeScript implicit-any errors.

reviews.name: openship
reviews.verdict: Our build completed in 122 seconds, but the full test command exited 1 after 370 seconds with 2 adapter failures in the log tail.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring a fully settled production platform, because v0.6.8 and 182 open issues signal ongoing change Operators unwilling to investigate test failures or maintain a large Node/Bun monorepo Anyone expecting the desktop app to host public apps directly on a…

reviews.name: evolution-go
reviews.verdict: Evolution Go has the better measured foundation of the two Evolution services in this batch: its pinned source installed, built, and passed all eight lab tests.
reviews.skip_if: Businesses that require Meta's official WhatsApp Cloud API and its policy framework: Evolution Go uses the unofficial whatsmeow web client.

reviews.name: bookorbit
reviews.verdict: Our BookOrbit install added 1,641 packages, and 10,645 of 10,668 tests passed before 15 Calibre-Web Automated snapshot tests failed.
reviews.skip_if: KOReader users who frequently replace or edit book files in Calibre: issue 926 reports that rescans can retain an old file hash and break matching.

reviews.name: openflight
reviews.verdict: Our OpenFlight run installed 58 packages and passed all 1,341 tests in 93 seconds combined, which is unusually strong software evidence for a DIY hardware project.
reviews.skip_if: Buyers who want calibrated spin and carry out of the box: the README calls spin experimental, excludes it from carry by default, and uses fallbacks when measurements are missing.

reviews.name: freehire
reviews.verdict: Our root check finished in 7 seconds but installed 0 packages and found no build or test target, so it says nothing about whether freehire's 7-service local stack starts cleanly.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone wanting a small personal application tracker: our checkout had 6,555 files and about 466,086 source lines across a catalogue, CV system, mail pipeline, assistant, extension, and many workers.

reviews.name: casdoor
reviews.verdict: Our Casdoor build succeeded in 158 seconds, but its Go test run passed 6 of 14 tests and failed 8, including an XLSX reader panic.
reviews.skip_if: Security teams that expect hiding a password method in the console to disable it at the API: issue 5761 says the backend ignores the rule and can still accept password login.

reviews.name: agent-sandbox
reviews.verdict: Our Agent Sandbox run built in 136 seconds, but 2 of 28 test groups failed because the end-to-end extension tests could not find `/work/repo/bin/KUBECONFIG`.
reviews.skip_if: Teams without a Kubernetes control plane: the install is a CRD and controller, and useful isolation also depends on a configured RuntimeClass Buyers expecting the controller itself to contain untrusted code: the README says it delegates kernel and network isolation…

reviews.name: harness
reviews.verdict: Our Harness run installed 799 packages, used 104 seconds for setup, and finished its 504-second test run with 87 of 88 passing, so this is a substantial platform with one unresolved measured failure.
reviews.skip_if: Operators unwilling to expose the Docker socket to the application: the documented pipeline setup mounts `/var/run/docker.sock`, which grants sensitive control over the host daemon.

reviews.name: dub
reviews.verdict: Our Dub install consumed 2,585 MB, the web build was killed after 296 seconds, and the Stripe app test task failed after 9 seconds, so self-hosting this repository is a platform project rather than a quick deployment.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone who only needs private short links: the self-hosting guide requires several databases, caches, storage services, authentication setup, and a deployment platform.

reviews.name: open-seo
reviews.verdict: Our OpenSEO run installed 984 packages, then passed a 67-second build and 36-second test step, making it the cleanest full repository run in this batch.
reviews.skip_if: Teams expecting self-hosting to eliminate outside data costs: every deployment requires DataForSEO credentials, and its setup guide states a $50 minimum top-up.

reviews.name: atomic
reviews.verdict: Our Atomic run passed install, build, and tests in 55 seconds total, but npm audit found 29 known vulnerabilities, including 19 at high or critical severity.
reviews.skip_if: Security-sensitive deployments that require a clean dependency audit before launch: our npm audit found 29 known vulnerabilities, including 3 critical and 16 high findings.

reviews.name: godoxy
reviews.verdict: Our GoDoxy run built in 77 seconds, but Go test finished with 42 of 49 packages failing at linker references.
reviews.skip_if: Environments that forbid host networking: the quick start explicitly says GoDoxy is designed for host network mode.

reviews.name: portmaster
reviews.verdict: Our Portmaster build completed in 67 seconds, but 6 of 52 Go package tests failed, so the current checkout does not earn blind trust at the layer that controls every network connection.
reviews.skip_if: macOS users: the README describes Portmaster as a Windows and Linux privacy suite.

reviews.name: JavBoss
reviews.verdict: Our JavBoss run installed 120 packages, built successfully, and passed all 13 tests, so the checked-out Go project cleared its basic engineering checks.
reviews.skip_if: English-only users: the README is Chinese, contains no English guide, and issue 186 reports that the English language selection disappeared after v1.9.0.

reviews.name: panel
reviews.verdict: Our documentation build installed 1,283 packages and exposed 69 known vulnerabilities, including 2 critical and 38 high-severity findings, so Remnawave deserves a security review before it manages real users.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone looking for a consumer VPN app: Remnawave manages infrastructure and subscriptions, while end users still need compatible client software.

reviews.name: donutbrowser
reviews.verdict: Our Donut Browser build passed in 48 seconds, but the test command exited 101 after 61 seconds despite 6 passing Node tests because the log ended on Xray-core checksum mismatches.
reviews.skip_if: Buyers who need a guarantee that fingerprinting defenses remain undetected: the README makes that claim, while issue 549 reports more Cloudflare blocking than expected.

reviews.name: kumone
reviews.verdict: Kumone requires macOS 15+ or a self-signed iOS 16+ installation, so its polished Apple experience comes with a narrow platform and unofficial-service boundary.
reviews.skip_if: Windows, Linux, or Android users: the distributed clients require macOS 15+ or iOS 16+.

reviews.name: threeui
reviews.verdict: Our ThreeUI run built in 33 seconds and passed all 25 tests, so the free package has credible release and boundary checks behind its polished catalog.
reviews.skip_if: Teams expecting the entire ThreeUI catalog under an open license: the README says Pro and Beta components are removed from this repository.

reviews.name: pdfcn
reviews.verdict: Our pdfcn install pulled 716 packages and used 729 MB, then its production build passed in 96 seconds, but there was no test target to run.
reviews.skip_if: Teams wanting a hosted API that accepts HTML or data and returns a PDF: pdfcn gives you React source and renderer integrations to run in your application.

reviews.name: kage
reviews.verdict: Use Kage as a reference, a visual benchmark, or the starting point for a private experiment.
reviews.skip_if: Production teams that require a clearly reusable code license Developers seeking a packaged component library or documented API Content-heavy sites that need routine editing by nontechnical staff Projects that must support old devices or guarantee low GPU usage

reviews.name: BPB-Worker-Panel
reviews.verdict: Our BPB Worker Panel run installed 204 packages in 29 seconds, built in 10 seconds, and showed 0 known npm vulnerabilities, but the repository supplied no test target.
reviews.skip_if: Groups larger than a few people: the README says a Worker has a 100,000-request daily limit for VLESS and Trojan and is suitable for 2 to 3 users.

reviews.name: up
reviews.verdict: Up is useful if you need a small operating system for self-directed learning, especially in Chinese.
reviews.skip_if: Developers looking for an executable AI tutor or learning app: this is an open-content guide and static site, not a service that tracks progress for you.

reviews.name: LinkSwift
reviews.verdict: Our LinkSwift checkout installed 76 packages in 8 seconds with 0 audit findings, but its only test exits with `Error: no test specified`, so reliability rests on live provider pages and manual reports.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone seeking a speed-limit bypass: the README explicitly says LinkSwift uses public provider APIs and does not promise or implement throttling circumvention.

reviews.name: blitz
reviews.verdict: Our Blitz checkout built in 10 seconds, but its 341-second `cargo test` run discovered 0 tests, so adoption should depend on your own rendered-page suite.
reviews.skip_if: Applications that require ordinary browser JavaScript: the roadmap lists JavaScript support in the backlog.

reviews.name: GPT-SoVITS
reviews.verdict: Our GPT-SoVITS install consumed 6,247 MB and pip-audit found 57 known vulnerabilities, while the repository supplied no automated test target for us to run.
reviews.skip_if: Small servers with tight storage budgets: our dependency install occupied 6,247 MB before pretrained model downloads.

reviews.name: hayamimi
reviews.verdict: Our Hayamimi run installed in 45 seconds and all 23 tests passed, an unusually clean result for a 73-file speech project.
reviews.skip_if: Conversations that switch languages within one sentence: the README says one route is chosen per utterance and minority-language words may be mangled or dropped.

reviews.name: sprix-sage-router
reviews.verdict: Our Sprix SAGE Router checkout built in 3 seconds and occupied just 0.1 MB, but the lab found no test target and the project does not execute an A2A handoff.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone seeking a working A2A router service: the README says the prototype returns a decision and intentionally does not transmit tasks.

reviews.name: cloudflare-os
reviews.verdict: Cloudflare OS is one of the more interesting attempts to make agent-built internal software governable, especially its Gatekeeper design and private Gadget model.
reviews.skip_if: Small teams wanting a finished, low-maintenance office suite, this is explicitly early access Organizations that need a conventional on-premises package or a documented Docker deployment Buyers expecting stable releases and predictable upgrade paths, no release is listed Nontechnical teams without…

reviews.name: airi
reviews.verdict: Airi is one of the more ambitious open companion projects, and it already joins voice, animated characters, multiple model providers, and game or chat integrations in a coherent direction.
reviews.skip_if: Users seeking a finished offline companion with no provider setup: the roadmap still lists pure browser WebGPU inference and the Memory Alaya system as unfinished.

reviews.name: maka
reviews.verdict: Our Maka run installed 849 packages and built successfully, but its test command exited 1 after 801 seconds with 3 of 1,095 node:test cases failed.
reviews.skip_if: Linux or Intel Mac users seeking a supported desktop build: the README says neither platform is supported yet, while Windows remains an unsigned preview.

reviews.name: magnitude
reviews.verdict: Our Magnitude install used 858 MB, the build failed in 5 seconds, and tests were still running when the 900-second cap expired.
reviews.skip_if: Native Windows users: the documentation explicitly requires WSL, and issue #36 still tracks a `/bin/sh.exe` failure from running outside it.

reviews.name: SenseNova-Skills
reviews.verdict: Our `sn-image-base` run installed 41 packages and built in 16 seconds, but pytest discovered 0 tests, so the measured path has packaging evidence without behavioral test evidence.
reviews.skip_if: Users who expect a standalone application: the repository needs a compatible agent runtime and category-specific Python, Node, browser, or API dependencies.

reviews.name: AI-Infra-Guard
reviews.verdict: Our AI-Infra-Guard run installed 301 packages and built successfully, but 7 of 16 tested packages failed, so it belongs in an evaluation lab before it belongs in a security process.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone planning a public deployment: the README says the web platform has no authentication and must stay off public networks.

reviews.name: ebook2audiobook
reviews.verdict: Our Ebook2Audiobook install consumed 7103 MB and pip-audit reported 44 known vulnerabilities, even though the build itself passed in 10 seconds.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone converting DRM-protected or unlawfully obtained books: the README limits intended use to non-DRM, legally acquired ebooks.

reviews.name: chatbot-template
reviews.verdict: Our chatbot-template run installed 686 packages in 28 seconds and built in 21 seconds, but it had no test target, so it is a quick prototype base rather than a verified production baseline.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone planning to deploy the starter unchanged to public traffic: its `/api/chat` route is unauthenticated and every request can spend AI Gateway credits.

reviews.name: ASu-skills
reviews.verdict: Our ASu-skills checkout installed 0 packages in 22 seconds and had no npm build or test target, so adoption is mostly a review of instructions, templates, and privacy boundaries rather than software setup.
reviews.skip_if: Applicants outside the Chinese recruiting context who want native English materials: an English README exists, but the plugin describes Chinese templates, fall recruiting, and WeChat or HR outreach.

reviews.name: dsh-TUI
reviews.verdict: Our dsh-TUI install completed in 33 seconds, but its source build failed after 41 seconds on an exact pnpm 11.21.0 versus 11.23.0 check, and the repository exposed no test target.
reviews.skip_if: Users who do not want DeepSeek Harness: dsh-TUI is an interface plugin and still requires the official `dsh` CLI.

reviews.name: nofx
reviews.verdict: Our NOFX run built successfully and passed 24 tests, but open reports still touch order duplication, backtest timing, and OKX equity used for sizing.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone who cannot lose the full account balance: the project's disclaimer says losses can exceed the initial deposit and AI behavior may be unpredictable.

reviews.name: koharu
reviews.verdict: Our Koharu run passed all 88 tests but could not finish its 358-second build because the fresh Debian image lacked `atk`, so packaged releases are the sensible first trial.
reviews.skip_if: Contributors expecting a plain Bun build on fresh Debian: our build failed because the native `atk` library was missing.

reviews.name: modly
reviews.verdict: Our Modly run passed all 37 tests in 9 seconds, but npm audit found 29 known vulnerabilities, including 1 critical and 23 high.
reviews.skip_if: CPU-only users: the README describes generation as running on a GPU, and the useful models arrive through separate extensions.

reviews.name: GR00T-WholeBodyControl
reviews.verdict: Our GR00T Whole-Body Control run built in 6 seconds, but all 9 collected test modules errored before a single test ran because Python could not import `yaml`.
reviews.skip_if: General Python developers seeking a hardware-neutral robotics library: the clearest deployment path targets Unitree G1, with one CloudXR route limited to G1 plus a Thor backpack.

reviews.name: openhuman
reviews.verdict: Our build finished in 55 seconds after installing 1,313 packages and 897 MB, but the test run still had no final result at the 900-second cap, so OpenHuman is an ambitious beta rather than a dependable personal data hub.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone needing stable production software today: the README labels OpenHuman an early beta and says to expect rough edges.

reviews.name: deepwiki-rs
reviews.verdict: Our Litho run built in 130 seconds and all 60 tests passed in 26 seconds, making it the cleanest lab result in this group.
reviews.skip_if: Teams expecting predictable cost on a large monorepo: closed issue 107 reports more than $100 spent analyzing 1,697 files before a 504 ended generation.

reviews.name: weathernext
reviews.verdict: Our WeatherNext install took 167 seconds and 886 MB, then built in 6 seconds, but there was no test target to run.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone making safety decisions from model output: the README says WeatherNext does not replace official alerts, warnings, or notices.

reviews.name: ADR
reviews.verdict: Our ADR Detection environment occupied 6,219 MB, pip-audit reported 100 known vulnerabilities, and test collection stopped with 61 tests passed and 1 marker error.
reviews.skip_if: Teams seeking an open-source tool that blocks unsafe actions: the README says ADR Prevention is absent from this release.

reviews.name: shell_gpt
reviews.verdict: Our ShellGPT install took 38 seconds and 61 MB, but all 4 test modules failed during collection before a single test passed.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone expecting safe command execution from the default function settings: open issue 793 reports that `execute_shell_command` can run model-proposed commands without confirmation when function calling is enabled.

reviews.name: 500-AI-Agents-Projects
reviews.verdict: Our build of the 72-package web catalog finished in 8 seconds, but no test target existed and we did not validate hundreds of linked agents.
reviews.skip_if: Buyers seeking 500 production-vetted implementations: much of the README is a catalog of external links, and our lab built only the `web/` project.

reviews.name: oh-my-openagent
reviews.verdict: Our oh-my-openagent install consumed 3,058 MB and its test suite was still running at 900 seconds, so this is a serious harness commitment rather than a casual plugin.
reviews.skip_if: Commercial product builders who need permissive redistribution rights: the Sustainable Use License limits use and modification to internal business, personal, or non-commercial purposes.

reviews.name: career-ops
reviews.verdict: Our career-ops install stopped after 14 seconds because the process ran Node 18.20.8 and Playwright required Node 20 or newer, so we could not build or test it.
reviews.skip_if: Applicants who want automatic submissions: the README says career-ops never submits an application and leaves the final action to the user.

reviews.name: lamda
reviews.verdict: Our FIRERPA client run installed 44 packages in 17 seconds and built in 9 seconds with 0 known audited vulnerabilities, but the repository exposed no test target for us to run.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that need repository tests and visible CI before deployment: our scan found no test target, no tests directory, and no CI workflow files.

reviews.name: openstatus
reviews.verdict: Our OpenStatus install pulled 1,538 packages and occupied 1,832 MB, then both the 6-second build and 7-second test run failed, so source contributors should expect setup investigation.
reviews.skip_if: Self-hosters expecting a single small container for the whole platform: the Docker guide starts dashboard, API, workflows, status page, database, migrations, and monitoring services.

reviews.name: fastapi_mcp
reviews.verdict: Our FastAPI-MCP run finished with 12 of 66 tests passing, while 32 failed and 22 stopped during collection or setup, so a production trial needs its own end-to-end transport check.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that expect a current release to track MCP Python SDK 2.0: issue 323 asks for that support, while release 0.4.0 targets the older session model.

reviews.name: GenAI_Agents
reviews.verdict: Our GenAI Agents install took 69 seconds, pulled 119 packages, and returned 137 known vulnerability findings, so it is useful as a reading lab but a poor production dependency.
reviews.skip_if: Teams looking for a supported production agent platform: the README describes tutorials and implementations, and points production-minded readers to a separate project.

reviews.name: gin-vue-admin
reviews.verdict: Our Gin-Vue-Admin build passed in 101 seconds, but 5 of 27 Go test packages failed and the current BSL requires a commercial license for production use.
reviews.skip_if: Organizations expecting permissive open-source production rights: the BSL 1.1 file says production use requires a commercial license until each version's 3-year change date.

reviews.name: code-review-graph
reviews.verdict: Our install consumed 5,344 MB and the test suite reached only 16% before a 900-second timeout, so code-review-graph is a deliberate toolchain addition rather than a lightweight MCP extra.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring a quick, bounded test run: our suite hit the 900-second cap while output showed only 16% progress.

reviews.name: FastGPT
reviews.verdict: Our FastGPT install pulled 2,548 packages and used 2,445 MB, then its test command failed because `@fastgpt/admin` was missing from the workspace filter.
reviews.skip_if: Companies planning a competing multi-tenant SaaS without a commercial agreement: the FastGPT license explicitly prohibits that use unless authorized in writing.

reviews.name: ai-agent-book
reviews.verdict: Our AI Agent Book environment occupied 6,774 MB, the build failed in 10 seconds, and tests ended with 41 collection or setup errors, so this is a reading library with independent labs rather than one reproducible application.
reviews.skip_if: Developers looking for one production agent framework: this is a 10-chapter book with many separate experiments and external reproduction tracks.

reviews.name: OmniRoute
reviews.verdict: Our OmniRoute install consumed 5,276 MB, its production build failed after 64 seconds, and its tests exceeded 900 seconds, so the measured commit is too heavy and uncertain for an unqualified production recommendation.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone who reads local-first as local inference: the README says prompts go to the upstream provider selected for each request.

reviews.name: JeecgBoot
reviews.verdict: Our JeecgBoot front-end install failed after 9 seconds, so the 3,497-file platform is a poor choice for teams seeking a quick, low-risk starter.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that need an English-first onboarding path: English docs exist, but the English README still describes Vite 6 while the v3.9.3 release says the front end moved to Vite 8.

reviews.name: gkd
reviews.verdict: Our GKD run installed in 16 seconds, but its build and tests both ended with exit 126 and `./gradlew: Permission denied`, so source adopters should budget a manual build fix before evaluation.
reviews.skip_if: English-only users: the README and linked guidance are Chinese, and issue 1416 is still an open request for English support.

reviews.name: EasySpider
reviews.verdict: Our install pulled 468 packages and 392 MB in 40 seconds, while npm audit found 45 known vulnerabilities, so EasySpider deserves a disposable-machine trial before any sensitive login is used.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that require an English-only support path: the README is bilingual in places, but the wiki, many videos, issue discussions, and detailed guidance are Chinese-first.

reviews.name: suna
reviews.verdict: Our Suna install pulled 2,651 packages and 3,393 MB, then build and tests both failed within 4 seconds because Bun was missing.
reviews.skip_if: SaaS vendors planning to resell a similar managed service: Elastic License 2.0 prohibits providing substantial product functionality as a hosted or managed service.

reviews.name: phone-harness
reviews.verdict: Our phone-harness run installed 33 packages in 26 seconds and built in 7 seconds, but there was no test target to check its device helpers.
reviews.skip_if: CI teams needing repeatable assertions, parallel devices, and stable selectors: the project exposes agent helpers, not a full mobile testing service.

reviews.name: video-use
reviews.verdict: Our video-use install took 28 seconds, used 508 MB, and built in 8 seconds, but the repository exposed no automated test target.
reviews.skip_if: Editors who need a native nonlinear timeline, manual keyframing, or live collaborative review: the main workflow is files, Markdown, and shell tools.

reviews.name: openwork
reviews.verdict: Our OpenWork install consumed 1,439 packages and 2,055 MB, then tests stopped after 5 seconds because Bun was missing, so source contributors need more than the pnpm quick path implies.
reviews.skip_if: Organizations that require the whole stack under a permissive license: `ee/` uses the OpenWork EE License and production beyond five users requires a subscription.

reviews.name: ego-lite
reviews.verdict: Our ego-browser helper installed 49 packages, passed all 299 tests, and reported 0 known npm vulnerabilities, but that clean result does not cover the separate browser binary or its session boundary.
reviews.skip_if: Windows or Linux users who need support today: the README says the browser currently runs only on macOS.

reviews.name: phoneinfoga
reviews.verdict: Our PhoneInfoga run built in 13 seconds, but 3 of 12 tested packages failed and upstream says future bugs will not be fixed.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone trying to track a person's live or precise location: the README explicitly says PhoneInfoga cannot do either.

reviews.name: res-downloader
reviews.verdict: Our res-downloader build took 3 seconds, but its only discovered Go test package failed because the embedded `frontend/dist` files were missing.
reviews.skip_if: Users unwilling to install a local certificate or route traffic through 127.0.0.1:8899: both steps are part of the documented workflow.

reviews.name: automatisch
reviews.verdict: Our Automatisch install pulled 727 packages in 71 seconds, but its tests stopped after 8 seconds because the required `.env.test` file was missing.
reviews.skip_if: Operators who want a single stateless container: the supplied Compose stack runs the main app, a worker, PostgreSQL 14.5, and Redis 7.0.4, with three persistent volumes.

reviews.name: ai-data-extractor
reviews.verdict: Our run installed 35 packages in 21 seconds and found 0 known vulnerabilities, but this 1,707-line extractor has no automated test target.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone expecting guaranteed extraction from Windsurf or Trae: the README says their undocumented SQLite formats are parsed with a heuristic that can return zero conversations after a schema change.

reviews.name: RuVector
reviews.verdict: RuVector is worth testing for an embedded agent-memory system when you can start with `VectorDB` or the hooks CLI and ignore most of the monorepo.
reviews.skip_if: Teams wanting one stable facade over every memory type: the README says the unified manager lacks native save and load, and cross-type consolidation is incomplete.

reviews.name: crw
reviews.verdict: fastCRW is a credible choice when one compact service must feed web data to applications and MCP agents, particularly for teams testing a move from Firecrawl.
reviews.skip_if: Teams scraping heavily protected sites as a hard requirement: open issue #189 documents CARFAX content being blocked by client-side bot detection even with Chromium.

reviews.name: prettymaps
reviews.verdict: Our Prettymaps run installed 148 packages and used 1,913 MB, then built in 6 seconds and passed all 9 collected tests.
reviews.skip_if: Unattended render services that need each location to finish predictably: map creation calls OpenStreetMap services, and open issue 154 describes partial Overpass responses ending in a `KeyError`.

reviews.name: memvid
reviews.verdict: Our Memvid build finished in 105 seconds, but the full test run hit the 900-second cap with 3 lexical tests still running beyond 60 seconds.
reviews.skip_if: Multi-agent systems that need several processes writing at once: issue 218 says the current design has a single-writer limitation and requires a queue or central writer.

reviews.name: qlib
reviews.verdict: Our Qlib run installed 214 packages and built successfully; 10 tests failed and 9 more ended in collection or setup errors, so it suits quant research teams that can validate the stack themselves.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone expecting a dependable market dataset in the download: the README says the official dataset is temporarily disabled, points to a community archive, and warns that its Yahoo-derived data may be imperfect.

reviews.name: czsc
reviews.verdict: Our CZSC run installed 57 packages in 753 seconds and passed 516 of 517 executed tests, with one datetime-precision assertion failing.
reviews.skip_if: English-only developers who need first-party tutorials and reference material: the README, public API guide, changelog, examples, issue discussion, and linked community resources are primarily Chinese.

reviews.name: msgvault
reviews.verdict: Our msgvault build took 128 seconds, and the test run timed out at 900 seconds with 34 passed and 6 failed packages reported.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone unwilling to run alpha storage software: the README says APIs, storage format, and CLI flags may change without notice.

reviews.name: MediaCrawler
reviews.verdict: Our MediaCrawler checkout installed 269 npm packages in 26 seconds, but it exposed no npm build or test target for us to verify.
reviews.skip_if: Commercial teams: the included license permits non-commercial learning and research, and requires written consent for commercial use.

reviews.name: pgrust
reviews.verdict: Our pgrust build passed in 443 seconds and 152 of 153 tests passed, with the remaining case failing because `en_US.UTF-8` was absent from our Debian container.
reviews.skip_if: Any production workload or valuable data: the README explicitly says pgrust is not production ready and still has many bugs.

reviews.name: harvey-labs
reviews.verdict: Our Harvey LAB run passed 12,588 tests but still ended with 23 failures and 39 collection or setup errors, so this benchmark deserves inspection before its scores reach a procurement slide.
reviews.skip_if: Buyers seeking a compact benchmark download: our checkout occupied 3,260.2 MB and contained 63,074 files.

reviews.name: fhevm
reviews.verdict: Our FHEVM install pulled 2,587 packages and 2,071 MB, then its test command failed in 5 seconds because Bun was absent and npm audit reported 108 known vulnerabilities.
reviews.skip_if: Companies assuming the open-source license covers commercial deployment: the README says commercial use also requires Zama's paid patent license.

reviews.name: plugins
reviews.verdict: Our plugin-eval install added 0 packages in 4 seconds, but its test command failed after 8 seconds on a literal glob path, so this repository is better used as pinned source material than as a trusted monolithic package.
reviews.skip_if: Developers looking for a single npm library or server: the README describes a collection of independent plugin folders, and the tested Node project lives specifically in `plugins/plugin-eval`.

reviews.name: v
reviews.verdict: Our sandbox did not run commit 4ddbd6c because V is outside the lab's supported ecosystems, so this review cannot confirm the README's quick source-build story.
reviews.skip_if: Organizations that require a frozen language and standard-library API: the README says breaking language changes and minor core API changes may happen before 1.0.

reviews.name: autoprompt-skill
reviews.verdict: Our AutoPrompt test command finished with 78 of 80 tests passing and still exited 1, so version 1.0.4 is not a clean lab pass.
reviews.skip_if: Small edits where several agents cost more time than the change deserves: the README estimates about 3 times the time and 2 times the tokens, without retained logs for those estimates.

reviews.name: proliferate
reviews.verdict: Our Proliferate install pulled 1,108 packages and used 1,128 MB, while the root offered no generic build or test target for our harness to run.
reviews.skip_if: Solo developers who run one agent at a time and already manage its worktree comfortably: Proliferate's main value appears when tasks overlap.

reviews.name: no-mistakes
reviews.verdict: Our No Mistakes run built in 41 seconds but finished with 16 of 17 tests passing, so this Git gate is not ready to become the only authority between a branch and its remote.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that need every checked commit to pass the project's own suite: our run ended with 16 of 17 tests passing and a final `FAIL`, while the supplied log tail did not name the failed package.

reviews.name: ESP32-Cheap-Yellow-Display
reviews.verdict: Our Rust example stopped after 7 seconds because the required custom `esp` toolchain was absent, so Rust users must complete Espressif-specific setup before they can even compile.
reviews.skip_if: Owners of a lookalike board that is not marked ESP32-2432S028: the troubleshooting guide says the examples and pin information target that model.

reviews.name: union
reviews.verdict: Union is serious protocol infrastructure for teams that specifically want light-client-based interoperability and can evaluate its chain-specific code.
reviews.skip_if: Application developers seeking one small bridge library: this repository includes the chain, prover, relayer, contracts, sites, and several SDK workspaces.

reviews.name: RustPython
reviews.verdict: Our RustPython build and 2-test Cargo suite both passed, but they consumed 947 seconds combined and do not establish CPython 3.14 compatibility across a 1,311,696-line checkout.
reviews.skip_if: Teams needing drop-in CPython compatibility for arbitrary packages: the README says RustPython is not fully production-ready, and Python 3.14 library and test updates remain open.

reviews.name: Impactor
reviews.verdict: Our Impactor checkout built in 360 seconds, but `cargo test` found 0 tests, so the green command is not evidence that signing and pairing work.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone who needs a set-and-forget free-account install: the README says unpaid Apple accounts are limited to 7 days and a limited number of registered apps or components.

reviews.name: DevOps-Interview-Guide
reviews.verdict: Use DevOps Interview Guide as a stack of flash cards, especially when your target company appears in the folders.
reviews.skip_if: Beginners looking for explanations or model answers: the files are question lists, and the README does not claim to teach the underlying topics.

reviews.name: gastown
reviews.verdict: Our Gas Town run installed 651 packages and built in 108 seconds, but 27 of 75 Go test packages failed.
reviews.skip_if: Solo developers coordinating only 1 or 2 agents: the Mayor, Deacon, Witnesses, Refineries, Dolt, Beads, and tmux add substantial machinery.

reviews.name: nanoGPT
reviews.verdict: Our nanoGPT install took 32 seconds and its 21-second build passed, but the repository supplied no test target to run.
reviews.skip_if: New projects choosing a maintained Karpathy training stack: the README says nanoGPT is deprecated and points readers to nanochat.

reviews.name: 9router
reviews.verdict: Our 9Router install pulled 871 packages and used 675 MB, while the build passed but no test target ran and npm audit found 2 moderate vulnerabilities.
reviews.skip_if: Organizations that prohibit placing provider OAuth sessions and API keys in one local service: the dashboard manages both and supports multiple accounts.

reviews.name: DesktopCommanderMCP
reviews.verdict: Our Desktop Commander install ran for 900 seconds without completing, so we could not build or test the 301-file checkout.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone treating `allowedDirectories` or the command blocklist as a security boundary: the project says terminal commands can bypass both.

reviews.name: claudish-to-english
reviews.verdict: Use it if Claude Code's wording regularly slows you down and you already run Ollama or have a suitable API account.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone who needs guaranteed faithful wording, because another model performs the rewrite Users who want a zero-configuration plugin, especially on Windows People with limited memory or no interest in running a local model or paying API fees Production workflows that…

reviews.name: awesome-deepseek-agent
reviews.verdict: Awesome DeepSeek Agent is a useful first stop if your exact client appears in its table, especially because the guides are short and bilingual.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone looking for an agent runtime or installable library: the repository contains Markdown guides and screenshots, not application code.

reviews.name: Kun
reviews.verdict: Our Kun install consumed 2,374 MB, and its wider suite finished with 85 failed tests plus 114 known vulnerabilities, so v0.3.6 is not a low-risk default for sensitive work.
reviews.skip_if: Commercial teams expecting an open-source business license: PolyForm Noncommercial permits learning, research, and noncommercial use, while business use needs written authorization.

reviews.name: PraisonAI
reviews.verdict: Our PraisonAI npm audit found 48 known vulnerabilities, including 3 critical and 29 high, while the measured package exposed no build or test target.
reviews.skip_if: Security-sensitive automation that would trust the current approval layer without independent controls: open issue 3866 reports argument-blind deny rules and hooks that can fail open.

reviews.name: gentle-ai
reviews.verdict: Our harness installed 0 Node packages and failed in 6 seconds because the root npm test is a placeholder, so that result does not validate Gentle AI's Go implementation.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone looking for a standalone coding agent: the README says Gentle AI adapts detected runtimes and refuses to install a missing agent for you.

reviews.name: invoice-builder
reviews.verdict: Our Invoice Builder setup used 1,054 MB and built in 10 seconds, but its test process failed because the sqlite3 binary required GLIBC 2.38 even though all 4 executed tests passed.
reviews.skip_if: Organizations that need a vendor-backed compliance guarantee: the README claims standards-compliant exports, but adopters still need to validate files against their jurisdiction and delivery network.

reviews.name: OpenBot
reviews.verdict: OpenBot has one of the more convincing designs for giving agents real access without treating trust as a prompt-writing exercise.
reviews.skip_if: Security-sensitive production teams that need a settled release today: the README labels OpenBot alpha, and an open issue shows that an allowed agent URL can redirect to an address the initial safety check would refuse.

reviews.name: buzz
reviews.verdict: Our Buzz checkout exceeded 1 million source lines, and the pnpm install added 611 packages and 445 MB, yet the root package exposed no build or test target for our harness to verify.
reviews.skip_if: Teams replacing Slack, GitHub, or incident tooling this quarter: the README labels Buzz unfinished and lists workflow approvals, mobile clients, and huddle lifecycle work as still being wired up.

reviews.name: fluxer
reviews.verdict: Our Fluxer checkout installed 1,761 packages and used 1,630 MB, then both the 176-second build and 77-second test command exited 1.
reviews.skip_if: Small self-hosters expecting a single container: the operator guide requires a Compose stack and recommends at least 2 vCPU, 4 GB RAM, and 20 GB disk.

reviews.name: filestash
reviews.verdict: Our Filestash build passed in 21 seconds, but all 109 Go packages failed during the 172-second test step, so source adopters do not have a clean baseline from our run.
reviews.skip_if: Operators who cannot test destructive file operations: open issue 994 reports WebDAV folder deletion on S3 also deleting a sibling with the same prefix, and the related fix remains an open pull request.

reviews.name: planka
reviews.verdict: Our PLANKA source install failed after 39 seconds during the server's Python virtual-environment setup, so the build and tests never ran.
reviews.skip_if: Agencies or consultants inviting paying clients into a Community instance: the license guide says third-party access in a commercial relationship requires Pro or Enterprise.

reviews.name: Antigravity-Manager
reviews.verdict: Our Antigravity checkout built in 31 seconds, but it installed 817 packages, carried 22 known vulnerabilities, and offered no test target, so this is a personal-lab gateway rather than a service we would trust blindly.
reviews.skip_if: Commercial products that need permissive licensing: the repository uses CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, which limits licensed use to noncommercial purposes and requires ShareAlike for adaptations.

reviews.name: OpenBiliClaw
reviews.verdict: Our OpenBiliClaw test run was still only at 3% when the 900-second limit ended, so its 24-second successful build should not be mistaken for a fully verified release.
reviews.skip_if: Users who reject personality inference: the README says the agent infers MBTI, cognitive style, and deeper psychological needs.

reviews.name: flexprice
reviews.verdict: Our Flexprice run built in 233 seconds, but 2 of 48 Go test packages failed after a 266-second suite.
reviews.skip_if: Small SaaS products with flat subscriptions that already fit their payment provider: Flexprice adds several data and workflow services.

reviews.name: documenso
reviews.verdict: Our Documenso install pulled 2,506 packages and used 2,473 MB, while the 272-second build passed but no test target existed and npm audit found 9 advisories.
reviews.skip_if: Casual self-hosters looking for a tiny weekend service: our install used 2,473 MB before documents, Postgres, mail, or object storage.

reviews.name: cal.diy
reviews.verdict: Our run installed 4,673 packages and 3,958 MB, passed its test target in 224 seconds, then failed the build because `NEXTAUTH_SECRET` was missing, so Cal.diy is testable but configuration-heavy even before deployment.
reviews.skip_if: Businesses or production services: the README strictly recommends Cal.diy for personal, non-production use and directs commercial users to Cal.com.

reviews.name: Olares
reviews.verdict: Our Olares CLI build took 212 seconds, and 7 of 85 test groups failed after a 227-second run, so this 535.6 MB platform deserves a spare machine and a staged trial.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone looking for a light NAS dashboard: the Linux install requires at least 150 GB of SSD storage and the repository incorporates Kubernetes, K3s, JuiceFS, MinIO, Envoy, databases, and many system apps Operators who want conventional per-service ownership: Olares ties…

reviews.name: cal.diy
reviews.verdict: Our run installed 4,673 packages into 3,958 MB, passed the tests, and then failed the build because `NEXTAUTH_SECRET` was unset, so Cal.diy is a serious self-hosting commitment rather than a quick calendar widget.
reviews.skip_if: Businesses seeking a supported production deployment: the README strictly recommends Cal.diy for personal, non-production use and points commercial users to Cal.com.

reviews.name: workout-guide
reviews.verdict: Our checkout built in 11 seconds and all five Vitest tests passed, so Workout Guide is a credible starting point for adding static exercise art without inventing a catalog.
reviews.skip_if: Products that need coaching, rep counting, timers, workout planning, or user progress: the project supplies exercise metadata and images, not a training engine.

reviews.name: edit
reviews.verdict: Use FMHY when you want a maintained map of free online resources and accept that many destinations are third-party sites requiring your own judgment.
reviews.skip_if: Contributors adding paid or trial-only services, coding libraries, Linux distributions, or multiplayer cheats: the contribution guide explicitly rejects those categories or directs readers elsewhere.

reviews.name: topcoat
reviews.verdict: Our Topcoat run built in 241 seconds and all 239 tests passed in 151 seconds, giving this experimental framework a better code signal than its age suggests.
reviews.skip_if: Production teams requiring API stability: the README calls Topcoat early-stage and experimental and says to expect breaking changes.

reviews.name: Viscose-carousel
reviews.verdict: Our Viscose run installed 623 packages, built in 20 seconds, and found 0 known npm vulnerabilities, but there was no test target and the README lists four production-blocking interaction gaps.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone shipping the repository unchanged: the README says all images belong to other people, and PP Neue Montreal is included only for local evaluation without a commercial license.

reviews.name: Libraries
reviews.verdict: Our install added 226 packages in 34 seconds with 0 known vulnerabilities, but the measured root exposed no build or test target.
reviews.skip_if: Vue or other framework teams: the published web packages require React, and Vue 3 support is only an open question.

reviews.name: Infographic
reviews.verdict: Our AntV Infographic run built in 31 seconds and passed its 83-second test step, but installation took 207 seconds, used 986 MB, and exposed 4 high-severity advisories.
reviews.skip_if: Teams with a strict dependency-advisory gate: our install reported 7 known vulnerabilities, including 4 high-severity findings.

reviews.name: brush
reviews.verdict: Our Brush install took 14 seconds, but its web build failed after 7 seconds at the wasm-pack command, so the browser path needs more preparation than `npm install` suggests.
reviews.skip_if: Safari or Firefox web deployments: the README limits web support to Chrome 134 or newer on Windows and macOS, and calls Firefox and Safari hoped-for support.

reviews.name: unilm
reviews.verdict: Our PFPO install added 35 packages in 22 seconds and built in 10 seconds, but there was no test target to check the code path we installed.
reviews.skip_if: Teams seeking one coherent install for every UniLM project: the root README is an index of many separate research directories, each with its own assumptions.

reviews.name: Amagine3D
reviews.verdict: Our build finished in 14 seconds, but 5 of 32 tests failed, so Amagine3D is not ready for uncritical production adoption.
reviews.skip_if: Production teams that require a stable tagged release and a fully passing test suite Beginners expecting a one-command appliance with no Node.js or CAD-runtime knowledge Mechanical engineers who need certified tolerances, simulation, or manufacturing sign-off Users who want a mature…

reviews.name: DeepSeek-Balance-Whale-Widget
reviews.verdict: Our install took 5 seconds and added 0 packages, but the repository provides no build or test target to verify the widget's behavior.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone outside DeepSeek Harness: this is a DSH web-profile plugin, not a general desktop widget or provider dashboard.

reviews.name: eliza
reviews.verdict: Our elizaOS install stopped after 5 seconds with an npm override conflict, before the lab could record any build or test result.
reviews.skip_if: Developers looking for a small agent library to understand in one sitting: our checkout had 31,514 files and about 6,921,967 source lines.

reviews.name: Open-Generative-AI
reviews.verdict: Our 47-second install pulled 1,239 packages and 1,375 MB, then the production build failed in 18 seconds, so this checkout is a trial for curious MuAPI users rather than a production deployment.
reviews.skip_if: Buyers who interpret self-hosted as fully local: the README says the main catalog calls MuAPI, while local inference is desktop-only and covers fewer models.

reviews.name: CyberStrikeAI
reviews.verdict: Our CyberStrikeAI run installed 86 packages in 34 seconds and built in 6 seconds with 0 audit findings, but it exposed no test target for a 221,305-line system that can execute commands, manage WebShells, and run C2.
reviews.skip_if: Casual users looking for a chatbot: the project's security model calls this a high-privilege system with command execution, WebShell, and optional C2.

reviews.name: nakama
reviews.verdict: Our Nakama build passed in 37 seconds, but the 466-second test run ended with 3 database failures and 8 server failures, so this active v0.4.3 project still needs operator scrutiny.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that let untrusted users install custom tools: critical issue #447 says JavaScript handlers run inside the server process and Python receives the full server environment.

reviews.name: Pixelle-Video
reviews.verdict: Our Pixelle-Video install took 47 seconds and its build passed, but pytest found 0 tests and pip-audit reported 25 known vulnerabilities.
reviews.skip_if: Editors who need frame-level timeline control: the documented workflow is driven by narration segments and HTML templates, not tracks and keyframes.

reviews.name: WhatDreamsCost-ComfyUI
reviews.verdict: Our WhatDreamsCost-ComfyUI run installed 33 packages, passed its 23-second build check, and found no test target, so the code is cheap to try but weakly verified.
reviews.skip_if: Users who need a self-contained install: the README says LTX Director requires current ComfyUI-LTXVideo and ComfyUI-KJNodes.

reviews.name: h3.c
reviews.verdict: Our Linux build and test steps both failed in 4 seconds with 2 C errors around `strdup`, so h3.c is not a portable drop-in even though installation itself succeeded.
reviews.skip_if: Linux or Windows users seeking an official cross-platform binary: the README defines the project as native Apple Silicon inference, while CUDA support exists only in an open pull request.

reviews.name: bonsai
reviews.verdict: Our Bonsai build failed after 118 seconds and its test command failed after 6 seconds because the linker could not find Python 3.11, so a whole-workspace source checkout is not ready on a plain Rust image.
reviews.skip_if: Teams needing a typed port and blackboard model between nodes: open issue 61 says Bonsai currently passes one monolithic context object through the tree.

reviews.name: LingChat
reviews.verdict: Our LingChat checkout built in 28 seconds after installing 232 packages, but it provided no automated test target, so the most ambitious release claims remain manual checks.
reviews.skip_if: Users who will not grant an AI screen context or computer tools: v0.5.0 adds agent actions, web search, and proactive desktop observation.

reviews.name: compozy
reviews.verdict: Our CompozyOS build stopped after 18 seconds at Go module parsing, and the current v0.3 line is still beta, so production teams should trial it beside existing automation before handing it unattended work.
reviews.skip_if: Existing v0.2 users who need an in-place upgrade: the README says v0.3 does not revive the old `tasks run` pipeline and requires the migration guide.

reviews.name: AiToEarn
reviews.verdict: Our AiToEarn backend install pulled 1,487 packages and 986 MB in 58 seconds, then offered no build or test target to verify.
reviews.skip_if: Brands that cannot risk duplicate public posts: issue 586 reports TikTok Direct Post retries creating more than one post after an ambiguous failure.

reviews.name: cursor-byok
reviews.verdict: Our cursor-byok checkout built in 6 seconds, but 18 of 24 test packages failed because GTK and WebKitGTK development files were missing, so Linux setup is more than downloading a model proxy.
reviews.skip_if: Managed desktops that forbid local certificate installation: issue 352 asks for another route because corporate policy blocks the certificate required by the new release.

reviews.name: corsair
reviews.verdict: Our Corsair checkout installed 2,105 packages and consumed 2,278 MB, then 34 of 43 Jest tests failed even though the 565-second build passed.
reviews.skip_if: Projects with one or two simple integrations where direct SDK calls are easier to audit and maintain.

reviews.name: eigent
reviews.verdict: Our Eigent run used 1,634 MB, found 27 known vulnerabilities, and ended with 34 of 739 tests failing, so it is an evaluation build rather than a safe default for unattended desktop work.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that require a clean dependency audit before evaluation: our npm audit found 27 known vulnerabilities, including 3 critical and 14 high.

reviews.name: meetily
reviews.verdict: Our Meetily build hit the 900-second limit, and its test step failed after 267 seconds because the required Linux `llama-helper` binary was missing, so source deployment is not ready for a casual operator.
reviews.skip_if: Linux users who need a ready installer: release 0.4.0 provides Windows and Apple Silicon macOS assets, while the README directs Linux users to a source build.

reviews.name: deepteam
reviews.verdict: Our DeepTeam build took 5 seconds, but its test run stopped after 323 passes, 144 failures, and 56 errors, with missing `sentry_sdk` and an unconfigured OpenAI key in the log.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring a clean offline test suite from the package alone: our run hit missing `sentry_sdk` errors and tests that demanded an OpenAI API key.

reviews.name: BitFun
reviews.verdict: Our BitFun run installed 1,199 packages, built in 120 seconds, and found 10 high-severity vulnerabilities without an available test target.
reviews.skip_if: Small teams seeking a lightweight source build: our install added 1,199 packages, used 787 MB, and the build took 120 seconds.

reviews.name: LifeOS
reviews.verdict: Our measured npm subproject installed 2 packages in 5 seconds, but it did not exercise the AI-led installer, hooks, memory, or Pulse, so the real setup remains unverified by our run.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone unwilling to let an installer modify harness configuration, hooks, context files, and a shell launch command after approval: those changes are central to the documented setup.

reviews.name: VibeVoice
