reviews.verdict: VibeVoice is worth testing for long meetings where one pass should produce words, timestamps, and speaker turns, or for research on low-latency English speech.
reviews.skip_if: Production buyers seeking Microsoft's endorsement for deployment: the README says commercial and real-world use needs further testing and development.

reviews.name: MiroFish
reviews.verdict: Our MiroFish install added 31 packages in 13 seconds, but the build failed in 7 seconds because `vite` was not available in the frontend.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone making financial, political, or safety decisions from one run: the official FAQ says MiroFish does not guarantee causal validity, prediction confidence, or calibrated behavior.

reviews.name: computer
reviews.verdict: Our Cloudflare Computer run built in 46 seconds and reported 543 passing tests, yet the command exited 1 after 141 seconds and the install occupied 1,145 MB.
reviews.skip_if: Production workloads: the README explicitly says the APIs are unstable and the package is unsuitable for production use.

reviews.name: onlook
reviews.verdict: Our Onlook install pulled 2,522 packages and 2,547 MB, then the build stopped on a missing Supabase key and the overall test command exited 1.
reviews.skip_if: Vue, Svelte, plain HTML, or non-Tailwind projects: the README marks non-Next.js and non-Tailwind support as unfinished.

reviews.name: OSWorld
reviews.verdict: Our OSWorld environment used 6,915 MB, and pytest produced 8 passes plus 10 collection or setup errors, so this is research infrastructure rather than a ready-made test dependency.
reviews.skip_if: Developers seeking a normal Python package test: our install occupied 6,915 MB and pytest ended with 10 collection or setup errors.

reviews.name: plandex
reviews.verdict: Our Plandex run installed 360 packages and built in 40 seconds, but its successful test step found 0 tests and the hosted service no longer accepts users.
reviews.skip_if: New users expecting a hosted account: the README says Plandex Cloud began winding down on October 3, 2025 and no longer accepts users.

reviews.name: Vane
reviews.verdict: Our Vane install took 274 seconds, pulled 1,051 packages, and occupied 2,039 MB, while the repository offered no test target, so the polished Docker pitch hides a heavy and weakly verified code path.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone planning to expose it directly to the public internet: the README lists authentication as an upcoming feature, and issue 1180 reports API keys exposed to client-side code.

reviews.name: OpenMontage
reviews.verdict: Our OpenMontage build finished in 5 seconds, but the test run ended with 9 failures and 4 setup errors because several media paths expected `ffmpeg` or `npx`.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone expecting `make setup` to cover a bare Linux machine: the README lists FFmpeg and Node.js as prerequisites, and our tests stopped on missing `ffmpeg` and `npx`.

reviews.name: TRELLIS.2
reviews.verdict: Our O-Voxel install took 361 seconds and its build passed in 11 seconds, but the repository exposed no test target and our 8 GB sandbox could not exercise the 24 GB GPU workflow.
reviews.skip_if: Mac, Windows, AMD, or Intel GPU users seeking an official supported path: the README says testing is limited to Linux on NVIDIA A100 and H100 hardware, while non-CUDA support remains an open request.

reviews.name: ai-engineering-hub
reviews.verdict: Our measured researcher installed 33 packages in 30 seconds and built in 11 seconds, but it exposed no test target and the repository has 0 CI workflows.
reviews.skip_if: Teams looking for one supported production platform: the repository is a gallery of independent projects with separate dependencies and operating assumptions.

reviews.name: lobehub
reviews.verdict: Our LobeHub install spent 296 seconds before npm rejected `workspace:*`, so the first decision is whether your team will follow its pnpm workflow and accept a 198.4 MB monorepo.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone using `npm install` without checking the repository's package-manager instructions: our run failed on the `workspace:*` protocol, while the README tells contributors to use pnpm.

reviews.name: ds4
reviews.verdict: Our DwarfStar build finished in 5 seconds, but its 56-second test step stopped when `nvcc` was missing, so a clean CPU-only checkout did not clear the project's default test path.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone who wants to load arbitrary GGUF files: the README says unsupported tensor layouts, quantization mixes, metadata, and MTP state will not work.

reviews.name: skills
reviews.verdict: emilkowalski/skills is a clever and timely project that packages high-level design expertise into a format AI agents can understand.
reviews.skip_if: Developers not using AI or LLM-based agents for coding; the project's value is entirely in guiding these agents.

reviews.name: nippo
reviews.verdict: Our Nippo run installed 55 packages and passed all 106 tests after a 44-second build, making it an easy trial for Japanese-speaking Claude Code or Codex users.
reviews.skip_if: English-only teams: the README, templates, skill instructions, and user-facing examples are Japanese, with no English documentation found in the repository tree.

reviews.name: zapret-discord-youtube
reviews.verdict: Our 2026-08-26 Debian lab with 3 CPUs and 8 GB of RAM could not run this Windows Batch and WinDivert bundle, so no independent install or test result exists.
reviews.skip_if: Linux, macOS, Android, or iOS users: the documented package is built around Windows Batch files, services, `netsh`, and the WinDivert driver.

reviews.name: backlink_skills
reviews.verdict: Our lab could not run backlink_skills because it found no supported executable ecosystem and no Dockerfile, so this review cannot offer an independent install or test result.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone seeking a one-click backlink bot: the README explicitly rejects link spam, ranking manipulation, verification bypass, invented profiles, paid links, and forced reciprocal links.

reviews.name: macos-harness
reviews.verdict: Our Debian run built macOS Harness in 7 seconds, then passed 10 of 26 tests because the remaining 16 required unavailable macOS ApplicationServices bindings.
reviews.skip_if: Windows or Linux users: the README labels the project macOS-only, and 16 tests failed in our Debian sandbox because ApplicationServices bindings were unavailable.

reviews.name: cli
reviews.verdict: Our Lark CLI install failed after 28 seconds because its installer could not find `checksums.txt`, so commit 35bd5ec is a poor choice for unattended bootstrap despite the project's broad official coverage.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone who needs a cloud-native connector with no local machine: open issue #2527 asks for an official remote MCP endpoint because this project is a locally installed CLI.

reviews.name: mcp-server
reviews.verdict: Our SV Number MCP Server run installed 101 packages, built in 13 seconds, and reported 0 known vulnerabilities, but there was no test target to exercise its nine tools.
reviews.skip_if: Banking, payment, or government-account workflows: the README explicitly says these numbers are not intended for those services.

reviews.name: bettergi-scripts-list
reviews.verdict: Our ArtifactScore run installed 10 packages in 18 seconds, but the repository supplied no build or test target, so that clean audit does not establish that any game automation works.
reviews.skip_if: English-only users: this script repository has no English README, and individual scripts such as ArtifactScore require the Simplified Chinese game interface.

reviews.name: youtube-automation-agent
reviews.verdict: Our AgentTube test step passed but took 652 seconds, while npm audit reported 29 vulnerabilities, including 1 critical and 18 high.
reviews.skip_if: Creators seeking a zero-account local pipeline: YouTube publishing needs Google OAuth, and useful generation needs provider keys or local models plus FFmpeg.

reviews.name: superplane
reviews.verdict: Our SuperPlane run built in 11 seconds, but 9 of 142 tests failed, so its polished demo should lead to a bounded pilot rather than control of a critical release path.
reviews.skip_if: Teams requiring stable APIs today: the README labels SuperPlane beta, says primitives and integrations are maturing, and warns about breaking changes.

reviews.name: holehe
reviews.verdict: Our Holehe install took 36 seconds, used 42 MB, built in 9 seconds, and had no test target, so its clean setup says little about whether 120-plus live provider probes remain correct.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone trying to identify, stalk, embarrass, or take over another person's accounts: the tool exposes sensitive association signals and the README limits it to educational use.

reviews.name: claude-code-security-review
reviews.verdict: Our build of Claude Code Security Reviewer installed 52 packages in 17 seconds and built in 6 seconds, but the harness found no test target to run.
reviews.skip_if: Public repositories that automatically run secrets-enabled workflows on untrusted contributions: the README says the action is not hardened against prompt injection and recommends maintainer approval first.

reviews.name: SQLBot
reviews.verdict: Our SQLBot run installed 241 packages and consumed 5,405 MB, then pytest discovered 0 tests and pip-audit reported 30 known vulnerabilities, so adoption needs a real security and regression budget.
reviews.skip_if: Companies that require white-label redistribution: the modified GPLv3 license forbids removing or changing SQLBot's logo and copyright information.

reviews.name: Crucix
reviews.verdict: Our Crucix install took 14 seconds and 31 MB, but there was no build or test target and npm audit found 6 known vulnerabilities, so this is a localhost experiment rather than an intelligence system to trust.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone treating map positions as evidence: issue 112 says news coordinates are randomly shifted, and issue 116 says unmatched stories can be pinned to publication centroids.

reviews.name: quant-mind
reviews.verdict: Our QuantMind run passed 485 tests, but its 893 MB environment contained 24 known vulnerabilities, so adoption should start with dependency triage rather than production data.
reviews.skip_if: Security-sensitive teams that cannot review and remediate dependencies before use: pip-audit found 24 known vulnerabilities in our 178-package environment.

reviews.name: ChinaTextbook
reviews.verdict: ChinaTextbook is an immensely popular and valuable archive of Chinese educational materials, but it's best viewed as a dormant library, not an active project.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone who cannot read Mandarin, as the entire project and all its contents are in Chinese.

reviews.name: Kronos
reviews.verdict: Our Kronos environment occupied 4,791 MB, and pytest passed 4 tests before a fifth file failed during collection because parametrize received a zip.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone seeking a production trading system: the README calls its Qlib pipeline a simplified demonstration and lists portfolio, risk, cost, slippage, and market-impact work still required.

reviews.name: real-company-interview-ai-coding-projects
reviews.verdict: Our sandbox did not run commit 883fd50 because it has no supported ecosystem or Dockerfile.
reviews.skip_if: Candidates who need English material: all six files at commit 883fd50 are in Chinese, and the repository provides no translated edition.

reviews.name: asyar
reviews.verdict: Our Asyar build stopped after 9 seconds because Bun was missing, despite the 21-second dependency install succeeding, so source contributors should budget for an extra runtime prerequisite.
reviews.skip_if: Wayland users who depend on global snippet expansion: the README says input-heavy features such as Snippets do not work there.

reviews.name: cryptolayer
reviews.verdict: Our run passed all 6 tests and pip-audit found 0 known dependency vulnerabilities, but the project’s own open security warning says not to trust it with real confidential messages yet.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone protecting real confidential correspondence today: open issue 18 explicitly recommends against that use until its listed protocol flaws are fully resolved.

reviews.name: Wake
reviews.verdict: Our build failed after 896 seconds because the linker could not find `-lxkbcommon-x11`.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone who needs team sharing, cloud sync, or remote access Windows and Linux users who require polished, proven desktop integration today Users of Windsurf, Trae, Amp, Factory, or Warp, whose sessions are not supported People unwilling to bypass Gatekeeper or…

reviews.name: x64dbg-mcp-server
reviews.verdict: Version 1.1 gives an MCP client 84 debugger tools over unencrypted HTTP, so x64dbg-MCP Server should be treated like a remote code-and-memory control plane, not a convenience plugin.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone debugging software without explicit authorization: the plugin can execute commands, write process memory, dump modules, and manipulate a live target.

reviews.name: andrej-karpathy-skills
reviews.verdict: Use andrej-karpathy-skills if your main complaint is that Claude Code guesses too much, edits too broadly, or turns small jobs into large designs.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that need measured proof that the rules improve coding outcomes: the tested commit contains examples, while a benchmark and runner remain in an open pull request.

reviews.name: anti-slop
reviews.verdict: Our anti-slop run installed 11 packages in 25 seconds and passed its tests in 10 seconds, but adoption means owning 15 generic rules as vendored source.
reviews.skip_if: ESLint-only teams that cannot add Oxlint: open issue 23 asks for ESLint support, while the README documents only Oxlint and Vite+ configuration.

reviews.name: cockpit-tools
reviews.verdict: Our Cockpit Tools build succeeded in 77 seconds after a 198-package install, but the repository offered no general test target for us to run.
reviews.skip_if: Companies planning internal or commercial use without a separate agreement: the README applies CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 and explicitly bars enterprise internal commercial use.

reviews.name: mxc
reviews.verdict: Our MXC run installed 222 packages, then both build and test commands stopped because `windows-future` could not find `windows_threading::submit`, so the current source checkout is a research target rather than a drop-in containment layer.
reviews.skip_if: Production systems that need MXC itself to protect hosts or secrets: the README says current profiles are not security boundaries and generated policies have known overly permissive cases.

reviews.name: pr-af
reviews.verdict: Our PR-AF run built in 4 seconds, but 22 of 107 tests failed because the test environment lacked async support, so the checkout is promising rather than release-gate ready.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that need the test suite green in a fresh checkout: our run ended with 22 failures because async tests lacked a suitable pytest plugin.

reviews.name: microsandbox
reviews.verdict: Our Microsandbox build failed after 347 seconds and its tests failed after 110 seconds because the linker could not find `cap-ng`.
reviews.skip_if: Hosts without hardware virtualization: Linux needs KVM, Windows needs WHP, and the documented macOS path requires Apple Silicon.

reviews.name: writer-computer
reviews.verdict: Our Writer checkout installed 683 packages in 10 seconds and occupied 522 MB, yet its root provided no build or test target that the lab could run.
reviews.skip_if: Windows or Linux users seeking a released app: v0.5.0 ships an Apple Silicon DMG and macOS app archive, while open issues request Windows 11 and Linux releases Users who need mobile sync, collaboration, publishing, or a hosted account: the README…

reviews.name: manim
reviews.verdict: Our ManimGL run installed 33 packages and built in 2 seconds, but pytest stopped with 2 collection errors because `numpy` was missing.
reviews.skip_if: Most first-time Manim users: this repository's README says Manim Community aims to be more stable, better tested, more responsive to contributions, and friendlier to start with.

reviews.name: Dopamine
reviews.verdict: Dopamine is the leading option to try when its exact hardware and iOS matrix matches your device and you want a modern rootless jailbreak.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone outside the published chip and iOS combinations: the README says version-support issues will be deleted without a response, so unsupported devices are not an experimental target.

reviews.name: ucp
reviews.verdict: Our UCP checkout installed 133 documentation packages in 5 seconds with 0 known npm vulnerabilities, but it exposed no build or test target and did not run a commerce transaction.
reviews.skip_if: Merchants looking for a ready storefront or payment service: this repository holds schemas and documentation, while SDKs, samples, and conformance tools live elsewhere.

reviews.name: localstack
reviews.verdict: LocalStack remains useful for local AWS integration work, but this archived repository is no longer the product I would adopt.
reviews.skip_if: Developers seeking an actively maintained open-source upstream: this repository is archived and read-only, with future work consolidated into a unified image.

reviews.name: northcinder
reviews.verdict: Our NorthCinder run installed 409 packages in 16 seconds and its protocol suite passed 183 tests, but the overall build and test commands still exited 1 because the site path failed.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone seeking qualified autonomous shopping today: the README says no host and model combination is approved for routine research use.

reviews.name: book-to-skill
reviews.verdict: Use book-to-skill as an interesting local workflow, not yet as trusted knowledge infrastructure.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone expecting a polished hosted app with account sync and support People working mainly with scanned PDFs, because OCR must happen first Teams that need verbatim, citation-grade retrieval from source pages Users unwilling to install format-specific tools or inspect generated…

reviews.name: dsh-routing-suite
reviews.verdict: Our dsh-routing-suite build stopped after 6 seconds because it could not find the required DSH checkout, even though its 37-package npm install and audit completed cleanly.
reviews.skip_if: Users of general chat APIs, Claude Code, or other agents without DeepSeek Harness: the injector depends on DSH packages, profiles, services, and event hooks.

reviews.name: deepseek-harness
reviews.verdict: Our DeepSeek Harness run passed 14,583 of 14,707 tests, with 10 failures and 114 skips, so the large suite was close but not clean.
reviews.skip_if: Production teams requiring stable compatibility: the README labels the project a developer preview and explicitly warns of breaking changes.

reviews.name: Switchyard
reviews.verdict: Our Switchyard run built in 10 seconds, but pytest ended with 86 passes, 10 failures, and 2 collection/setup errors, so commit 053a61e is research-grade rather than a clean production dependency.
reviews.skip_if: Production teams that require stable APIs: the README calls Switchyard pre-alpha and labels its standalone server a demo.

reviews.name: airllm
reviews.verdict: Our AirLLM install took 120 seconds and its build took 16 seconds, but the repo gave us no test target, so it is best treated as an experiment for running oversized models rather than a proven serving layer.
reviews.skip_if: Teams serving latency-sensitive chat or high-throughput APIs: AirLLM streams weights from disk, and its own FAQ identifies disk loading as the bottleneck.

reviews.name: continue
reviews.verdict: Our Continue install took 16 seconds and reported 0 known npm vulnerabilities, but the maintainers now call 2.0.0 the final release and the repository read-only.
reviews.skip_if: Teams choosing a newly maintained coding assistant: the README says this repository is no longer actively maintained and calls 2.0.0 the final release.

reviews.name: autogen
reviews.verdict: Our AutoGen build passed in 10 seconds, but its test run produced 96 collection or setup errors and no passing tests, while Microsoft now labels the project maintenance-only.
reviews.skip_if: New production projects choosing a Microsoft agent stack: the README explicitly sends new users to Microsoft Agent Framework.

reviews.name: nasiko
reviews.verdict: Our sandbox installed 695 packages in 26 seconds, but Nasiko's server failed to compile in both the 279-second build and 111-second test run.
reviews.skip_if: Teams with agents on A2A 0.2.x or 0.3.0: the README says Nasiko hardcodes A2A 1.0 and rejects older protocol versions.

reviews.name: WeChat-AI
reviews.verdict: Our WeChat-AI run installed 136 packages and passed all 13 tests in 42 seconds across install, build, and test, so the code is easy to trial on a clean Node environment.
reviews.skip_if: Any commercial product, paid host, or consulting service: the Commons Clause license text forbids commercial use and resale.

reviews.name: pipeshub-ai
reviews.verdict: Our PipesHub frontend installed 1,526 packages, used 1,690 MB, and built in 124 seconds, while npm audit found 9 high-severity advisories and no test target was available.
reviews.skip_if: Small teams seeking a lightweight local knowledge app: our frontend alone installed 1,526 packages and occupied 1,690 MB.

reviews.name: evershop
reviews.verdict: Our EverShop source run installed 1,406 packages, then both build and test commands failed because expected compiled files were absent, while npm audit reported 30 known vulnerabilities.
reviews.skip_if: Teams expecting the source checkout to build immediately after `npm install`: our build could not find `packages/evershop/dist/bin/build/index.js`, and the README only presents the Docker quick start.

reviews.name: base
reviews.verdict: Our Base source build was still unfinished at 900 seconds, and the 536-second test run failed while a dependency tried to build a Go library, so use published binaries or containers unless you are prepared to own this mixed toolchain.
reviews.skip_if: Application developers who only want to deploy a contract or connect a wallet: the README sends those jobs to Base's separate developer documentation rather than this operator codebase.

reviews.name: sglang-omni
reviews.verdict: Our SGLang-Omni environment occupied 10,224 MB and the suite ended with 83 failures plus 117 errors, despite 1,899 passing tests.
reviews.skip_if: CPU-only self-hosters: the standard install targets NVIDIA CUDA, while the alternative path requires Intel GPUs and a separately prepared XPU stack.

reviews.name: remote.futrx
reviews.verdict: Our Remote backend built in 9 seconds, but 2 of 56 Go tests failed and the supplied log tail did not identify them.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone without a fresh server, root or sudo access, wildcard DNS, an SSH key, and open ports 80 and 443: the quick start requires all of them.

reviews.name: rustfs
reviews.verdict: Our RustFS build and test commands each spent 900 seconds compiling without finishing, while the README still marks distributed mode under testing, so it is an evaluation candidate rather than a safe drop-in storage replacement.
reviews.skip_if: Teams replacing proven storage without a long acceptance test: the README labels distributed mode and lifecycle management as under testing.

reviews.name: Pumpkin
reviews.verdict: Our Pumpkin build took 802 seconds, then all 710 tests passed in 726 seconds, which is serious engineering evidence for a pre-1.0 server.
reviews.skip_if: Established public servers that require vanilla parity today: the README marks combat, Redstone, mobs, Bedrock, plugins, and other mechanics as unfinished or tracked work.

reviews.name: TencentDB-Agent-Memory
reviews.verdict: Our MemoryCore install used 966 MB, then its build and tests both exited 1, while npm audit found 24 known vulnerabilities.
reviews.skip_if: Teams seeking a one-process memory library: the documented deployment starts Memory Core, Memory Hub, and a proxy, with two groups of LLM settings.

reviews.name: AppFlowy
reviews.verdict: Our AppFlowy build hit the 900-second limit and 178 of 312 tests failed, so contributors and self-hosters should treat adoption as a measured trial, not a quick install.
reviews.skip_if: Teams expecting an unrestricted free multi-user server: the AppFlowy Cloud README says its free self-hosted tier allows one user seat and up to three guest editors.

reviews.name: mapcn
reviews.verdict: mapcn is a good shortcut for a shadcn-style dashboard that needs a polished map and accepts source ownership.
reviews.skip_if: Commercial teams expecting the default tiles to be free: the README says commercial use of the included CARTO basemaps requires a CARTO Enterprise license.

reviews.name: TizenTube
reviews.verdict: TizenTube is the best first project to try if you own a recent Samsung TV and already accept the friction of sideloaded Tizen software.
reviews.skip_if: Android or Google TV owners: the README directs those users to the separate TizenTube Cobalt project.

reviews.name: router
reviews.verdict: Our Speedy Router checkout installed 193 packages, built in 9 seconds, and passed its tests in 29 seconds, so it clears the first trial gate.
reviews.skip_if: React 18 or Node 22 production applications: the README deliberately supports React 19.2 and Node 24 only.

reviews.name: convert
reviews.verdict: Our Convert to it!
reviews.skip_if: Archivists and production teams requiring deterministic, fidelity-checked output: the README says an output may not be what the user expected.

reviews.name: servo
reviews.verdict: Our Servo tooling install took 500 seconds and 294 MB, then the build exited in 16 seconds and pytest produced 69 setup or collection errors, so this checkout is research infrastructure rather than a drop-in webview.
reviews.skip_if: People seeking a daily browser with Chrome, Firefox, or Safari compatibility: Servo's own README calls it a prototype engine.

reviews.name: ladybird
reviews.verdict: Our Ladybird run installed 33 detected Python packages and built that tooling path in 5 seconds, but it found no test target and did not prove the full browser build.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone choosing a daily browser today: the README labels Ladybird pre-alpha and suitable only for developers.

reviews.name: tutti
reviews.verdict: Our Tutti install failed after 17 seconds because pnpm found conflicting built-dependency settings across 45 workspaces, so source adopters should wait for a reproducible clean install or use a packaged desktop release.
reviews.skip_if: Linux desktop users looking for a packaged local app: the Quick Start offers macOS and Windows downloads, with no Linux download listed.

reviews.name: godogen
reviews.verdict: Our Godogen install pulled 92 packages and occupied 3,078 MB, while the repository offered no test target, so this is an interesting prototype kit with a thin safety net.
reviews.skip_if: Developers expecting a conventional game framework with reusable runtime code: the README says Godogen is a generator source, and the published repository is mostly instructions plus an asset skill.

reviews.name: open-higgsfield
reviews.verdict: Our OpenHiggsfield run installed 63 packages in 16 seconds and built in 21 seconds, but the repository supplied no tests or CI workflows.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that require an explicit open-source license before adoption: GitHub reports no license and the repository tree has no license file.

reviews.name: apex-inference-chip
reviews.verdict: Our 8-second Python-side build succeeded with 35 packages, but the harness found no test target and did not reproduce the FPGA claims.
reviews.skip_if: Teams shopping for a production inference server or purchasable chip: the README calls APEX pre-silicon and limits the repository to one tile.

reviews.name: cumora
reviews.verdict: Our Cumora install pulled 898 packages and 1,053 MB, then 21 of 447 counted tests failed and npm audit found 39 known vulnerabilities.
reviews.skip_if: Windows users depending on npm-installed BYOA engines today: open issue 58 says the published package still selects the wrong command shim and agent turns fail with `spawn ENOENT`.

reviews.name: ComfyUI-ALLinONE-MinimaxH3
reviews.verdict: Our 6-second build succeeded, but Pytest executed 0 tests because collection stopped on a missing `folder_paths` import, so the only meaningful acceptance test is inside a matched ComfyUI installation.
reviews.skip_if: People who do not already operate ComfyUI and local generation models: this is a custom node, not a standalone video application.

reviews.name: deepseek-harness-studio
reviews.verdict: Our DeepSeek Harness Studio test run reached the 900-second cap while its log showed repeated plugin restoration failures, despite an 86-second install and successful 124-second build.
reviews.skip_if: Linux desktop users: the README provides preview downloads only for macOS arm64 and Windows x64.

reviews.name: sam
reviews.verdict: Our SAM build passed in 78 seconds, but its only reported integration test failed after 385 seconds because the unprivileged container could not use `unshare`.
reviews.skip_if: Teams seeking an officially supported Google service: the README explicitly says SAM is unsupported and outside Google's open-source vulnerability reward program.

reviews.name: oil-motion
reviews.verdict: Our Oil Motion run installed 35 packages and built successfully, but its tests stopped with 3 collection errors because `PIL` was missing.
reviews.skip_if: English-only teams that must audit every production instruction: the English README exists, but `SKILL.md` and nine reference guides are Chinese, while their translation remains an open pull request.

reviews.name: exo
reviews.verdict: Our build finished in 5 seconds and pip-audit found 0 vulnerabilities, but pytest ran 0 tests because `exo_tools` was missing, and the exact measured commit has an open report of remotely reachable data deletion through its unauthenticated API.
reviews.skip_if: Linux users expecting GPU inference today: the README says Linux currently runs on CPU and GPU support is under development.

reviews.name: everyone-can-use-english
reviews.verdict: Our install pulled 2,681 packages and used 2,624 MB, while the lab found no generic build or test target, so contributors inherit much more uncertainty than hosted users.
reviews.skip_if: English-speaking users who need complete documentation in English: the root README and learning guides are Chinese, and issue #1409 asks for basic product instructions even in Chinese.

reviews.name: claude-video-vision
reviews.verdict: Our build passed in 9 seconds, but 10 of 148 tests failed without ffmpeg and ffprobe, while npm audit found 9 high-severity advisories among 15 total.
reviews.skip_if: Users without ffmpeg and ffprobe: 10 of 148 tests failed in our sandbox because those binaries were missing Security teams that cannot accept the current dependency state: npm audit reported 15 known vulnerabilities, including 9 high-severity advisories People expecting a…

reviews.name: go-cursor-help
reviews.verdict: This tool is a brutally simple and effective solution for resetting Cursor's trial, but it's a solution frozen in time.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone in a professional or corporate environment, as using this tool likely violates Cursor's terms of service and company policies.

reviews.name: claude-task-master
reviews.verdict: Our Taskmaster install consumed 1,812 MB and npm audit found 159 vulnerabilities, while 1,521 tests passed before one Jest worker was terminated, so release 0.43.1 needs a security and dependency review before adoption.
reviews.skip_if: Security-sensitive agent deployments on release 0.43.1: open issues document out-of-workspace writes through `projectRoot` and arbitrary reads through `prdPath`.

reviews.name: system-prompts-and-models-of-ai-tools
reviews.verdict: This is less a software project and more a controversial but valuable dataset.
reviews.skip_if: Non-technical users looking for a runnable application or a simple AI tool.

reviews.name: RuView
reviews.verdict: Our RuView install consumed 5,366 MB, the build failed in 6 seconds, and the test command exited 1 because coverage was 0% even though all 34 tests passed.
reviews.skip_if: Medical, elder-care, or safety deployments needing clinically validated alarms: the README labels several sensing paths experimental, synthetic, below target, or not wired.

reviews.name: xiaozhi-esp32-server
reviews.verdict: Our mobile-manager run installed 1,407 packages in 73 seconds and built in 21 seconds, but it exposed no test target and did not exercise the server or an ESP32 device.
reviews.skip_if: Production deployments: the project's own warning says functionality is incomplete and has not passed a network security assessment.

reviews.name: ruflo
reviews.verdict: Ruflo is interesting for expert Claude Code and Codex users who have already hit the limits of one agent and can audit a large amount of installed machinery.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone wanting a small, predictable extension: the full initializer writes `.claude/`, `.claude-flow/`, `CLAUDE.md`, helpers, settings, hooks, a daemon, and an MCP registration.

reviews.name: voice-pro
reviews.verdict: Our Voice-Pro install used 7,192 MB for 310 packages, and pip-audit found 7 known vulnerabilities before any test target was available.
reviews.skip_if: Mac or Linux teams needing verified support: the README lists launch scripts for both but plainly says operation on those systems has not been verified.

reviews.name: UI-TARS-desktop
reviews.verdict: Our UI-TARS-desktop run installed a 1,910 MB workspace and failed 57 of 337 tests, so this is an experimental agent stack to isolate and supervise, not a dependable unattended operator.
reviews.skip_if: Multi-monitor desktop users: the quick start says only single-monitor setups are supported and other layouts may fail.

reviews.name: mindshub
reviews.verdict: Our MindsHub frontend installed 511 packages and built in 53 seconds combined, but npm audit found 23 known vulnerabilities and no test target was available.
reviews.skip_if: Security-sensitive teams seeking a clean dependency result: our frontend audit found 23 known vulnerabilities, including 3 critical and 19 high.

reviews.name: GitHub520
reviews.verdict: Our run installed 61 packages and built in 7 seconds, but the absence of a test target and 5 pip-audit findings make GitHub520's generator less reassuring than its tiny size suggests.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone who cannot read Chinese technical instructions: the README and current issue discussion are Chinese, with no English guide in the repository.

reviews.name: Cybermes
reviews.verdict: Our Cybermes install added 252 packages and the audit found six high-severity advisories, while the repository offered no npm test target, so this is a framework to isolate and inspect before it touches an authorized target.
reviews.skip_if: Beginners who expect the framework to make authorization decisions for them: the troubleshooting guide says wildcard dynamic target authorization is enabled by default, and the sample environment sets `HERMES_YOLO_MODE=1`.

reviews.name: lanshu-create-ai-presenter-video
reviews.verdict: Our install added 35 packages in 11 seconds and the build passed in 4 seconds, but no test target exercised an actual video job.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone expecting the repository itself to generate a presenter: the README requires at least one callable video-generation, voice-generation, and lip-sync capability in the current environment.

reviews.name: nft-public-mint
reviews.verdict: Our NFT Public Mint Sniper run installed 67 packages in 9 seconds and built in 7 seconds with 0 audit findings, but there was no test target for the code that signs real transactions.
reviews.skip_if: Allowlist or first-come signed stages: the README says these require OpenSea's per-wallet `mintSigned()` signature and are unsupported.

reviews.name: eve-software-factory-template
reviews.verdict: Our Eve template install took 32 seconds, but its build failed in 8 seconds because the required `FACTORY_REPO` value was absent, and the repository supplied no test target.
reviews.skip_if: Teams outside the Vercel Connect and Eve stack: deployment depends on GitHub and Linear connector UIDs, Vercel Blob, and Vercel-managed sandboxes.

reviews.name: centaur
reviews.verdict: Our Centaur checkout installed 364 pnpm packages in 20 seconds, but it offered no root build or test target to prove that the multi-service platform worked.
reviews.skip_if: A solo developer wanting a quick local coding assistant: the default bootstrap requires Kubernetes, 1Password, Slack credentials, and a model credential before one agent turn.

reviews.name: projeto-dados-ia-databricks
reviews.verdict: Our run installed 35 packages in 11 seconds and built in 3 seconds, but the repository supplied no automated test target.
reviews.skip_if: English-only learners: the main README, lesson guides, column names, prompts, slides, and business vocabulary are in Portuguese, with no English guide.

reviews.name: desktop-fly
reviews.verdict: Our 4-second Python-side build succeeded, but no test target ran and the macOS Swift application was outside that sandbox result.
reviews.skip_if: Windows or Linux users expecting official support: the README requires macOS 13 or newer, while issues #7 and #8 point to separate community ports.

reviews.name: tick-stock-panel
reviews.verdict: Our TickFlow Stock Panel run finished with 28 passes, 20 failures, and 69 collection or setup errors, so this is a codebase to repair before using for research decisions.
reviews.skip_if: Commercial adopters who need unambiguous permission: the repository declares MIT, while the README also says commercial use is strictly prohibited.

reviews.name: PLFM_RADAR

reviews.skip_if: Makers ready to order boards from the repository without an engineering review: issue 186 asks whether Gerbers, schematics, BOMs, known fixes, stack-up, and the 50T versus 200T FPGA choice are consistent.

reviews.name: semantica

reviews.skip_if: Teams that require a clean full suite before adoption: our run recorded 159 failures and 41 collection or setup errors.

reviews.name: herdrm

reviews.skip_if: Anyone on Windows, Linux, or macOS 13 and older: the app requires macOS 14 or newer.

reviews.name: dsh-explore
reviews.verdict: Use Deepseek Harness Explore as a focused technical reading resource, not as the foundation of a production system.
reviews.skip_if: Teams seeking a ready-to-deploy agent framework, because this is mainly an explanatory publication Readers who need the full article collection in English, because the articles are stated to be Chinese Buyers who require a stable release, declared license, and production…

reviews.name: genlayer-project-boilerplate
reviews.verdict: Our GenLayer boilerplate install pulled 2,324 packages and 47 known vulnerabilities, including 1 critical, while the build passed and no root test target existed.
reviews.skip_if: Teams seeking a chain-neutral starter: the contract, deployment scripts, wallet setup, and frontend client are all built around GenLayer.

reviews.name: defending-code-reference-harness
reviews.verdict: Our harness build passed in 8 seconds and 411 of 426 tests passed, while 14 failures and 1 setup error all stopped on a missing `docker` executable.
reviews.skip_if: Teams seeking a maintained scanner with product support: the README says this repository is not maintained and does not accept contributions.

reviews.name: cordis
reviews.verdict: Our Cordis checkout installed 432 packages with 0 known vulnerabilities, but both build and test stopped within 10 seconds because the npm-created workspace state did not satisfy Yarn 4.14.1.
reviews.skip_if: Application teams wanting a stable public API: the README says Cordis is under active development and may change without notice.

reviews.name: hop
reviews.verdict: Our Hop run installed 54 packages in 6 seconds and passed the JavaScript tests, but the full command failed because Cargo was absent.
reviews.skip_if: Users who need to save edited HWPX files: the development guide says HWPX saving is disabled until a safe serializer exists.

reviews.name: d-inference
reviews.verdict: Our Darkbloom build passed in 78 seconds, but 3 of 37 Go package results failed in 128 seconds, all in end-to-end coverage, which matches the project's public-alpha warning.

reviews.name: lean-ctx
reviews.verdict: Our LeanCTX source build succeeded in 402 seconds, but its 223-second test run exited 101 and current issues report broken safety and verbatim-read expectations.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone relying on IDE plan mode as a security boundary: open issue 1500 says `ctx_shell`, `ctx_execute`, and `ctx_patch` remain callable in plan or readonly mode.

reviews.name: walgit

reviews.skip_if: Teams expecting a GitHub or GitLab replacement with issues, pull requests, CI, and code review: the README scopes walgit to repository serving and browsing.

reviews.name: evolution-api
reviews.verdict: Evolution API makes sense when its unusually wide set of WhatsApp, webhook, queue, CRM, and storage connections would replace glue code you already expect to maintain.

reviews.name: tick-stock-panel

reviews.skip_if: English-only users: the README, setup guide, configuration reference, interface examples, and linked manuals are in Chinese, with no English guide listed.

reviews.name: substrate
reviews.verdict: Our Substrate run built in 208 seconds, but 2 of 82 tests failed, so this is research infrastructure to investigate rather than a production base to trust.
reviews.skip_if: Production workloads: the README explicitly says the project is not ready and its APIs are almost guaranteed to change.

reviews.name: scroll-craft
reviews.verdict: The lab found JavaScript but no supported executable target or Dockerfile, so scrollcraft has no independent build or test result on our page.
reviews.skip_if: Developers outside Claude Code who want a documented first-class install path: the README installs it through Claude Code's plugin marketplace.

reviews.name: libros-programacion-gratis
reviews.verdict: Our libros-programacion-gratis install took 19 seconds, but its Astro build failed after 12 seconds on a refused localhost connection and there was no test target.
reviews.skip_if: Readers who need English material: the contribution rules reject content that is not in Spanish, and no English catalog is linked.

reviews.name: open-tv
reviews.verdict: Our Open TV v1.9.1 checkout failed its build in 10 seconds, timed out waiting for Chrome for 900 seconds, and reported 89 known dependency vulnerabilities, so source adoption should wait for cleanup.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone expecting channels to be included: the README only describes importing your own M3U or Xtream sources.

reviews.name: biosecurity-agent
reviews.verdict: Our Biosecurity Agent run installed 576 packages, used 686 MB, and passed all 83 tests, so version 0.1.2 is more than a terminal mockup.
reviews.skip_if: Clinicians or patients seeking diagnosis or treatment: the README explicitly says the project is not for clinical diagnosis, and the safety code rejects some diagnostic and dosage language.

reviews.name: tradingview-mcp
reviews.verdict: Our tradingview-mcp run installed in 13 seconds, but 1 of 17 tests failed and npm audit found 7 known vulnerabilities.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone seeking automated trade execution: the README explicitly says the bridge does not execute real trades.

reviews.name: cwc-workshops
reviews.verdict: Our `agent-battle/` install took 28 seconds and its build passed in 4 seconds, but the repository supplied no test target for us to run.
reviews.skip_if: Teams seeking a maintained production starter: the root README and individual workshops explicitly say they are not maintained and do not accept contributions.

reviews.name: Roo-Code
reviews.verdict: Our Roo Code run installed 2,665 packages, used 1,431 MB, and passed both build and tests, but the extension was shut down and the repository archived on May 15, 2026.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone choosing a maintained coding agent today: the README says Roo Code shut down on May 15, 2026, and GitHub marks the repository archived.

reviews.name: wecom-cli

reviews.skip_if: Agents that must draft email without sending it: issue 118 says `mail send` delivers immediately and has no server-side draft mode.

reviews.name: WeMM-Embedding
reviews.verdict: Our WeMM-Embedding install pulled 92 packages, occupied 5,047 MB, and exposed 3 known vulnerabilities before any model weights were downloaded.
reviews.skip_if: Audio retrieval projects: the README says audio input is not supported, and its MMEB-v3 audio score is therefore zero.

reviews.name: ambient-context
reviews.verdict: Our run installed 79 packages in 5 seconds, built in 6 seconds, and found 0 known vulnerabilities, but no automated test target ran.
reviews.skip_if: Intel Mac, Windows, Linux, or older macOS users: the README requires macOS 14 or newer on Apple Silicon.

reviews.name: babua-dsa-patterns-course
reviews.verdict: Use Babua DSA Patterns Course if Hindi instruction and a fixed daily sequence help you keep practicing.
reviews.skip_if: Learners who need English spoken instruction: the README says the explanations are in Hindi, although the main written pages are in English.

reviews.name: paper
reviews.verdict: Read this paper if you are designing a serious plugin host or self-modifying agent runtime, because it gives unusually precise names and rules to problems that are often handled with restart hooks.
reviews.skip_if: Developers looking for an installable library in this repository: it contains only a README and PDF, while the implementation lives separately in `cordiverse/cordis`.

reviews.name: open_deep_research
reviews.verdict: Our Open Deep Research build took 4 seconds, but its only test failed on a LangSmith HTTP 401 and the upstream repository is archived with 73 issues and pull requests open.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that require upstream fixes or accepted pull requests: GitHub marks the repository archived, with 73 issues and pull requests still open.

reviews.name: swarm-forge
reviews.verdict: SwarmForge is a brilliantly unconventional tool for developers who live in the terminal.
reviews.skip_if: Beginners unfamiliar with `tmux`, shell scripting, or advanced git concepts like worktrees.

reviews.name: reverse-skill
reviews.verdict: reverse-skill is a brilliant and wildly ambitious attempt to solve a real problem: AI agents are powerful but lack strategic, domain-specific knowledge for complex security tasks.
reviews.skip_if: Beginners in cybersecurity.

reviews.name: SpiderPanel
reviews.verdict: Our SpiderPanel install pulled 66 packages and pip-audit found 34 known vulnerabilities, while the repository supplied no test target or CI workflow, so it is not ready for unattended production use as published.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone who might expose the defaults: the README documents `admin` as the initial password and `spider-panel-secret-key-v2` as the default session secret.

reviews.name: midday
reviews.verdict: Midday has an appealing product shape for independent workers, but this repository is a serious platform deployment rather than a weekend self-host.
reviews.skip_if: Operators seeking a compact self-hosted finance app: the README names Supabase, Railway, Vercel, Cloudflare, Trigger.dev, Resend, bank providers, analytics, payments, search, and AI services.

reviews.name: spacedrive
reviews.verdict: Our Spacedrive install failed after 76 seconds at its Bun-only preinstall guard, which makes the current v2 alpha suitable only for developers testing with disposable data.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone unwilling to test with disposable data first: open issue 3056 reports that v2.0.0-alpha.2 deleted a nonempty root-level `tmp` folder on tracked Windows volumes.

reviews.name: aegis-vault
reviews.verdict: Our Aegis Vault run installed 35 packages and built in 9 seconds, but it had no test target and its owner documents a Sentinel path that can expose the master password to anyone reading browser storage.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone choosing a primary vault for valuable credentials: the README says Aegis has no formal third-party security audit, and our run found no test target.

reviews.name: Nova-Proxy
reviews.verdict: Our Nova Proxy build and test both failed because the repository references a missing `scripts/build.mjs`, so this release artifact is deployable by the guided path but not reproducible from the public checkout we tested.
reviews.skip_if: Businesses, paid proxy operators, or resellers: releases from 4.3.0 use PolyForm Noncommercial, and paid hosting requires written permission.

reviews.name: fanqiang
reviews.verdict: Our Fanqiang install stopped after 11 seconds because a replaced local Go module was missing, so developers should not expect the measured checkout to build as-is.
reviews.skip_if: English-only users: the main README and linked setup guides are Chinese, and the FQNews page has only a brief English project note.

reviews.name: 30-Days-Of-React
reviews.verdict: Our Node 22 sandbox installed 1,223 packages in 82 seconds, but both the build and test commands failed, so use 30 Days of React as course text and bring a current practice environment.
reviews.skip_if: Complete programming beginners: the README requires intermediate HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, and points weaker JavaScript learners to a separate 30-day course first.

reviews.name: Sigma-Web-Dev-Course
reviews.verdict: Our `Video 101` run installed 142 packages and built in 12 seconds, but it had no real tests and npm audit found 13 known vulnerabilities.
reviews.skip_if: Learners who need a self-contained written course: the README points to YouTube and does not map 137 numbered folders to topics or prerequisites.

reviews.name: linuxdo-idea-ui
reviews.verdict: Our lab did not run linuxdo-idea-ui because the JavaScript userscript exposed no supported ecosystem and the repository had no Dockerfile.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone who does not read Chinese: the README and interface description are Chinese, with no English guide linked.

reviews.name: layer5

reviews.skip_if: Developers looking for the Meshery management plane: that product lives in `meshery/meshery`, while this repository builds the Layer5 website.

reviews.name: octo-web
reviews.verdict: Our OCTO Web install consumed 1,178 MB, then both the 8-second build and 10-second test steps failed, so this checkout is a risky foundation unless your team can trace a large pnpm monorepo.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone looking for a standalone chat application: the README says the client expects `octo-server` at `http://localhost:8080`, and several features belong to other OCTO repositories.

reviews.name: OpenCut

reviews.skip_if: Anyone who needs a working editor from this repository today: its README directs users to `opencut-classic`, and the desktop guide says it only opens a window.

reviews.name: watermark-remover
reviews.verdict: Our watermark-remover build passed in 7 seconds, but the 80-second test run failed across installer paths because `install_skill.py` was missing from the tested checkout.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone seeking proof that a vendor detector will fail: the README explicitly says the tool cannot certify that outcome.

reviews.name: obsidian-skills
reviews.verdict: Obsidian Skills is a forward-thinking toolkit for a very specific audience: developers integrating AI agents into their personal knowledge management.
reviews.skip_if: Casual Obsidian users looking for a simple, in-app AI writing assistant.

reviews.name: TelegramGroup

reviews.skip_if: Developers looking for a Telegram API library, bot framework, or runnable search engine: the repository is a Markdown directory with no detected programming language or Dockerfile.

reviews.name: minio
reviews.verdict: Our MinIO build succeeded, but 45 of 46 Go packages passed before the test run failed, and the repository is now archived.
reviews.skip_if: New production storage deployments expecting an active open-source upstream: the repository says it is no longer maintained and GitHub marks it archived.

reviews.name: Antigravity

reviews.skip_if: macOS or Linux users: the README describes a Windows program, while open requests ask for ports to those systems.

reviews.name: everything-claude-code

reviews.name: dsh-gitbash-preset

reviews.name: skitter-creek-bath-salts

reviews.name: typescript-go

reviews.skip_if: New TypeScript contributors: the README says development and discussion have moved to microsoft/TypeScript, while this repository will be archived in September 2026.

reviews.name: opencode
reviews.verdict: Our archived OpenCode checkout built in 49 seconds, but 1 of 4 test packages failed and active development has moved to Crush, so new users should not adopt this repository.
reviews.skip_if: New users choosing a coding agent: the README says this repository is archived and directs ongoing development to `charmbracelet/crush`.

reviews.name: Flowise
reviews.verdict: Do not start a new production system on the archived Flowise repository.
reviews.skip_if: New production adopters who expect vendor maintenance: the maintainers announced a code freeze, archived the repository on August 13, 2026, and set end of life for August 31.

reviews.name: personal-edge-proxy
reviews.verdict: Our harness could not run Personal Edge Proxy because it has no detected language ecosystem or Dockerfile, so treat it as an architecture note and sanitized configuration set, not verified software.
reviews.skip_if: English-only readers: the README and both topic guides are Chinese, with only the AI maintainer instructions written in English.

reviews.name: daytona
reviews.verdict: Daytona presents a powerful and comprehensive vision for AI agent infrastructure, but its open-source version is a ghost ship.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone needing a production-ready, supported, and maintained solution.

reviews.name: hexstrike-ai

reviews.skip_if: Anyone planning to expose the server to a normal office or public network: the README documents an arbitrary-command endpoint and says operators should consider adding authentication.

reviews.name: outlook-auto-register
reviews.verdict: Our run installed 47 packages in 13 seconds and built in 4 seconds, but there was no test target, so the polished console sits on unverified account-creation code.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone planning to create usable Outlook accounts in bulk: Microsoft Support explicitly says not to use programs, scripts, or bots to create Microsoft accounts.

reviews.name: gpt_nerver

reviews.skip_if: Anyone seeking an approved way to create or maintain ChatGPT accounts: the README warns that service rules and risk controls can change and places compliance responsibility on the user.

reviews.name: cve-2026-41940-PoC
reviews.verdict: Our run installed 35 packages in 11 seconds and built in 3 seconds, but there was no test target, so this PoC is easy to prepare and unproven as a diagnostic.
reviews.skip_if: cPanel administrators looking for the safest exposure check: cPanel publishes its own patch versions and detection guidance, while this project performs exploitation and post-access actions.

reviews.name: grok-bot-0.18-reconstructed
reviews.verdict: Our install added 383 packages, but both the 3-second build and 3-second test run failed, so this reconstruction is research material rather than a dependable desktop-agent dependency.
reviews.skip_if: Production teams needing a clean license chain: GitHub reports no license, NOTICE describes retained upstream boundaries, and issue 7 asks for licensing and derivative-work permission to be clarified.

reviews.name: youtube-music
reviews.verdict: Our checkout built in 12 seconds and passed 5 of 6 tests, but its package metadata names Pear Desktop and points to `pear-devs/pear-desktop` rather than this project.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone unwilling to run a password-protected ZIP from a new publisher: the README distributes one EXE inside an archive protected with `ytm4all`.

reviews.name: media-inference-worker
reviews.verdict: Our run installed 35 packages in 20 seconds and found 0 known vulnerabilities, but commit `eab94b0` publishes two service credential values in a tracked `.env`, so nobody should deploy it as received.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone unable to rotate exposed credentials immediately: commit `eab94b0` tracks a `.env` with two credential values, and the README says the copied service account was active with unknown rotation timing.

reviews.name: learn
reviews.verdict: Our install attempt failed in 5 seconds inside `extensions/visual-tools/`, so Learn is best treated as a readable personal configuration for current pi users, not an install-and-forget tutor.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone expecting a standalone tutor: the repository is a `.pi` directory and requires the separate pi agent.

reviews.name: grok-1
reviews.verdict: Use Grok-1 when the object of study is Grok-1 itself.
reviews.skip_if: Developers looking for a laptop or single-GPU chatbot: the README says the 314B-parameter model needs enough GPU memory, and the included runner configures an eight-device local mesh.

reviews.name: Dalaran
reviews.verdict: Our Dalaran run built in 9 seconds, but pytest produced 29 failures and 96 collection or setup errors, so this fork is a research trial rather than a safe default for a robotics team.
reviews.skip_if: Teams that need a stable API or long support window: the README calls the project pre-1.0, warns of breaking changes, and supports only the latest release.

reviews.name: v4-flash-godmode-opencode-go
reviews.verdict: Do not choose this fork for a new deployment.
reviews.skip_if: New users seeking a maintained installation, because the project explicitly no longer evolves Production teams that need releases, a known license, and a stable support path English-only readers, because no English documentation is evidenced here Anyone wanting the newer standard…

reviews.name: nitter
reviews.verdict: Our Nitter tools run installed 47 Python packages and found 0 tests, while the full repository was archived after a stated August 24, 2026 takedown demand.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone choosing a supported X reader for a new service: the repository is archived, and its README says X Corp demanded permanent takedown of the project and instances.

reviews.name: life-ipo
reviews.verdict: Our Life IPO install pulled 748 packages and 735 MB, then both build and tests stopped on the same Rolldown/Vite build error, while npm audit found 16 high-severity advisories.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone who needs normal open-source reuse rights: the README says no license has been specified and public visibility does not grant permission to copy, modify, or redistribute.

reviews.name: deploy-vercel
reviews.verdict: Our install pulled 66 packages into 81 MB, while the five-file project supplied no build or test target, so deploy-vercel asks you to trust security-sensitive network code without a verification suite.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone looking for English setup or security documentation: the README is Chinese and does not provide an English guide.

reviews.name: node
reviews.verdict: Our Rust contract-sample build installed 4 packages, then failed in 34 seconds with 20 type errors, so the repository does not currently offer a dependable Rust contract starting point at commit `01e66db`.
reviews.skip_if: Contract developers who need a working Rust sample today: our build of `contract_samples/rust/` failed with 20 compiler errors.

reviews.name: cloud-cost-optimization-hub
reviews.verdict: Our backend run installed 149 packages and passed its single test, but Azure and GCP cost paths still use or call for mock-data replacement.
reviews.skip_if: Teams expecting real three-cloud billing data: Azure generates sample costs in source, and issue 5 says GCP still needs the Cloud Billing API.

reviews.name: DeepSeek-V4-J-Space-Capability-Realization-Report
reviews.verdict: The v2.0 repository ships 2 report files and no executable harness, raw task traces, or machine-readable results, so its score table is not decision-grade evidence.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone choosing a model or agent stack from reproducible evidence: the v2.0 release lists only Chinese and English report files.

reviews.name: wenai
reviews.verdict: Our lab could not run wenai at commit a25b95b because it had no detected ecosystem and no Dockerfile, so none of its access, persistence, or image steps are verified here.
reviews.skip_if: Minors or anyone seeking non-adult role-play: the skill is explicitly for fictional consenting adults and contains explicit sexual workflows.

reviews.name: Polymarket-Telegram-Bot
reviews.verdict: The repository contains 1 JavaScript feed example and no Telegram bot implementation, so it cannot support an independent code review of the wallet or trading claims.
reviews.skip_if: Anyone seeking a self-hosted Telegram trading bot: the README explicitly says the example is not the bot and contains no business logic, filters, or Telegram integration.

reviews.name: iready-tool
reviews.verdict: Our sandbox did not run iReady Tool because it exposes no supported runnable ecosystem or Dockerfile, and the repository has 0 releases and 0 open issues or pull requests to substantiate compatibility.
reviews.skip_if: Students seeking legitimate help with i-Ready work: the tool is designed to falsify lesson completion, minutes, quizzes, and diagnostics, which can violate school rules and corrupt learning records.

reviews.name: CVE-2026-9830
reviews.verdict: Static inspection of our 373-line checkout found an obfuscated statement that fetches and executes remote text from `5.255.114.98:8090`, so nobody should run this repository as supplied.
reviews.skip_if: WordPress administrators trying to check a live site: `main.py` executes code fetched over plain HTTP from `5.255.114.98:8090` before it creates the advertised BookingPress client Penetration testers handling customer data: the script can print and save names, email addresses, phone numbers,…
